title: Hoshizora no Uta (Song of the Starry Sky) (Japanese Version)
album: Hoshizora no Uta: Voyages on the Seto Inland Sea
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

The original Japanese-language broadcast recording of 'Hoshizora no Uta (星空の歌)' played aboard the overnight passenger ferry across the Inland Sea.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Warm City Pop electric guitar melody, lush strings, and bell chimes)

[Verse 1]
夕暮れの港に優しい風が吹く (Yūgure no minato ni yasashii kaze ga fuku) [The gentle wind blows on the evening port]
重い影は岸に残していく (Omoi kage wa kishi ni nokoshite iku) [Leave your heavy shadows behind on the shore]

[Chorus]
穏やかな波が明日へ運ぶよ (Odayaka na nami ga asu e hakobu yo) [The gentle waves will carry you to tomorrow]
星空の下で瞳を休めて (Hoshizora no shita de hitomi o yasumete) [Rest your eyes under the starry sky]
海の上ならもう安全だから (Umi no ue nara mō anzen dakara) [For upon the sea, you are safe now]

[Verse 2]
船は静かな子守唄を歌う (Fune wa shizuka na komoriuta o utau) [The ship sings a quiet lullaby]
急がなくていい、時を預けて (Isoganakute ii, toki o azukete) [There is no need to rush, just entrust the time to the waves]

[Chorus]
穏やかな波が明日へ運ぶよ (Odayaka na nami ga asu e hakobu yo) [The gentle waves will carry you to tomorrow]
星空の下で瞳を休めて (Hoshizora no shita de hitomi o yasumete) [Rest your eyes under the starry sky]
海の上ならもう安全だから (Umi no ue nara mō anzen dakara) [For upon the sea, you are safe now]

[Outro]
ああ、星空よ、夜を越えてゆけ (Aa, hoshizora yo, yoru o koete yuke) [Ah, starry sky, travel across the night]
おやすみ、旅人、また明日 (Oyasumi, tabibito, mata ashita) [Goodnight, traveler, see you tomorrow]

title: Hoshizora no Uta (Song of the Starry Sky) (English Version)
album: Hoshizora no Uta: Voyages on the Seto Inland Sea
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A gentle maritime City Pop lullaby from the family's global healing voyage across Japan—assuring the weary traveler that the heavy shadows have been left behind on the shore and that he is finally safe upon the sea.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Warm electric guitar lead, lush strings, and gentle vibraphone chimes)

[Verse 1]
The evening wind blows gently on the port
Leave your heavy shadows on the shore

[Chorus]
The gentle waves will carry you to tomorrow
Rest your eyes under the starry sky
For you are safe upon the sea

[Verse 2]
The ship hums a quiet, steady lullaby
There is no need to rush
Just give the time to the waves

[Chorus]
The gentle waves will carry you to tomorrow
Rest your eyes under the starry sky
For you are safe upon the sea

[Outro]
Ah, starry sky, travel across the night
Goodnight, traveler
See you tomorrow

title: The Hollow Square
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The opening track and thesis statement of the 1983 *Carnaby Street* album. "The Hollow Square" was a massive transatlantic commercial success, sitting at #1 on the charts for 14 consecutive weeks. However, beneath its polished progressive pop exterior lies a profound grief. 

The "square" represents the four missing members of the Manning Family Orchestra (Gwen, Alistair, Julian, and Simon) who were killed in the 1981 Shap Fell disaster. Leaving Rhys and Claire as the only surviving members, the lyrics explicitly document their flight to Maryland (*"We crossed the water to find a shore"*) and Rhys's desperate, mechanical resurrection of the band using analog synthesizers and drum machines to fill the deafening silence left by their family (*"We sequence notes to fill the void"*).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(Brooding, solitary drum machine rhythm begins)*
*(Joined by a slow, pulsing analog synth bass)*

[Verse 1]
Four empty spaces in the room
A silent echo in the gloom
We crossed the water to find a shore
But left behind what came before
The city lights are cold and bright
A different sky, a different night

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, massive gated snare drum enters)*
Standing in the hollow square!
Reaching out, but no one's there!
We forge the armour, paint the sky
To keep the fading embers high!
In the hollow square...

[Verse 2]
*(Dynamics drop back down to the brooding synth)*
The cables hum, the circuits glow
To mask the quiet down below
We sequence notes to fill the void
A symphony we re-employed
Just two remain to hold the line
And reconstruct the grand design

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, massive gated snare drum enters)*
Standing in the hollow square!
Reaching out, but no one's there!
We forge the armour, paint the sky
To keep the fading embers high!
In the hollow square...

[Bridge]
*(Layered, atmospheric keyboards take over)*
*(Vocalist sings with intense emotion)*
The stage is smaller, but the sound is deep
A promise that we swore to keep
Through the silence, hear the spark
We light the beacons in the dark!

[Instrumental Break]
*(Soaring, melodic guitar solo over a driving drum machine beat)*

[Chorus]
Standing in the hollow square!
Reaching out, but no one's there!
We forge the armour, paint the sky
To keep the fading embers high!
In the hollow square!

[Outro]
*(The massive drums fade out)*
*(Leaving only the pulsing synth bass)*
The hollow square...
We hold the line...
*(Fades to silence)*

title: A Prophecy Unfolds
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"A Prophecy Unfolds" showcases Rhys Manning's obsessive mechanical resurrection of the band's percussion. The track's relentless, rolling tribal toms are his direct attempt to mechanically rebuild the sprawling, chaotic heartbeat of his deceased older brother, Alistair, who previously anchored the family's sound on a massive drum kit. 

Claire's lyrics ("hiding from the freezing of the sun," "against the bitter cold") serve as a visceral, artistic reflection of the winter 1981 Shap Fell disaster. The sudden "white-out" of freezing fog and black ice on that desolate road claimed the lives of their four bandmates. As the lyrics starkly declare, "Just two remain against the tide," cementing Claire and Rhys's isolated reality as the sole surviving members of their generation.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A fast, tense, arpeggiated synth sequence begins)*
*(Joined by relentless, rolling tribal toms and a driving bassline)*

[Verse 1]
The shadows lengthen on the wall, the sequence has begun
A chill is blowing through the hall, awakening the sun
We read the signs in broken glass, and trace the hidden lines
Another empty day will pass, another fate declines
The gears are turning in the dark, above the factory floor
We try to catch the fading spark, behind the heavy door

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, synthesizers become massive and sweeping)*
Can you see the prophecy unfold?
(It's unfolding...)
Shadows in the stories we were told!
Turn the wheel and watch the colours run!
Hiding from the freezing of the sun...
A prophecy unfolds!

[Verse 2]
*(Dynamics pull back slightly, keeping the tense sequencer pulse)*
A thousand voices in the wire, a whisper in the screen
We feed the papers to the fire, to keep the engine clean
You lock the gate and turn the key, you try to understand
How anything was meant to be, inside this hollow land
Just two remain against the tide, against the bitter cold
With nowhere left for us to hide, exactly as foretold

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, massive gated snare drum joins the rolling toms)*
Can you see the prophecy unfold?
(It's unfolding...)
Shadows in the stories we were told!
Turn the wheel and watch the colours run!
Hiding from the freezing of the sun...
A prophecy unfolds!

[Bridge]
*(The drums drop out completely)*
*(Just the fast, tense synth sequencer and urgent, layered vocals)*
Is it written in the code?
At the ending of the road?
We are running out of time!
We are running out of time!

[Instrumental Break]
*(A frantic, swirling analog synthesizer solo over the heavy rolling drums)*

[Chorus]
Can you see the prophecy unfold?
(It's unfolding...)
Shadows in the stories we were told!
Turn the wheel and watch the colours run!
Hiding from the freezing of the sun...
A prophecy unfolds!

[Outro]
*(The heavy drums stop suddenly)*
*(Leaving just the tense synth sequencer fading into the distance)*
It's unfolding...
*(Fade to silence)*

title: Strangers in the Stream
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Strangers in the Stream" captures the profound culture shock and isolation Rhys and Claire experienced after fleeing Romford for their father's childhood home in Williamsport, Maryland. The lyrics explicitly reference this transatlantic dislocation ("We stepped ashore in a different age / A thousand miles from the open stage") and the surreal quiet of their new sanctuary. 

Sonically, the track relies heavily on a smooth fretless bass groove. This is Rhys's synthetic, mechanical attempt to replicate the deep, complex low-end melodies of their late cousin Julian Hayes, whose Rickenbacker bass and cello gave the family's original 1970s sound its cinematic weight. Without Julian, Rhys leans entirely on these colder, synthetic string replications to bridge the gap.

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet)*

[Intro]
*(Lush, sweeping analog synthesizer pads)*
*(A melodic, chorus-soaked guitar line enters)*
*(Joined by a smooth fretless bass and steady drum machine)*

[Verse 1]
We stepped ashore in a different age
A thousand miles from the open stage
The water's deep and the current's strong
We hum the tune of a faded song
The radio plays a foreign sound
But we are drifting above the ground

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, drums become more driving)*
Like strangers in the stream!
Waiting for the dawn to break the dream!
Holding on to what we used to know
Another place, another time ago!
Strangers in the stream...

[Verse 2]
*(Dynamics pull back to focus on the fretless bass and vocals)*
The letters pile by the open door
A shadow falls on the wooden floor
I see your face in the patterned glass
And watch the days as they slowly pass
We row against an invisible tide
With nowhere left for the ghosts to hide

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, drums become more driving)*
Like strangers in the stream!
Waiting for the dawn to break the dream!
Holding on to what we used to know
Another place, another time ago!
Strangers in the stream...

[Bridge]
*(Atmospheric breakdown, vocals are hushed and urgent)*
Is it a matter of time?
A mountain we have to climb?
The water is cold, the water is wide
We have to reach the other side!

[Instrumental Break]
*(A soaring, emotional synthesizer solo over a driving beat)*

[Chorus]
Like strangers in the stream!
Waiting for the dawn to break the dream!
Holding on to what we used to know
Another place, another time ago!
Strangers in the stream!

[Outro]
*(The sweeping synth pads slowly fade)*
Strangers in the stream...
Waiting for the dawn...
*(Fades to silence)*

title: The Masquerade
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"The Masquerade" introduces the explicit concept of the "fragile fortress"—a direct reference to the physical and emotional sanctuary Rhys built for Claire in Williamsport. The "gallery of ghosts" represents the haunting presence of their four deceased bandmates. By dressing up and playing the parts of a full six-piece band using mechanical synthesizers and salvaged instruments, Rhys and Claire are putting on a theatrical "masquerade" to mask the overwhelming emptiness left behind. 

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet, theatrical)*

[Intro]
*(A dramatic, solitary piano melody begins)*
*(Sweeping analog strings and a pulsing synth bass join in)*

[Verse 1]
We paint the faces, we choose the dress
To hide the pieces of the emptiness
We walk the avenue in borrowed clothes
And play the part that everybody knows
A gallery of ghosts inside the hall
We smile to prove we haven't lost it all

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, the gated snare drum hits hard)*
Welcome to the masquerade!
In the fragile fortress we have made!
Spinning in the shadows, out of sight!
Dancing on the edges of the night!
In the masquerade...

[Verse 2]
*(Dynamics pull back to the pulsing bass and dramatic piano)*
The music swelters and the voices rise
To drown the secrets in our weary eyes
We hold together when the curtain falls
But no one answers when the echo calls
A beautiful illusion we protect
A grand design of cause and of effect

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, sweeping analog strings soar)*
Welcome to the masquerade!
In the fragile fortress we have made!
Spinning in the shadows, out of sight!
Dancing on the edges of the night!
In the masquerade...

[Bridge]
*(The drums drop out, leaving tense, layered vocals)*
Take off the mask! The hour is late!
We cannot always hide from fate!
The colours bleed, the mirrors crack!
And there is no way turning back!

[Instrumental Break]
*(A grandiose, theatrical synthesizer solo, weaving with the sweeping strings)*

[Chorus]
Welcome to the masquerade!
In the fragile fortress we have made!
Spinning in the shadows, out of sight!
Dancing on the edges of the night!
In the masquerade!

[Outro]
*(The heavy drums fade out)*
*(Leaving just the solitary piano)*
The painted smiles...
The fading spark...
*(Fade to silence)*

title: Fractured Prisms
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The title track of the album serves as the emotional crux of the duo's new identity. The lyric *"There was a time we had a name"* is a direct, mournful reference to the Manning Family Orchestra, the sprawling six-piece 1970s band that existed before the tragedy. 

This track also marks the first time we hear the "Safe Harbor" leitmotif played on Gwen's salvaged wooden flute. While Claire is credited with the flute parts, her performance here is intentionally sparse. The emotional weight of playing her deceased cousin's instrument was so paralyzing that she could only bring herself to play the haunting melody at the beginning, before pushing through the grief to weave it into the thundering stadium-rock climax.

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet, slow burn)*

[Intro]
*(A low, ominous analog synth drone)*
*(A haunting, ethereal flute melody—the 'Safe Harbor' leitmotif—drifts through the dark)*
*(Slow, deliberate guitar chords echo)*

[Verse 1]
*(Hushed, tense)*
We took the pieces from the fire
We pulled the diamonds from the wire
There was a time we had a name
Before the fracture and the flame
Now all the colours bleed to white
Beneath this artificial light...

[Chorus]
*(Pulsing bassline enters)*
We are the fractured prisms in the cold!
We bend the light from stories we were told!
A shattered glass to catch the morning sun!
Look at the beautiful damage we have done!

[Verse 2]
*(Rhythm pulses harder)*
They built a wall to keep us in
They tried to wash away the sin
But every crack inside the stone
Is just a path that we have known
We hold the edges, sharp and clear
There is no room for pity here!

[Bridge]
*(The synths swell massively)*
*(The 'Safe Harbor' flute returns, but now it is urgent and soaring)*
We bend the light!
We bend the light!

[Instrumental Break - The Climax]
*(A THUNDERING, massive gated drum fill explodes!)*
*(Heavy stadium-rock drums and a soaring electric guitar solo weave with the flute)*

[Chorus]
*(Full, massive stadium rock energy)*
We are the fractured prisms in the cold!
We bend the light from stories we were told!
A shattered glass to catch the morning sun!
Look at the beautiful damage we have done!

[Outro]
*(The heavy drums continue to pound)*
*(The flute leitmotif plays one final, lonely time over the fading guitar)*
The fractured prisms...
*(Final massive drum hit)*
*(Fade to silence)*

title: Mirrors of Yesterday
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Mirrors of Yesterday" represents a significant emotional breakthrough for Claire. After the paralyzing grief that limited her performance on the title track, she finally finds the strength to play her late cousin Gwen’s salvaged wooden flute throughout an entire song. 

The upbeat, melodic progressive pop production masks a profound desperation to cope with their loss. Most notably, the track features a sweeping, virtuoso flute solo in the bridge. Because the tragic loss of their cousin Simon severed the band's connection to traditional rock and roll, Claire and Rhys were forced to let the woodwinds and synthesizers carry the soaring emotional weight that a guitar solo would have traditionally held.

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet, nostalgic)*

[Intro]
*(A warm, melodic analog synth pad enters)*
*(The flute begins a long, flowing melody that continues under the vocals)*

[Verse 1]
The dust has settled on the keys
A whisper in the willow trees
I see a face I used to know
In a mirror from along ago
The glass is silvered, cracked and grey
The shadows of a yesterday

[Chorus]
*(Flute melody becomes more rhythmic and prominent)*
Turn the page and let the colours fade
In the mirrors of the lives we made!
We are looking through a broken lens
Finding where the circle ends and begins!
Mirrors of yesterday...

[Verse 2]
*(Flute continues to weave between vocal lines)*
You trace the outline of the frame
And softly speak a faded name
The hallway echoes with the sound
Of orchestras beneath the ground
But in the glass, the light is new
And I am standing here with you

[Chorus]
*(Full ensemble, flute playing high melodic counterpoint)*
Turn the page and let the colours fade
In the mirrors of the lives we made!
We are looking through a broken lens
Finding where the circle ends and begins!
Mirrors of yesterday...

[Bridge]
*(Dynamics drop to just the flute and hushed vocals)*
*(The flute plays a sad, slow version of the 'Safe Harbor' theme)*
It's all we have, it's all we keep
Awakening from twenty years of sleep...

[Instrumental Break - Flute Solo]
*(A long, virtuoso flute solo replaces the guitar, soaring over a steady 80s beat)*
*(The melody is complex, airy, and deeply emotional)*

[Chorus]
*(Massive 1983 production, flute and synths in unison)*
Turn the page and let the colours fade
In the mirrors of the lives we made!
We are looking through a broken lens
Finding where the circle ends and begins!
Mirrors of yesterday!

[Outro]
*(The drums fade out, leaving only the flute)*
*(The flute plays until the very end, becoming the only sound left)*
Mirrors of yesterday...
*(Flute fades to silence)*

title: The Fading Spark
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"The Fading Spark" captures the profound, paranoid anxiety of maintaining the "fragile fortress" Rhys built for Claire in Maryland. The fortress of synthesizers and drum machines was engineered not just to make music, but to create a highly controlled, predictable environment to keep Claire's sensory processing safe from the overwhelming noise of the outside world, and to keep the ghosts of their family at bay. 

The track's frantic, staccato rhythm mimics a failing machine. When Claire plays the fast, echoing flute solo—sounding "like a bird trapped in a machine"—it represents the terrifying realization that their isolated mechanical sanctuary is only a temporary fix, and the emotional weight of their grief might eventually cause the whole system to crash.

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet, urgent, staccato)*

[Intro]
*(A fast, dry, staccato synth pulse starts immediately)*
*(A frantic, echoing flute melody weaves through the rhythm)*
*(Tight, snapping drum machine enters)*

[Verse 1]
*(Vocals are rhythmic and clipped)*
The lights are dimming in the hall
The shadows climbing up the wall
We check the dials, turn the wheel
But there is nothing left to feel
The engine shudders, then it stops
The pressure in the chamber drops

[Chorus]
*(Music becomes denser, more paranoid)*
It's just a fading spark!
A flicker in the growing dark!
We're running out of time and space!
Inside this hollow, empty place!
The fading spark...

[Verse 2]
*(Staccato rhythm continues, more intense)*
You search the wiring for a sign
You trace the path of every line
The system crashes, one by one
Until the work is left undone
We built the fortress way too high
And watched the colours bleed and die

[Chorus]
*(Full energy, frantic flute counter-melodies)*
It's just a fading spark!
A flicker in the growing dark!
We're running out of time and space!
Inside this hollow, empty place!
The fading spark...

[Bridge]
*(The drums become a relentless, dry pulse)*
*(Layered, whispered vocals)*
Is it over?
Is it done?
Waiting for the fading sun...
No one's left to play the part
Hide the secret in your heart!

[Instrumental Break - Flute Solo]
*(The flute plays a fast, staccato, rhythmic solo that mimics the synth pulse)*
*(It sounds urgent, almost like a bird trapped in a machine)*

[Chorus]
It's just a fading spark!
A flicker in the growing dark!
We're running out of time and space!
Inside this hollow, empty place!
The fading spark!

[Outro]
*(The drums and bass drop out suddenly)*
*(Leaving only the frantic, echoing flute and the fading synth pulse)*
Fade to grey...
Fade to black...
*(The synth pulse slows down and stops like a dying machine)*
*(Final breath of the flute)*

title: Kaleidoscope Sun
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Released on Fractured Prisms' 1983 album, Carnaby Street. Following the devastating loss of their four bandmates and siblings in a 1981 crash, and Claire’s subsequent escape from an abusive, legally fraudulent relationship in Romford, the surviving siblings fled to their father's childhood home in Williamsport, Maryland.

Written in the safety of that transatlantic sanctuary, "Kaleidoscope Sun" is a literal call to come home. Claire penned the lyrics as a beacon of hope for anyone trapped in a false reality, urging them toward where the "true light gleams." The track represents a massive emotional breakthrough for Claire. After struggling to play her late cousin Gwen’s salvaged wooden flute on earlier tracks, she finally feels ready to properly play it here. She delivers a distinct flute melody from 1:45 to 2:00, a returning leitmotif at 3:50, and most importantly, a soaring flute solo from 4:00 to 4:32 that completely replaces a traditional rock guitar solo.

In the extended timeline of the Ocean View Archives, this track transcends its 1983 origins. Luna uses the exact melody from the 1:45 mark—either played on her own instrument or simply hummed—as a non-verbal lifeline for her brother, Leo, communicating: "We hear you, and we're getting you out now."

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet)*

[Intro]
*(Begins with a distinctive, slightly melancholic keyboard arpeggio, joined by a driving bassline and crisp drumming. A soaring guitar melody enters, then fades as Rhys Manning's vocals begin.)*

[Verse 1]
The city sleeps in shades of grey, another dawn begins
Another street, another day, where no one ever wins
A hollow echo in the square, a promise whispered low
Of somewhere else, beyond compare, a place where true things grow.
The faces blur, a passing stream, a river deep and wide
Lost in a half-forgotten dream, where do the lost ones hide?

[Chorus]
*(Music swells, becoming more layered, with harmonies. The tempo lifts slightly.)*
Do you hear it?
A whisper on the wind, a melody so clear?
*(Keyboard flourish, echoing a flute-like sound)*
(Oh, the true light gleams...)
Will you come back?
To where the true light gleams, and home is always near?

[Short Instrumental Break]
*(From 1:45 to 2:00, the specific, brief, and distinctive FLUTE MELODY plays. It is poignant, clear, and memorable—the exact melody Luna uses as Leo's lifeline.)*

[Verse 2]
We chase the shadows on the wall, illusions that we build
Afraid to leap, afraid to fall, a prophecy fulfilled.
The painted smiles, a masquerade, to hide the fading spark
A fragile fortress we have made, against the growing dark.
But in the distance, I can see a shimmer in the air
A different kind of mystery, a world beyond compare.

[Chorus]
Do you hear it?
A whisper on the wind, a melody so clear?
*(Keyboard flourish, echoing a flute-like sound)*
(Oh, the true light gleams...)
Will you come back?
To where the true light gleams, and home is always near?

[Bridge]
*(Music becomes more atmospheric, layered keyboards, a searching guitar line, and more prominent bass. Tempo slows slightly before building again.)*
Through fractured prisms, light divides, in patterns sharp and bright
A thousand paths, where fate presides, between the day and night.
Is it a vision, just a trace? A trick of weary eyes?
Or is there truly such a place, beneath those shifting skies?
A shelter from the endless rain, a refuge from the cold…
A story waiting to unfold, a legend to be told.

[Instrumental Section]
*(At 3:50, the flute leitmotif echoes subtly. Then, from 4:00 to 4:32, Claire takes center stage with a sweeping, virtuoso FLUTE SOLO, fully replacing the traditional guitar lead and cementing her emotional return.)*

[Chorus]
Do you hear it?
A whisper on the wind, a melody so clear?
*(Keyboard flourish, echoing a flute-like sound)*
(Oh, the true light gleams...)
Will you come back?
To where the true light gleams, and home is always near?

[Outro]
*(Music begins to fade, the initial keyboard arpeggio returning. The vocals become softer, more distant)*
Home is always near...
Kaleidoscope Sun...
*(The distinctive flute melody plays one last time, very softly, as the song fades to silence)*

title: The Silent Storm
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"The Silent Storm" serves as the cinematic, deeply intimate closer to *Carnaby Street*. The frantic tension of the album's earlier tracks finally breaks, leaving only a slow, open grand piano and sweeping synthesizer pads. The lyrics gently lay the ghosts of the Manning Family Orchestra to rest ("The orchestra has gone to sleep / And gave us promises to keep").

Behind the scenes, this was an agonizing track for the siblings to finish. Claire, who is autistic and processes emotional and sensory input with intense depth, experienced several meltdowns during the refinement of this song. Stripped of the mechanical, driving drum machines that usually anchored her, the overwhelming emotional resonance of the music—and the finality of letting the grief go—was frequently too much to bear. It remains a difficult, but profoundly peaceful, track to listen to, representing the moment the siblings finally found their sanctuary.

**LYRICS:**

*(Vocal Style: British Pop, male and female duet, intimate, slow)*

[Intro]
*(A solitary, echoing grand piano plays a slow, open chord progression)*
*(Wide, warm analog synthesizer pads slowly rise like dawn)*
*(The 'Safe Harbor' flute plays a soft, comforting melody)*

[Verse 1]
*(Vocals are gentle, close to the microphone)*
The wind has dropped beyond the trees
A sudden calm upon the seas
We watched the lightning strike the ground
But now there is no other sound
The broken glass is swept away
To leave us in the light of day

[Chorus]
*(The synths swell warmly, no heavy drums, just a soft pulse)*
And we are walking in the silent storm...
Waiting for the water to keep us warm...
The empty space is just a shape we leave behind
A quiet place for us to finally find!
In the silent storm...

[Verse 2]
*(The flute weaves gently around the vocal lines)*
You fold the papers, close the door
We don't need answers anymore
The orchestra has gone to sleep
And gave us promises to keep
We crossed the ocean in the dark
To rescue one remaining spark

[Chorus]
*(The duet vocals soar, backed by massive, majestic synth pads)*
And we are walking in the silent storm...
Waiting for the water to keep us warm...
The empty space is just a shape we leave behind
A quiet place for us to finally find!
In the silent storm!

[Bridge]
*(The music drops to just the piano and the two voices in unison)*
The true light gleams...
It always gleams...
We wake up from the shattered dreams...

[Instrumental Break - The Final Resolution]
*(A slow, majestic crescendo of sweeping strings, piano, and the flute)*
*(It is triumphant, but deeply emotional and peaceful)*

[Outro]
*(The music begins a very long, slow fade out)*
*(Rhys and Claire trade soft vocal echoes)*
The silent storm...
The true light gleams...
*(The flute takes over, playing the 'Safe Harbor' theme one last time)*
*(Fading... fading...)*
*(Only the sound of a distant, warm synth pad remains)*
*(Fade to absolute silence)*

title: Architects of the Rain
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The sweeping opening duet of *1883*. Rhys and Claire step across a century into the gaslamp-lit iron gates of their Victorian sanctuary, where analog synthesizer wires and Gwen's wooden flute turn ghosts into gold.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Brooding analog synthesizer arpeggios and heavy gated drums)
(Gwen's wooden flute enters with a haunting Victorian melody)

[Verse 1]
Gaslight glimmers on the wet slate stone
A hundred years in a house we own
Rhys turns the dial, the gears engage
We live inside the empty page
Fog in the lungs, wire in the vein
We are the architects of the rain!

[Chorus]
We stand within the iron gate!
Defying time, defying fate!
The four are here, the square is whole
In this machine we find their soul!
In the Hollow Square...

[Verse 2]
I walk the halls in the London night
Finding my feet in the flickering light
A century fades to a gentle hum
To the beat of a distant drum
The prism turns the ghosts to gold
A story finished, yet to be told!

[Chorus]
We stand within the iron gate!
Defying time, defying fate!
The four are here, the square is whole
In this machine we find their soul!
In the Hollow Square...

[Guitar & Flute Bridge]
(Soaring electric guitar solo intertwined with synthesizer pads)
Gwen is in the wires...
Safe harbour...
Keep the fire!
(Flute and synthesizer duel)

[Chorus]
We stand within the iron gate!
Defying time, defying fate!
The four are here, the square is whole
In this machine we find their soul!

[Outro]
In the Hollow Square...
In the Hollow Square...
In the Hollow Square...
1883.
(Flute melody fades over pulsing synthesizer bass)

title: Four at the Table
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
In the *1883* psychological sanctuary, the 1981 Shap Fell tragedy never happened. Morning breaks over the slate roof as all six siblings—Alistair, Gwen, Simon, Julian, Rhys, and Claire—gather in the Victorian parlor ("four at the table, two by the fire") with Gwen's flute leading the morning song.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Bright, intricate wooden flute melody over acoustic guitar and warm 80s rhythm section)

[Verse 1]
The morning breaks the slate, the shadows pull away
The dust is dancing in the light of day
Alistair is counting, the brass and timbering
We gather in the parlor just to hear the timber sing
Simon tunes the silver, Julian bows the wood
A century is standing right where it should
No wires in the walls, no ghosts inside the frame
Just the six of us together, calling out the name!

[Chorus]
There are four at the table, two by the fire!
Building up the harmony, climbing ever higher!
The Square is whole, the foundation is strong
We are living in the center of the morning song!
Oh, the morning song!

[Verse 2]
Gwen is on the melody, breathing through the reed
A safe and gentle harbor is the only thing we need
The brass is shining golden, the strings are pulled in tight
We lock the heavy iron gate against the fading night
Simon tunes the silver, Julian bows the wood
A century is standing right where it should
No wires in the walls, no ghosts inside the frame
Just the six of us together, calling out the name!

[Chorus]
There are four at the table, two by the fire!
Building up the harmony, climbing ever higher!
The Square is whole, the foundation is strong
We are living in the center of the morning song!
Oh, the morning song!

[Bridge]
Breathe in the dust, breathe in the wood
A century standing where the family stood!
(Virtuosic electric guitar and wooden flute duet)

[Chorus]
There are four at the table, two by the fire!
Building up the harmony, climbing ever higher!
The Square is whole, the foundation is strong
We are living in the center of the morning song!
Four at the table, two by the fire!
The Square is whole!

title: The Brass Escapement
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
As the parlor sleeps, Rhys retreats to his mechanical workshop—reimagining his 1980s synthesizer sequencers as a Victorian brass escapement and pinned copper cylinder that locks the family's pulse into a flawless 100-year design that can never betray or die.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(High-speed analog sequencer pulse and brassy synthesizer fanfare)

[Verse 1]
The parlor sleeps, the fire dies
I measure the moon with glass in my eyes
Flesh and bone will falter and sway
But the teeth of the gear will never betray
Turn the lathe, cut the groove
Watch the copper cylinder move!

[Pre-Chorus]
Alistair beats on the heavy skin
But I found the pulse where the wires begin
No human hand, no breath, no ache
Just the perfect rhythm the metal can make!

[Chorus]
In the brass escapement, the timing is locked!
The pendulum swings and the hammer is cocked!
A hundred years of a flawless design
I am keeping the tempo, I am holding the line!
(Holding the line! Holding the line!)

[Verse 2]
The metronome clicks on the polished wood
I am building the heart that they never could
A golden cage for a silver spring
Just wind it up and listen to it sing
The pin-barrel turns, the hammer falls
Echoing out through the silent halls!

[Pre-Chorus]
Alistair beats on the heavy skin
But I found the pulse where the wires begin
No human hand, no breath, no ache
Just the perfect rhythm the metal can make!

[Chorus]
In the brass escapement, the timing is locked!
The pendulum swings and the hammer is cocked!
A hundred years of a flawless design
I am keeping the tempo, I am holding the line!
(Holding the line! Holding the line!)

[Bridge]
(Blistering neoclassical guitar and synthesizer arpeggio duel)
Measure the weight
Balance the wheel
Nothing is true
But the copper and steel!

[Chorus]
In the brass escapement, the timing is locked!
The pendulum swings and the hammer is cocked!
A hundred years of a flawless design
I am keeping the tempo, I am holding the line!
(Holding the line! Holding the line!)
The timing is locked!
Holding the line!

title: Shadows on the Slate
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Even inside the *1883* sanctuary where she can walk, Claire is still haunted by night terrors as the gaslight drops. Rhys anchors her nervous system through the midnight storm, turning the dial down and holding the line until the break of day.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Haunting synthesizer whistle and crystalline bell sequence over a driving dark-wave bassline)

[Verse 1]
The gaslight drops to a copper wire
The heavy oak doors close on the fire
A ticking clock in the empty hall
And the shadows stretch across the wall
The floorboards breathe, the iron sighs
I see the phantoms in the corners of my eyes

[Pre-Chorus]
The slate is cold, the night is deep
The edges blur before the sleep
It's closing in, the dark is loud
A heavy velvet, suffocating shroud!

[Chorus]
But the anchor holds when the terror spins!
This is the room where the safe begins!
Turn the dial down, keep the monsters at bay
Hold the line until the break of day!
There is no ghost, there is no threat
Just the rain on the slate, and the silhouette

[Verse 2]
The window rattles in the sudden wind
Where does the storm end and the room begin?
The corridors are winding, long and black
If I step out, I might not make it back
The mind is a prism bending the light
Turning the silence into the fright

[Pre-Chorus]
The slate is cold, the night is deep
The edges blur before the sleep
It's closing in, the dark is loud
A heavy velvet, suffocating shroud!

[Chorus]
But the anchor holds when the terror spins!
This is the room where the safe begins!
Turn the dial down, keep the monsters at bay
Hold the line until the break of day!
There is no ghost, there is no threat
Just the rain on the slate, and the silhouette

[Bridge]
Breathe in the dust, breathe in the wood
A century standing where the family stood
The foundation is stone, the lock is turned tight
We banish the bump in the middle of the night!
(Soaring electric guitar and flute solo)

[Chorus]
The anchor holds when the terror spins!
This is the room where the safe begins!
Turn the dial down, keep the monsters at bay
Hold the line until the break of day!
There is no ghost, there is no threat
Just the rain on the slate, and the silhouette

[Outro]
Just the rain...
The silhouette...
Hold the line.

title: The Hollow Square (Live at Independence Stadium)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

Recorded August 15, 1985 before 90,000 fans at Independence Stadium in Philadelphia—Fractured Prisms' first-ever live concert. Enforcing the 'Sacred Perimeter' and 'Session Ghosts' stage manifesto, Rhys and Claire delivered an extended 5:24 stadium rendition of their #1 anthem featuring an opening solo on Gwen's wooden flute.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro - Live at Independence Stadium, 1985]
(Roar of 90,000 fans in Philadelphia)
(Claire opens with a soaring, solitary cadenza on Gwen's wooden flute)
(Massive gated stadium drums and Rhys's analog synthesizer fortress crash in)

[Verse 1]
Four empty spaces in the room
A silent echo in the gloom
We crossed the water to find a shore
But left behind what came before
The city lights are cold and bright
A different sky, a different night!

[Chorus]
Standing in the hollow square!
Reaching out, but no one's there!
We forge the armour, paint the sky
To keep the fading embers high!
In the hollow square!

[Verse 2]
The cables hum, the circuits glow
To mask the quiet down below
We sequence notes to fill the void
A symphony we re-employed
Just two remain to hold the line
And reconstruct the grand design!

[Chorus]
(Instrumental stadium synth and guitar eruption)

[Bridge]
The stage is smaller, but the sound is deep
A promise that we swore to keep
Through the silence, hear the spark
We light the beacons in the dark!

[Instrumental Break]
(Extended live flute, synthesizer, and stadium guitar solo)

[Chorus]
Standing in the hollow square!
Reaching out, but no one's there!
We forge the armour, paint the sky
To keep the fading embers high!
In the hollow square!
In the hollow square!

[Outro]
(90,000 voices roar as the final stadium chord echoes into the Philadelphia night)

title: Electric Color
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The solid **#2 hit**. It sat at the runner-up spot for six weeks, famously blocked from #1 by a certain "novelty song" that swept the summer of '87.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Woke up this morning, the world was gray
Didn't know the colors had all faded away
Been living in a room with the curtains drawn tight
Then you flipped a switch and turned on the light

(Chorus)
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

(Verse 2)
The city sounds were just a buzz in my ear
A static station I could never quite hear
But now the noise is turning into a song
And I finally feel like I belong

(Chorus)
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

(Bridge)
The beat is getting stronger
I can't hide it any longer
My heart is playing catch-up
To the music turning way up!

(Guitar Solo)

(Chorus)
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

(Outro)
Electric color
Feeling so new
It's all because of you

title: Plastic Sky
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Ryan's first act of "malicious compliance." He hid angsty, anti-corporate lyrics about "living under a plastic sky" inside a polished, studio-approved pop-rock wrapper. It is a direct protest against the "thin" sound the studio demanded—Ryan sings explicitly about his guitar being "clean" and the drums being "thin" while the executives nodded along, missing the insult completely.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The camera's on, the smile is bright
Another take in the burning light
They painted the set with a perfect blue
But it doesn't feel real, it doesn't feel true

(Chorus)
We're living under a plastic sky (Oh-oh-oh)
They tell me "jump," I ask "how high?"
(Oh-oh-oh)
It's just a set, it's all a lie
Living under a plastic sky

(Verse 2)
My guitar is clean, the drums are thin
They polished away all the grit and sin
I want to scream, I want to roar
But they just ask me to sing some more

(Chorus)
We're living under a plastic sky (Oh-oh-oh)
They tell me "jump," I ask "how high?"
(Oh-oh-oh)
It's just a set, it's all a lie
Living under a plastic sky

(Bridge)
Is this the dream we were chasing?
A different part, a different face
I'm losing me, I'm losing you
In all this shiny, plastic blue

(Guitar Solo)

(Chorus)
We're living under a plastic sky (Oh-oh-oh)
They tell me "jump," I ask "how high?"
(Oh-oh-oh)
It's just a set, it's all a lie
Living under a plastic sky

(Outro)
Plastic sky...
Feeling so new...
(fades out)

title: My Anchor Holds
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A power ballad the studio marketed as a romance, but which the band wrote about their family bond. This "sibling-love-disguised-as-romance" became a staple of their early sound.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The lights are bright, but the room is cold
Another story that's bought and sold
I'm trying to find a reason why
Beneath this plastic, empty sky

(Chorus)
But when the world is spinning out of my control
You're the one true thing that I can hold
Through the static and the driving rain
You're the one who keeps me sane
You are the shelter, you are the truth
My anchor in this crazy youth

(Verse 2)
They pull us under, they push us high
They build us up just to watch us die
It's hard to know who you can trust
When all the promises turn to dust

(Chorus)
But when the world is spinning out of my control
You're the one true thing that I can hold
Through the static and the driving rain
You're the one who keeps me sane
You are the shelter, you are the truth
My anchor in this crazy youth

(Guitar Solo)

(Bridge)
So let them talk, let them stare
As long as you are standing there
I'm not afraid of what's to come
I know where I belong...

(Chorus)
'Cause when the world is spinning out of my control
You're the one true thing that I can hold
Through the static and the driving rain
You're the one who keeps me sane
You are the shelter, you are the truth
My anchor in this crazy youth

(Outro)
My anchor...
My anchor holds...
(Fades out with piano and synth)

title: Dancing in the Neon
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"I wanna see you dancing to this one, Chicago!" A crowd-pleaser that fit the label's "pop" image perfectly. This was one of the "safe" synth-pop singles Apex Records pushed for, prioritizing high energy and polished production over the band's rock roots.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The city's quiet, the sun is down
We're in the glow of the other side of town
The beat is calling from a place I know
Just follow the sound, and let it go

(Chorus)
We're dancing in the neon (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
We're moving 'til the night is gone (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Forget about tomorrow
We're shining like a light
Dancing in the neon tonight!

(Verse 2)
The rhythm's heavy, a flashing bright
Reflected colors in your eyes
I don't care what the real world wants
This moment's all that I could ever want

(Chorus)
We're dancing in the neon (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
We're moving 'til the night is gone (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Forget about tomorrow
We're shining like a light
Dancing in the neon tonight!

(Bridge)
Don't stop, don't stop the feeling
This music's got me reeling
Don't stop, don't stop the beat
(Synth-pop breakdown / keyboard solo)

(Chorus)
We're dancing in the neon (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
We're moving 'til the night is gone (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Forget about tomorrow
We're shining like a light
Dancing in the neon tonight!

(Outro)
Dancing in the neon... (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
'Til the night is gone...
(fades)

title: Running on the Edge
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Another protest song. Ryan sings about being a "shadow in the light" and having his guitar suppressed ("This keyboard hook is all a bore / I know this guitar's made for more"). It features angsty, anti-corporate lyrics hidden inside a "safe" pop-rock wrapper.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Another day, another show
They tell me which way the wind should blow
I'm smiling 'til my face is numb
Waiting for the day to come

(Pre-Chorus)
I can hear a different sound
A rumble starting underground
This pretty world is gonna break
How much more can I take?

(Chorus)
I'm running on the edge, about to lose control (Oh-oh-oh)
Trying to save my rock and roll soul
I'm running on the edge, a shadow in the light (Oh-oh-oh)
Gonna break out into the night!

(Verse 2)
This keyboard hook is all a bore
I know this guitar's made for more
I want to feel the fire and grit
I'm getting really sick of it

(Pre-Chorus)
I can hear a different sound
A rumble starting underground
This pretty world is gonna break
How much more can I take?

(Chorus)
I'm running on the edge, about to lose control (Oh-oh-oh)
Trying to save my rock and roll soul
I'm running on the edge, a shadow in the light (Oh-oh-oh)
Gonna break out into the night!

(Guitar Solo)

(Chorus)
I'm running on the edge, about to lose control (Oh-oh-oh)
Trying to save my rock and roll soul
I'm running on the edge, a shadow in the light (Oh-oh-oh)
Gonna break out into the night!

(Outro)
Running on the edge...
Running on the edge...
(fades)

title: Just a Girl
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Cassidy's quiet rebellion. Apex executives dismissed this moody, introspective track as "filler," but it became a grassroots anthem for female fans. The honest lyrics about her treatment in the industry ("They tell me 'sing the high note' / They tell me 'wear the red dress'") resonated deeply with young women who felt similarly boxed in by expectations.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
They tell me "sing the high note"
They tell me "wear the red dress"
They never ask me what I wrote
They only want to see the press

(Verse 2)
I bring my chords, my melody
They pat my head and disagree
They turn to him, "now *that's* a sound"
And I'm just standing in the background

(Chorus)
Am I ever gonna break through?
Am I ever gonna get my due?
Or am I just a girl in the band?
A pretty picture, holding your hand

(Verse 3)
They say "be 'Stardust', be the grace"
"Know your role and keep your place"
But I am more than what you see
I'm fighting just to be... me

(Chorus)
Am I ever gonna break through?
Am I ever gonna get my due?
Or am I just a girl in the band?
A pretty picture, holding your hand

(Bridge)
But the music's in my blood
The synth, the key, the flood
You can't erase the fire
My voice is getting higher

(Chorus)
Am I ever gonna break through?
Am I ever gonna get my due?
Or am I just a girl in the band?
A pretty picture, holding your hand

(Outro)
Just a girl...
Just a girl...
(fades out on a shimmering synth pad)

title: Light Up the Night
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The song Apex Records poured *all* of their money into. They were convinced this polished synth-pop track would be "The Big One." It wasn't. Despite the massive marketing campaign, the "safe" sound failed to connect with audiences in the way the band's authentic rock tracks did.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
I was walking in the shadows
I was living in the gray
Waiting for a signal
To help me find my way

(Pre-Chorus)
I can feel a new connection
Like a spark inside the dark
You're my one true direction
You're the fire, you're the spark

(Chorus)
We're gonna light up the night! (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Chasing the stars 'til the morning light
We're gonna make it all right (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Turning our color on, shining so bright
We're gonna light up the night!

(Verse 2)
This city sleeps, but we're awake
A promise that we'll never break
The future's ours, I see the sign
Just put your hand in mine

(Pre-Chorus)
I can feel a new connection
Like a spark inside the dark
You're my one true direction
You're the fire, you're the spark

(Chorus)
We're gonna light up the night! (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Chasing the stars 'til the morning light
We're gonna make it all right (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Turning our color on, shining so bright
We're gonna light up the night!

(Bridge)
No more shadows, no more gray
(Keyboard Solo)

(Chorus)
We're gonna light up the night! (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Chasing the stars 'til the morning light
We're gonna make it all right (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Turning our color on, shining so bright
We're gonna light up the night!

(Outro)
Light up the night... (Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Shining so bright...
(fades)

title: Break the Walls
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The one "pure rock" anthem Apex allowed on the album. It opened Side B and became an immediate fan-favorite for its raw energy. While the studio pushed "Light Up the Night," the fans embraced this track as the true spirit of the band.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Been counting the days in this neon cage
Smiling for the cameras on a plastic stage
They turned the synths up, drowned the sound
But you can't keep a good thing down

(Chorus)
We're gonna break the walls tonight! (Yeah!)
Turn up the volume, hit the light!
No more whispers, time to shout
The Engine's roaring, let it out!

(Verse 2)
I'm tired of the glitter, tired of the gloss
Tired of the suits who think they're the boss
This guitar is loaded, it's ready to scream
Waking up from their pretty dream

(Chorus)
We're gonna break the walls tonight! (Yeah!)
Turn up the volume, hit the light!
No more whispers, time to shout
The Engine's roaring, let it out!

(Guitar Solo)
(A blistering, technical, shredding solo that Ryan fought to keep on the record)

(Bridge)
For every kid who feels the same
Trapped in a world, playing their game
This one's for you, this one's for me
Time to be free!

(Chorus)
We're gonna break the walls tonight! (Yeah!)
Turn up the volume, hit the light!
No more whispers, time to shout
The Engine's roaring, let it out!

(Outro)
Let it out!
Break the walls!
C'mon!
(fades on a hanging guitar chord)

title: Worlds Apart
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
An epic mid-tempo rock ballad that defied the studio's attempt to separate the band's "Stardust" and "Engine" personas. It features a massive, soaring duet between Ryan and Cassidy, proving their voices worked best when fighting together rather than apart. The lyrics in the third verse ("They want the 'Stardust,' they want the 'Engine'") are a direct meta-commentary on their struggle with Apex Records.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Another mile on a lonely road
Just trying to get back to you
I'm carrying this heavy load
They're telling me what I have to do

(Verse 2)
The lights are bright, the stage is cold
They're trying to fit me in their mold
I see your face across the black
I know that we can find our way back

(Chorus)
We're worlds apart, but our hearts beat the same (Oh-oh)
I can hear you call my name
Through the distance, through the static and the dark
We're finding a way back to the start (Oh-oh)
Even when we're worlds apart

(Verse 3)
They want the "Stardust," they want the "Engine"
A different version for a different show
But we're the ones who'll be here in the end
We've got a fire they'll never know

(Chorus)
We're worlds apart, but our hearts beat the same (Oh-oh)
I can hear you call my name
Through the distance, through the static and the dark
We're finding a way back to the start (Oh-oh)
Even when we're worlds apart

(Guitar Solo)

(Bridge)
And when the mountains fall
And when the oceans rise
I'll find you (I'll find you!)

(Chorus)
We're worlds apart, but our hearts beat the same (Oh-oh)
I can hear you call my name
Through the distance, through the static and the dark
We're finding a way back to the start (Oh-oh)
Even when we're worlds apart

(Outro)
Worlds apart...
(fades)

title: Another Night
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A "safe" filler track demanded by Apex to pad out the album with radio-friendly pop. Ryan was explicitly banned from playing on this track ("No guitar allowed" was written on the session sheet), leaving Cassidy isolated with just a synthesizer backing track. Her vocal performance is genuinely upset, but not because of a breakup—she was miserable recording without her brother in the studio.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The clock on the wall is ticking slow
I'm watching the rain fall on the window
I pick up the phone, but I let it go
Just waiting for a voice I know

(Chorus)
It's just another night without you (Oh-oh)
Another night I've got to get through
The city's sleeping, but I'm awake
Another night, for goodness sake

(Verse 2)
The TV's on, but the sound is low
I've got no other place to go
The silence is a heavy sound
I wish that you were here right now

(Chorus)
It's just another night without you (Oh-oh)
Another night I've got to get through
The city's sleeping, but I'm awake
Another night, for goodness sake

(Bridge)
(A very simple, minimal, clean keyboard solo. No guitar allowed.)

(Chorus)
It's just another night without you (Oh-oh)
Another night I've got to get through
The city's sleeping, but I'm awake
Another night, for goodness sake

(Outro)
Another night...
Another night...
(fades out)

title: Out of Time
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Ryan's punk-inspired vent. The 13-track album was too long for a standard vinyl LP, so Apex executives "gleefully" cut this short, 1:35 track from the original vinyl release to save space. They viewed it as "noise," but to Ryan, cutting his rawest song was a direct attempt to silence the "Engine."

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Tick-tock goes the plastic clock
Another meeting on another block
They're selling me a future that I don't want
It's just the same old tired font

(Chorus)
I'm out of patience!
I'm out of time!
This ain't your product, this life is mine!
Out of patience!
Out of time!
Gonna break free, gonna cross the line!

(Verse 2)
You want another ballad, soft and slow
Another song for the radio
But I've got a fire burning in my hands
You'll never, ever understand

(Chorus)
I'm out of patience!
I'm out of time!
This ain't your product, this life is mine!
Out of patience!
Out of time!
Gonna break free, gonna cross the line!

(Guitar Solo)
(Short, fast, and chaotic. Pure punk-rock energy)

(Chorus)
I'm out of patience!
I'm out of time!
This ain't your product, this life is mine!
Out of patience!
Out of time!
Gonna break free, gonna cross the line!

(Outro)
Out of time!
(Song ends abruptly on a final, crashing chord)

title: Rearview Mirror
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A moody, atmospheric "driving song" that sets the stage for the album's finale. While Apex approved it for its polished synth-pop sound, Cassidy used the lyrics to express her feeling of being a "passenger" in her own career. The poignant line "With all this 'Stardust' left inside" serves as a double entendre for her suppressed creative potential vs. the manufactured image she was forced to project.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Another city, another night
We're speeding past the exit light
I see the skyline start to fade
A memory of a choice I made

(Chorus)
I'm looking in the rearview mirror
The past is getting clearer
Was it all just a mistake?
A heart that's learning how to break
It's all in the rearview mirror

(Verse 2)
This neon glow feels cold and thin
I don't know where I'm supposed to begin
I'm just a passenger in this ride
With all this "Stardust" left inside

(Chorus)
I'm looking in the rearview mirror
The past is getting clearer
Was it all just a mistake?
A heart that's learning how to break
It's all in the rearview mirror

(Bridge)
(A moody, atmospheric keyboard solo)
I'm driving fast, but I'm not free
Just running from the girl I used to be

(Chorus)
I'm looking in the rearview mirror
The past is getting clearer
Was it all just a mistake?
A heart that's learning how to break
It's all in the rearview mirror

(Outro)
Fading... fading...
In the rearview mirror...
(fades)

title: The Stardust Engine
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Released in 1987 alongside the rest of *Electric Color* and buried by Apex Records at the very end of the album, this is the band's true origin anthem. *"The Stardust Engine"* was the very first song Cassidy and Ryan O'Connell came up with in 1986 when their twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright joined them at CPI. Too scared at the time to shop the song around, the four of them kept it to themselves and decided to use that first song to name their band—celebrating their love of the cosmos ("Stardust") and the rockets to get you there ("Engine"). (Apex Records later screwed around and labeled Cassidy as their "Stardust" and Ryan as their "Engine"—a cheap 1980s corporate naming gimmick the band hated because it took away from their love of the cosmos and the rockets to get you there.) Critics and chart historians agree: had Apex released this as the lead single instead of burying it, it would have spent **11 straight weeks at #1**, dethroning the existing record holder for the decade.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
We were looking for a signal
A light in the endless black
A single voice in the universe
To tell us we're on the right track

(Verse 2)
We found the fire in the wires
We found the heart in the machine
Building a dream from nothing
A sound the world has never seen

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Verse 3)
They tried to ground us, keep us small
Tell us that we were gonna fall
But they don't know the things we know
They haven't seen the places we'll go

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Guitar Solo)
(A soaring, melodic solo that trades licks with a bright synthesizer hook)

(Bridge)
We are the cosmos, we are the fire
We're taking this one, higher and higher
We are the Stardust!
(We are the Engine!)
We are the Stardust Engine!

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Outro)
Shining so bright...
We're taking flight...
(fades out on an epic, sustained guitar chord)

title: Neon Hearts
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The "safe" title track. Apex forced the band to include a callback lyric to their first hit ("It's an electric-colored feeling") to ensure brand consistency. The studio demanded this track open the album to assure fans that the "Stardust" sound hadn't changed, despite the band's desire to move toward rock.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The city's humming, the lights are low
I'm waiting for you, I'm ready to go
The rain is tapping on the glass
I knew this feeling was built to last

(Pre-Chorus)
I hear your footsteps in the hall
I'm not afraid to fall
This is the only thing I know is true

(Chorus)
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

(Verse 2)
We're walking fast on the wet concrete
The rhythm matches when our eyes meet
Don't need a promise, don't need a vow
My only moment is right here, right now

(Pre-Chorus)
I hear your footsteps in the hall
I'm not afraid to fall
This is the only thing I know is true

(Chorus)
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

(Bridge)
(A bright, energetic keyboard solo)
Let the city sleep, we're wide awake
A chance that we're both gonna take!

(Chorus)
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

(Outro)
My neon heart... (Shining for you)
My neon heart...
(fades out)

title: Hollow Sound
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Ryan's act of "malicious compliance." He delivered the requested synth-pop sound but made the track **5:31 long**—knowing it was too long for radio—and included the protest line, "They're all afraid of the burning cross" (a reference to the canceled "Promise" single). It stands as a middle finger to the studio's "safe" direction.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The red light's on, the tape is rolling
They're telling me what words to say
I'm trying to find the man I was
But he gets farther every day

(Verse 2)
They want the polish, they want the gleam
The "safer" version of the dream
But all I hear is a thin machine
Another part of their big scene

(Chorus)
It's just a hollow sound
My voice is in the mix
But the words are not my own
It's just a hollow sound
Another plastic fix
I'm singing all alone

(Verse 3)
They're all afraid of the burning cross
Terrified of what they lost
So now they're sanding off the edge
Pushing me back from the ledge

(Chorus)
It's just a hollow sound
My voice is in the mix
But the words are not my own
It's just a hollow sound
Another plastic fix
I'm singing all alone

(Bridge)
(A very clean, melodic, studio-approved keyboard solo)
A hollow sound...
Just a hollow sound...

(Chorus)
It's just a hollow sound
My voice is in the mix
But the words are not my own
It's just a hollow sound
Another plastic fix
I'm singing all alone
(fades)

title: Side by Side
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The studio's furious overcorrection to "Hollow Sound." After Ryan delivered a 5:31 protest track, Apex demanded an absurdly short, safe pop song to balance the runtime and "fix" the album's pacing. The result is this 1:54 "bubblegum" track that feels almost manic in its enforced cheerfulness.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
When the rain is falling
And you feel all alone
Just remember I'm here
You can call me on the phone

(Chorus)
'Cause we're always better together
In any kind of weather
We don't have to hide
We're walking side by side (Oh-oh)
Side by side

(Verse 2)
The world can be a lonely place
A fast and hurried, crazy race
But we can slow it down a while
It's always better when I see you smile

(Chorus)
'Cause we're always better together
In any kind of weather
We don't have to hide
We're walking side by side (Oh-oh)
Side by side

(Bridge)
(A very short, simple, melodic keyboard riff)
Through the highs, through the lows
That's just the way it goes

(Chorus)
'Cause we're always better together
In any kind of weather
We don't have to hide
We're walking side by side (Oh-oh)
Side by side

(Outro)
Side by side...
(fades quickly)

title: If You Walked Away
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The "late-night radio" ballad Apex demanded to balance out the album's "weirdness." The studio marketed this as a romantic "breakup what-if" song. In reality, Cassidy sang it to Ryan. Isolated by the studio's attempts to separate their "Stardust" and "Engine" personas, this was her genuine expression of fear that he might actually leave her alone in the machine.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The streetlights make a blurry line
I'm running through the same old signs
I'm just a face in a passing crowd
Afraid to speak my thoughts out loud

(Verse 2)
But then you found me in the noise
You heard a whisper in my voice
You gave me something to believe
A reason I would never leave

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Verse 3)
They build these walls so high and steep
With promises they never keep
But we have a fortress, strong and true
I'm safe as long as I have you

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Bridge)
(A very safe, melodic, clean keyboard solo)
I'm holding on, I'm holding tight
Don't let me go into the night...

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Outro)
Don't walk away...
(fades out on piano)

title: Same Old Song
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Ryan's "Trojan Horse." The track opens with a bright, optimistic keyboard hook that promises a radio-friendly hit, but the lyrics are a scathing critique of the studio's formulaic songwriting process. Ryan delivered the exact "polished sheen" Apex demanded, but used it to sing about how "safe" and suffocating the production had become ("Turn on the keyboard, keep the guitar low").

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
They hand me the chords, they're all the same
A different title for the same old game
Turn on the keyboard, keep the guitar low
Just another track for the radio

(Chorus)
It's just the same old song (Oh-oh)
Another right to make a wrong
I'm singing words I don't believe
It's getting harder and harder to breathe
It's just the same old song

(Verse 2)
I'm dreaming of a feedback wail
A drum kit hit like a hammer on a nail
But all I get is this polished sheen
The safest sound you've ever seen

(Chorus)
It's just the same old song (Oh-oh)
Another right to make a wrong
I'm singing words I don't believe
It's getting harder and harder to breathe
It's just the same old song

(Bridge)
(A very clean, melodic, studio-approved guitar solo)
Is anybody listening?
Is anybody real?
Or do you just like the way it feels?

(Chorus)
It's just the same old song (Oh-oh)
Another right to make a wrong
I'm singing words I don't believe
It's getting harder and harder to breathe
It's just the same old song

(Outro)
The same old song...
(fades out)

title: Chain Reaction
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The start of the "Side B Rebellion." After an A-Side full of studio-mandated synth-pop, Apex allowed this "one-two punch" of pure rock (paired with the following track, "Not Your Doll") as a concession. It became an immediate fan favorite, proving that the "Engine" sound was what the audience actually wanted.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
Another day, another line to say
They're trying to wash the real me away
But there's a fire, a burning sound
You can't keep a good thing down

(Chorus)
It's a chain reaction! (Oh-oh)
I can't be contained
Starting up a fire that can't be explained
A chain reaction!
It's time to break the mold
A story that's about to be told!

(Guitar Solo 1)
(A blistering, technical, shredding solo that Ryan fought to keep on the record)

(Verse 2)
This plastic world is gonna crack
I'm never ever looking back
I'm turning up my guitar loud
I'm gonna stand out from the crowd

(Chorus)
A chain reaction!
I can't be contained
Starting up a fire that can't be explained
A chain reaction!
It's time to break the mold
A story that's about to be told!

(Guitar Solo 2)
(Extended technical guitar solo)

(Chorus)
A chain reaction!
I can't be contained
Starting up a fire that can't be explained
A chain reaction!
It's time to break the mold
A story that's about to be told!

(Outro)
Chain reaction...
(fades on a hanging guitar chord)

title: Not Your Doll
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Cassidy's "fierce side" finally breaking through. Following immediately after "Chain Reaction," this arena rock anthem completes the "Side B Rebellion." In it, Cassidy directly rejects the "Stardust" persona Apex forced upon her. While the studio tried to suppress her "Engine" side, this track became the definitive proof that she could rock just as hard as her brother.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
You put me in a box, you told me to be sweet
The "Stardust" girl, the perfect beat
You told me "soften up," you told me "know your place"
But you never saw the fire in my face

(Chorus)
'Cause I'm not your doll!
I'm not your pretty toy
I'm not just a picture for a poster boy
I'm not your doll!
I'm here to make a choice
And I'm gonna make you hear my voice!

(Verse 2)
You're scared of the noise, you're scared of the grit
You're terrified that I'm not gonna fit
In the tiny world you built for me
But I'm about to set myself free

(Chorus)
'Cause I'm not your doll!
I'm not your pretty toy
I'm not just a picture for a poster boy
I'm not your doll!
I'm here to make a choice
And I'm gonna make you hear my voice!

(Guitar Solo)

(Bridge)
You heard the "story to be told"?
Well, I'm the one who'll break the mold!
You wanted 'Stardust'? You get the fire!
My voice is real, and it's getting higher!

(Chorus)
'Cause I'm not your doll!
I'm not your pretty toy
I'm not just a picture for a poster boy
I'm not your doll!
I'm here to make a choice
And I'm gonna make you hear my voice!

(Outro)
Not your doll!
Hear my voice!
(fades out on a wailing guitar note)

title: Quiet on the Set
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The "Punishment" begins. After the explosive rock energy of the "one-two punch" on Side B, Apex executives stepped in to "shut the Engine down." They forced Ryan to record this quiet, introspective ballad to kill the momentum. The lyrics are a meta-commentary on his silencing ("This is the price for being loud / Getting lost back in the crowd").

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The "story" has been told
The echo's fading fast
I tried to "break the mold"
They told me it would never last
They're shutting down the "Engine"

(Chorus)
Now it's quiet on the set (Oh-oh)
Back to the silence and regret
This is the price for being loud
Getting lost back in the crowd
After the laughter...

(Verse 2)
The "noise" we made was all too real
They're terrified of what they feel
So turn the keyboards up again
And hide the anger and the pain

(Chorus)
Now it's quiet on the set (Oh-oh)
Back to the silence and regret
This is the price for being loud
Getting lost back in the crowd
After the laughter...

(Bridge)
(A soft, melodic keyboard solo. No guitars.)
They want the "Stardust," safe and light
Just close your eyes and end the fight
Just close your eyes...

(Chorus)
Now it's quiet on the set (Oh-oh)
Back to the silence and regret
This is the price for being loud
Getting lost back in the crowd
After the laughter...

(Outro)
After the laughter...
Just... quiet...
(fades out on a single piano note)

title: Shadow Dancing
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The studio strikes back. Immediately following the "rebellion" of Side B's opening tracks, Apex Records moved to crush the momentum. They forced Cassidy back into her "Stardust" persona for this moody, atmospheric synth track, explicitly banning electric guitars from the mix to ensure the album returned to a "safe, marketable" sound before the end.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The city lights are cold tonight
I'm walking under the pale moonlight
I see two people passing by
Reflected in a stranger's eye

(Chorus)
We're just shadow dancing
A pantomime, a game of chance
Trying to make it look like romance
We're just shadow dancing
Afraid to stop, afraid to fall
Just shadows on the wall

(Verse 2)
You say the words I want to hear
You whisper "love" to hide the fear
We're both performing in this play
Hoping the night will turn to day

(Chorus)
We're just shadow dancing
A pantomime, a game of chance
Trying to make it look like romance
We're just shadow dancing
Afraid to stop, afraid to fall
Just shadows on the wall

(Bridge)
(A moody, atmospheric keyboard solo)
Is this real? I'll never know
Just follow where the music goes
Just keep on dancing...

(Chorus)
We're just shadow dancing
A pantomime, a game of chance
Trying to make it look like romance
We're just shadow dancing
Afraid to stop, afraid to fall
Just shadows on the wall

(Outro)
Shadows on the wall...
Shadow dancing...
(fades)

title: After the Show
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Ryan's final laugh. As "punishment" for the heavy rock tracks earlier on Side B, Apex ordered him to close the album with a quiet ballad, explicitly forbidding "pounding drums" on the track sheet. Ryan complied by recording the song using **percussive acoustic guitar**—slapping the body of the instrument to simulate a beat. It was a subtle, rhythmic "middle finger" to the executives who tried to silence the "Engine."

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
The stage is empty, the crowd is gone
Another night, another dawn
We played the part, we sang the song
And now we have to move along

(Verse 2)
The neon heart is turning low
It's just a faded, distant glow
Is this the dream we wanted so?
I guess we'll never know

(Chorus)
We're just echoes in the city
It's not so bad, it's not so pretty
Just echoes, turning to gray
We'll come back and fight another day

(Bridge)
(A soft, melodic acoustic guitar solo, underscored by the rhythmic slapping of the guitar body)
Another day...
Another way...

(Chorus)
Just echoes, turning to gray
We'll come back and fight another day

(Outro)
After the show...
Goodnight...
(fades out on acoustic guitar)

title: The Promise (Corporate Demo)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The exact sound Apex Records wanted: safe, sterile, and perfectly calibrated for a televangelist broadcast. This was the studio's cynical attempt to cash in on the "religious pop" trend. The guitar solo is painfully restrained, engineered specifically not to offend anyone. The entire project was scrapped in a panic by executives after the massive controversy surrounding Cydele's "Worship" video dropped on MTV the very next day.

title: The Stardust Engine (Live in Chicago)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
This track is the "Smoking Gun" that proves Julian Vance (the executive behind the *Friction* disaster) never did his homework. In the intro, Ryan O'Connell—who, like his sister, is autistic and values absolute clarity—explicitly introduces Cassidy as "my sister," publicly disproving the "married couple" assumption years before it destroyed their contract.

Musically, this recording is a source of fury for the band. It was the only concession Apex made—allowing them to play their self-titled anthem as the opener of their strict 30-minute support slot. However, the mix is "sabotaged": Cassidy's iconic "Stardust" synth leitmotif—the musical heart of the song—is buried so deep in the mix it is practically inaudible, leaving only the "Engine" rock elements.

(We are the Engine!)

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light

Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Outro)
Shining so bright...
We're taking flight...
(Spoken) Thank you!

title: Neon Hearts (Live in Chicago)

As the title track of the album they were touring, this was a mandatory inclusion in the setlist. Apex Records insisted the band focus on their "Stardust" synth-pop sound to promote the new record, forcing Ryan to play the "good soldier" and deliver a polished, high-energy performance, even as he chafed against the "safe" creative direction.

**LYRICS:**

title: Dancing in the Neon (Live in Chicago)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Time is money!" With a strict 30-minute opening slot and a tour manager watching the clock, the band had no time for deep cuts. Apex Records demanded they prioritize their high-energy synth-pop hits to win over the headliner's pop-focused audience. You can hear the urgency in the performance—the tempo is slightly faster than the studio version as they race to fit the setlist into their allotted window.

**LYRICS:**

I wanna see you dancing to this one, Chicago!

The city's quiet, the sun is down

title: If You Walked Away (Live in Chicago)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
For Cassidy, who is autistic, the lyrics of this song were not a performance—they were a terrifying "what-if" scenario that she experienced viscerally every time she sang it. While the studio marketed it as a romantic breakup ballad, Cassidy sang it as a desperate plea to her brother. **The fear in her voice on this recording is real.**

Ryan, who is also autistic, understood her need for absolute certainty better than anyone. He famously had to reassure her after *every single concert*—often using the exact same phrase, **"Family sticks together"**—to ground her back in reality and confirm that he was never going to leave her.

**Note: After this specific performance, Cassidy broke down in tears backstage. Ryan had to hold her in a deep pressure hug for twenty minutes to help her reset and remind her that he was right there.**

**LYRICS:**

(Spoken Intro)
Thank you. We're gonna slow things down for you for just a minute...

(Verse 1)
The streetlights make a blurry line
I'm running through the same old signs
I'm just a face in a passing crowd
Afraid to speak my thoughts out loud

(Verse 2)
But then you found me in the noise
You heard a whisper in my voice
You gave me something to believe
A reason I would never leave

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Verse 3)
They build these walls so high and steep
With promises they never keep
But we have a fortress, strong and true
I'm safe as long as I have you

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Bridge)
(A very safe, melodic, clean keyboard solo)
I'm holding on, I'm holding tight
Don't let me go into the night...

(Chorus)
If you walked away
The sky would lose its blue
I wouldn't know what to do
I'd be lost in the gray
If you walked away
My world would fall apart
You're the owner of my (Neon) heart

(Outro)
Don't walk away...
(Spoken) Thank you so much.

The "Big Bet." Apex Records had poured their entire marketing budget into this track, convinced it was the #1 hit that would define the album. Consequently, the band was under immense pressure to deliver a "perfect," high-energy performance of it every night. You can hear the professional polish here—Cassidy hits every note and Ryan plays the "good soldier," executing the catchy hooks exactly as the studio demanded, proving they could play the game even if they hated the rules.

This city sleeps, but we're awake
