I know exactly what you were thinking when you bought these tickets.
A bunch of stubborn Ironheads marching into The Chancellery...
You expected us to come out here bleeding maroon, right?
But tonight, we aren't rivals. We're all just chasing the exact same signal.

[female]
And for the record... your acoustic baffling in this arena is mathematically perfect.
You have a very structurally sound home.

[male]
She's not wrong!
Listen... back on the Neon Hearts tour, we were just an opening act.
We had family friends headlining, and they wanted us to jam with them to close the night.
The label executives said, "Absolutely not."
They kept us in our thirty-minute box.
Well tonight, we call the shots! We don't do traditional opening acts anymore!
If we're closing down The Chancellery, we're doing it with family!
Two drum kits! Two sets of instruments! Everyone on the floor!
We slipped a new song into the middle of our sets this year.
We never announced it. We never said a word about it.
But you've been screaming the lyrics back at us every single night!
Well, I have a confession to make: we didn't write it. We just kept it warm.
Tonight, we brought the architects out here to play it with us!
You didn't have to look far to find them, either.
They built this engine in a garage right here off Route 29!
Charlottesville, meet your hometown heroes... CRIMSON NODE!

[Audience Cheering in the Dark]

(Building tension with two drum kits and soaring lead guitar...)

title: 1996 (An Extension of Me)
content:
# 1996 (An Extension of Me)

**LORE NOTE:**
The song establishes the backstory of Jordan's birth year, 1996, and the origins of his mother's controlling nature. Aubrie Sinclair's worldview was entirely shaped by her one sexual encounter with David Fuller, which she falsely believed would lead to marriage. After he abandoned her, she developed a deep-seated bitterness and resentment toward the world. Consequently, she views her son, Aubrey "Jordan" Fuller, not as an individual, but as her property and a literal extension of herself. This mindset drives her to keep him isolated, treating the outside world as a threat to maintain his dependence on her.

**LYRICS:**

(Intro)
(A cold, pulsing, mechanical beat begins, like a factory machine. A low, dissonant synth drone hums underneath.)

(Verse 1)

That one and only night
He left me in the pieces
He was my only light
But he left a single ember
A part of him for me
A debt he'll pay forever
For all eternity

(Chorus)
(The beat becomes a pounding, rhythmic, industrial crash)
This is my son
An extension of me
My perfect boy
My property
You will never be alone
You will never be free
You are my comfort
An extension of me

(Verse 2)
The world is loud and dirty
It's full of pain and lies
I'll keep you safe forever
Just look in mother's eyes
I'll be your hands and voice
I'll be the air you breathe
You'll never have to make a choice
You'll never have to leave

(Chorus)
(Music swells, adding a grinding, metallic texture)
This is my son
An extension of me
My perfect boy
My property
You will never be alone
You will never be free
You are my comfort
An extension of me

(Bridge)
(The beat drops to a cold, rhythmic pulse)
I'll keep you here
I'll keep you pure
My only love
My only cure
You are mine
You are mine
You are mine

(Chorus)
(The music explodes to its loudest, most oppressive peak)
This is my son
An extension of me
My perfect boy
My property
You will never be alone
You will never be free
You are my comfort
An extension of me

(Outro)
(The beat fades slowly, leaving only the cold, dissonant drone)
(Whispered)
An extension of me...
Just... like... me...

title: The Dependency Loop
content:
# The Dependency Loop

**LORE NOTE:**
This track delves into the specific mechanics of Aubrie Sinclair's control over her son. She deliberately weaponized "care" by refusing to teach Jordan basic life skills, such as how to dress himself or tie his shoes, forcing him to rely entirely on her for survival. By framing the outside world as dangerous and positioning herself as his sole protector and provider, she created a suffocating "cage of comfort." The song also touches upon her medical deception—keeping him unvaccinated and isolated from doctors—ensuring her absolute authority over his physical and mental well-being to guarantee he would never leave her.

(The low drone from the previous track fades in, joined by a slow, heavy, grinding beat, like gears turning. THUD... chk... THUD... chk...)

The air is full of harm
You don't need to lift a finger

Mother's here to do it for you
It's the least that I can do

You don't need to move, you don't need to think
Just stay right here, my love, and drink

title: Inappropriate (The Opt-Out)
content:
# Inappropriate (The Opt-Out)

**LORE NOTE:**
This track explores Aubrie Sinclair's deliberate strategy to keep Jordan ignorant about human anatomy, relationships, and sexuality. By repeatedly opting him out of mandatory school health and family life classes—labeling the curriculum "inappropriate" for him—she weaponized his innocence. Her goal was to ensure he remained isolated, dependent, and entirely under her control, shielding him from any knowledge that might lead to romantic connections, personal autonomy, or an understanding of his own body.

She views his desire for higher education as a "silly college experiment" and deliberately sets him up to fail by selecting Astrophysics—a highly complex and mathematically demanding major—as his degree path. Her intention is not for him to succeed, but to use this "insurmountable mountain" to prove his incompetence, shatter his confidence, and force him to return home, cementing his lifelong dependency on her.

title: Route Four-Sixty (The Seven-Hour Drive)
content:
# Route Four-Sixty (The Seven-Hour Drive)

**LORE NOTE:**
This track captures the tense, seven-hour journey from the humid flatlands of Hampton Roads to the rolling mountains of the New River Valley for college move-in day. Traveling westward along U.S. Route 460, Jordan is trapped in the passenger seat, forced to endure a relentless stream of anxious instructions and oppressive rules from his mother, Aubrie Sinclair. Instead of feeling the excitement of a new beginning, he feels like a prisoner being transported to an academic jail, overwhelmed by panic and the suffocating fear that he is destined to fail her "silly college experiment."

**LYRICS:**

(Intro)
(A fast, pulsing, anxious beat, like a rapid heartbeat. The sound of a car engine idling, distorted and rhythmic. A high, whining synth note, like a ringing in the ears.)

(Verse 1)
Seven hours of silence
Seven hours of her voice
A list of rules and warnings
I didn't have a choice
The mountains rolling past the glass
A world I'll never know
I'm just a passenger, I'm trapped
With nowhere else to go

(Chorus)
(The beat becomes a fast, driving, industrial chug, like a runaway train)
Route four-sixty, rolling west
A knot of panic in my chest
The engine is a pounding drum
From everything I've overcome
...Or everything I'm running to
I don't know what I'm going to do
This silly college experiment
I'll break before I'm bent

(Verse 2)

While the house provides a necessary safe haven from the looming court case and the immediate threat of the PI, it presents a grueling physical challenge for Jordan. title: I-64 (The Gauntlet)

**LORE NOTE:**
This track explores the visceral, geographic nature of trauma. In an attempt to conquer his demons and see the Blue Ridge Parkway at Rockfish Gap, Jordan agrees to a road trip. To Jordan, I-64 is not just a highway; it is a psychological "rootkit virus," intrinsically tied to the route back to his abuser, Aubrie Sinclair, in Hampton Roads. The tension mounts during the agonizing 30-mile stretch starting in Lexington, where I-81 and I-64 merge. Despite his desire to be brave, the moment Mark actually takes Exit 221 to continue onto I-64 East in Staunton, Jordan's system catastrophically crashes. The sheer terror of being on the road heading toward his mother induces a severe meltdown, forcing Mark to immediately abort the mission and bail out at the very next ramp—Exit 91 (SR-285 towards Fishersville)—to break the virus's hold.

title: 99.8 (The Fever)

**LORE NOTE:**
This track highlights the lingering, practical consequences of Aubrie Sinclair's medical and emotional neglect. Jordan wakes up feeling unwell and discovers he has a low-grade temperature of 99.8°F. To a typical young adult, this is a minor inconvenience easily solved with over-the-counter medication. But because his mother deliberately weaponized his dependency by never teaching him basic self-care, health literacy, or how to handle minor illnesses, Jordan spirals into a panic. He views this slight fever as a catastrophic system failure. The "very preventable problem" is simply his lack of knowledge on how to take a Tylenol and drink fluids. The track resolves with his chosen family gently stepping in, not just to care for him, but to teach him the basic medical protocols he was maliciously denied.

title: What If I'm Like Her? (Stork & Cradle)
content:
# What If I'm Like Her? (Stork & Cradle)

**LORE NOTE:**
While enjoying a peaceful day out at the mall with his chosen family, the group walks past "Stork & Cradle," a maternity clothing store. The sight of the pregnant mannequins and baby clothes abruptly shatters Jordan's calm, triggering a deep, existential panic. Having spent his entire life surviving Aubrie Sinclair's calculated cruelty, he is suddenly struck by a terrifying, intrusive thought about the future: what if the capacity for abuse is genetic? He becomes paralyzed by the fear that if he ever becomes a father, he might unwittingly perpetuate the cycle of generational trauma and become the very monster he escaped. The track captures this intense internal spiral, ending with his partners gently grounding him, reminding him that his profound empathy and fear of becoming her are the absolute proof that he never will.

**LYRICS:**

(Intro)
(The bright, echoing sounds of a shopping mall. Laughter. It suddenly distorts and fades away, replaced by a slow, heavy, echoing heartbeat and a moody, anxious electric guitar riff.)

A normal life under a normal sky

A store we were just about to pass

In response, the group gathers around him to formally declare "The Pact of Six." They dismantle his anxiety by explaining that love isn't a transactional equation to be balanced. title: Friday, 9:32 AM (The Attack)
content:
# Friday, 9:32 AM (The Attack)

**LORE NOTE:**
Just as Jordan finally begins to accept the unconditional love of his chosen family, the years of extreme psychological terror, chronic stress, and profound medical neglect inflicted by Aubrie Sinclair culminate in a sudden, catastrophic physical failure. Despite being only nineteen years old, Jordan suffers a critical STEMI (ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction)—a massive, full-blown heart attack. The event strikes out of nowhere on a routine Friday morning at exactly 9:32 AM. Musically, the album violently shifts gears: the bright, triumphant 80s pop-rock is abruptly severed, replaced by a chaotic, racing, irregular tempo that mirrors his failing heart. It is a terrifying reminder that while his mind is finally safe, his body still bears the lethal, physical toll of his abuser's reign. 

**LYRICS:**

(Intro)
(The bright 80s synth from the previous track suddenly cuts out with the harsh sound of a needle scratching a record. A moment of dead silence. Then, a high-pitched, ringing tinnitus tone. A bass drum kicks in—erratic, panicked, and painfully heavy, mimicking an irregular, failing heartbeat.)

(Verse 1)
(Vocals are breathless, strained, and terrified)
It's Friday morning, the sun is bright
We're laughing in the kitchen light
A normal day, a normal plan
I'm standing up... a normal man
But then a shadow hits my chest
A crushing weight, an anvil press
The room is spinning, tilting down
I cannot hear a single sound

(Pre-Chorus)
(The rhythm becomes frantic, anxious)
My left arm goes entirely numb
The air is gone, my throat is dumb
I drop the glass, it hits the floor
I'm falling back against the door
I'm nineteen years old! This cannot be!
What is my body doing to me?!

(Chorus)
(Music is a chaotic, heavy, driving assault)
NINE THIRTY-TWO AM!
The system fails! The final blow!
A critical STEMI taking hold!
A heart attack at nineteen years old!
The stress, the trauma, the years of fear
Have finally come to kill me here!
The damage done, the toll it takes
The moment that the engine breaks!

(Verse 2)
(Vocals are fragmented, drifting in and out of focus)
Aubrie's screaming, she hits the ground
She's holding my head, spinning around
"Call 9-1-1! Call them right now!"
Madi is crying, wiping my brow
The pain is a fire, a searing white
I'm losing my grip, I'm losing the fight
The ghost of my mother, the stress that she built
Is drowning my heart in a river of guilt

(Pre-Chorus)
I'm nineteen years old! I just got free!
Why is this happening to me?!
I finally found a place to belong
And now my heart is beating wrong!

(Chorus)
NINE THIRTY-TWO AM!
The system fails! The final blow!
A critical STEMI taking hold!
A heart attack at nineteen years old!
The stress, the trauma, the years of fear
Have finally come to kill me here!
The damage done, the toll it takes
The moment that the engine breaks!

(Bridge)
(The heavy music drops away. Just the erratic bass drum, fading slowly. The vocals are a weak whisper.)
I don't want to go...
I just got here...
Zoe, I'm scared...
Aubrie, please don't let me go...
It hurts so much...
(A faint sound of sirens in the far distance)

(Guitar Solo - Frantic, screaming, and dissonant, imitating the sirens getting closer)

(Outro)
(The erratic heartbeat drum slows down dangerously)
Nine thirty-two...
System failing...
(Spoken, distant voices)
"Stay with us, Jordan! Stay with us!"
"Ambulance is pulling up!"
"He's crashing!"
(A flatline synthesizer tone holds, then abruptly cuts to silence.)

title: The Longest Night (NPO)
content:
# The Longest Night (NPO)

**LORE NOTE:**
Jordan survives the catastrophic STEMI, but the immediate aftermath introduces him to the grueling, unglamorous reality of inpatient cardiac recovery. This track captures his first night in the hospital. He is placed on strict "NPO" (nil per os / nothing by mouth) status in case he needs emergency surgery, leaving him intensely, frustratingly hungry and thirsty. To compound his misery, the nurses wake him every two hours for mandatory vitals checks, wrapping a cold blood pressure cuff around his arm just as he drifts off. Yet, amidst the sterile environment, the incessant beeping, and the gnawing hunger, there is a profound comfort: Aubrie Kelly refuses to leave his side. Sleeping in a terribly uncomfortable vinyl hospital chair, her presence transforms a night of physical misery into a quiet testament of enduring, unconditional love.

**LYRICS:**

(Intro)
(A slow, steady, rhythmic electronic "beep... beep..." mimicking a stable heart monitor. A soft, melodic acoustic guitar enters, gentle but weary.)

(Verse 1)
(Vocals are tired, raspy, and slightly annoyed)
The blood pressure cuff inflates again
It's two AM, or maybe ten?
The nurse comes in with a flashlight beam
And rips me out of a fever dream
A poke, a prod, a gentle sigh
"Just checking your vitals, the numbers are high."
She leaves the room, the door clicks shut
And my stomach churns in a hungry rut

(Pre-Chorus)
NPO. Nothing by mouth.
My whole digestive tract has gone south.
I would trade my soul for a single chip
For a drop of water upon my lip
I'm starving, I'm tired, the wires are tight
Welcome to the longest night

(Chorus)
(Music swells slightly, adding a warm cello)
This is the longest night I've ever known
A sterile room in a clinical zone
Beeping machines and a flashing light
No sleep to be found in the longest night
But then I look to my left, and the panic clears
Because the best thing in my life is sitting right here

(Verse 2)
In a vinyl chair that was built for pain
Underneath the glow of the window pane
Aubrie is sleeping, her head rests low
She refused to leave, she refused to go
My mother would have left me to suffer alone
Or complained about the time on her cellular phone
But Aubrie's just breathing, holding my hand
The fiercest protector in all of the land

(Pre-Chorus)
NPO. Nothing by mouth.
My whole digestive tract has gone south.
I'm dreaming of a burger and a massive shake
But I'll bear this hunger for both our sakes
I'm starving, I'm tired, the wires are tight
Welcome to the longest night

(Chorus)
This is the longest night I've ever known
A sterile room in a clinical zone
Beeping machines and a flashing light
No sleep to be found in the longest night
But then I look to my left, and the panic clears
Because the best thing in my life is sitting right here

(Bridge)
(Just the acoustic guitar and the steady heart monitor beep)
(Spoken, with a tired chuckle)
Four AM. The cuff squeezes again.
I ask the nurse if I can just have one ice chip.
She says no.
I look at Aubrie. She opens one eye, smiles, and squeezes my hand.
I guess I can wait until morning.

(Guitar Solo - Slow, bluesy, and full of longing, echoing the feeling of an empty stomach and a full heart)

(Chorus)
(Music is full, warm, and acoustic)
This is the longest night I've ever known
A sterile room in a clinical zone
Beeping machines and a flashing light
No sleep to be found in the longest night
But I'm not alone, and the panic clears
Because the best thing in my life is sitting right here

(Outro)
(The acoustic guitar fades slowly)
Just one cracker...
Please...
(The monitor beeps steadily)
I love you, Aubrie.
(Deep breath, fading to silence)

This track captures the physical and psychological "breaking point" where the pain and frustration make him want to quit entirely. However, unlike his isolated past, he is surrounded by the unbreakable wall of his chosen family. Mark acts as his spotter, Hannah brings him water, and the entire Pact of Six anchors him. title: The Accessibility Project
content:
# The Accessibility Project

**LORE NOTE:**
Now firmly in his recovery phase and back to his coursework, Jordan and his chosen family tackle a massive class assignment: mapping CPI's accessibility features. The group realistically acknowledges that they cannot physically fix the campus—they don't have the budget to pour concrete ramps or install new elevators. However, they realize that *information* is just as powerful as infrastructure. They set out to create comprehensive maps detailing every automatic door, hidden ramp, and accessible path across the rugged terrain. A major victory in their research is mapping the "Hillside Pass-Throughs." They document the university's policy allowing disabled non-residents to get their student IDs specially encoded by the Office of Educational Accessibility. This grants 24/7 access to the 1st and 2nd-floor lobbies and the elevator of buildings built on inclines—like Jordan's old dorm, "The Old Lady on the Hill" (Eleanor Bennett Hall)—allowing students to safely bypass steep hills regardless of standard guest hours. Musically, this track is an upbeat, focused, and triumphant "heist" song, turning data collection into a grand adventure.

We won!

Safe.

title: Neon Pulse (Live in Virginia Beach)

Nocturnal highway synth-rock from 2001's *Midnight Drivers* pulsing across the Virginia Beach summer night.

Racing through the streets, glowing like a fire
No looking back, we’re out of the frame
Running on the spark, wild and untamed
Catch the neon pulse tonight

The dashboard is glowing, a steady bright green
The fastest escape that this city has seen

A steady transmission out on the street

Catch the neon pulse, riding on the wire
Racing through the streets, glowing like a fire

title: The Flight Path (Live in Virginia Beach)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**First-Ever Recorded Live Performance of *"The Flight Path"* (Mid-Concert Unannounced Mystery Song, `5:14`).** Slipped unannounced right into the middle of the set (*"We're gonna keep it moving. We've been testing this next one out on the road for the last few weeks. Let's see if you've caught on to the words yet!"*), Ryan and Cassidy test whether the Virginia Beach crowd knows the lyrics from recent tour tape-trading. All 20,000 fans at the CTI Virginia Beach Amphitheater roar the chorus back at the stage, 100% convinced it is a brand-new Stardust Engine song—with no song title or mention of **Crimson Node** given! Released in February 2003 after *Crimson Node* and *Live at the Chancellery*.

**LYRICS:**

[Atmospheric Analog Synth Arpeggio]

Yeah-yeah!

A steady voice above the crowd

The double-tap upon my hand
We never launch without the green light

Leaving the gravity far behind

Following the numbers in the silent code
Shoulder to shoulder, synchronized and true
I'll always share the flight path with you

(Blistering dual guitar and analog synth riff)

The naval clock is ticking in my head

I call the coordinates out loud
A steady voice above the crowd
I hold my hand out, wait for the command
The double-tap upon my hand
We never launch without the green light

We are charting the flight path, perfectly aligned
Leaving the gravity far behind

Sing it out!

[male]
When the system overloads and the signals start to fray
We build a fortress on the ground to keep the storm at bay
A heavy blanket in the dark, the pressure brings you home
You'll never have to navigate the atmosphere alone

We are charting the flight path, perfectly aligned
Leaving the gravity far behind

Following the numbers in the silent code

title: Moon 2 (Roche Limit)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Exploding out of the gate as the opening track for *Mile Marker 98*, this is the spark that ignited Ryan's 2003 solo orbit. Freed from the need to balance the "Stardust" with his "Engine," Ryan takes the astrophysical concept of the Roche limit—the exact point gravity tears a moon to pieces—and uses it to set the destructive, high-friction tone for the entire record. It serves as a violent, visceral thesis statement for his confrontation with the trauma of the "Crash of '90", introducing blistering, distorted electric guitars and pure, aggressive rock energy right from the first second. 

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(An aggressive, pounding 1980s drum fill shatters the ambient space. A heavy, distorted electric guitar riff locks in with a driving analog synth-bass. It is high energy, frantic, and immediately dangerous.)*

[Verse 1]
I see the warning on the console screen
You're pulling harder than I've ever seen
I'm caught inside the gravity well
A one-way ticket on a carousel
The navigation is totally blind
I'm leaving all the safety behind

[Pre-Chorus]
The structural integrity is starting to bend
I'm accelerating faster to the bitter end
You're a massive body, I'm a satellite
I'm breaking into pieces in the dead of night!

[Chorus]
We crossed the Roche Limit!
Tearing me apart, tearing me apart!
We crossed the Roche Limit!
A fatal attraction, a heavy heart!
There's no surviving when you get this close
A total system failure, a lethal dose
Yeah, we crossed the Roche Limit!

[Verse 2]
The telemetry is spinning into the red
I should've listened to the things they said
But the magnetic field is pulling me in
I feel the friction underneath my skin
I'm caught in the orbit of a dangerous star
I didn't mean to take it this far!

[Pre-Chorus]
The structural integrity is starting to bend
I'm accelerating faster to the bitter end
You're a massive body, I'm a satellite
I'm breaking into pieces in the dead of night!

[Chorus]
We crossed the Roche Limit!
Tearing me apart, tearing me apart!
We crossed the Roche Limit!
A fatal attraction, a heavy heart!
There's no surviving when you get this close
A total system failure, a lethal dose
Yeah, we crossed the Roche Limit!

[Guitar Solo]
*(Ryan unleashes a blisteringly fast, aggressive, face-melting electric guitar solo. Explosive drums and heavy synth pads pulse underneath the shredding, simulating a vessel vibrating itself to pieces under extreme gravitational stress.)*

[Chorus]
We crossed the Roche Limit!
Tearing me apart, tearing me apart!
We crossed the Roche Limit!
A fatal attraction, a heavy heart!
There's no surviving when you get this close
A total system failure, a lethal dose
Yeah, we crossed the Roche Limit!

[Outro]
Tearing me apart.
System failure.
*(A final, heavy guitar chord rings out, turning into a wall of amplifier feedback that slowly fades out into the cold, indifferent silence of deep space)*

title: Fragmentation: Debris Field
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
With *Moon 2 (Roche Limit)* acting as the violent prologue, *Fragmentation (Debris Field)* is the moment the planet completely shatters. 

Bringing back the planetarium narrator from the *Sanctuary* album creates a brilliant, unsettling continuity. The calm, clinical voice of the narrator completely juxtaposes the blistering, industrial arena rock that follows. Lyrically and sonically, this track brings the *Mile Marker 98* cover art to life—a heavy, visceral explosion of distorted guitars and pounding drums representing the violent breaking of the terrestrial past. 

**LYRICS:**

[Spoken Intro]
*(Spoken clearly, calmly, and methodically, like a narrator in a planetarium documentary. A low, menacing rumble of amplifier feedback begins to swell in the background.)*
Welcome back to the Engine Room Records Planetarium. 
Having crossed the Roche Limit, the structural integrity of our satellite has officially failed. 
We are now experiencing terminal fragmentation. 
As tidal forces overcome gravitational self-attraction, the celestial body shatters into a high-velocity debris field. 
Please remain seated and brace for immediate impact.

[Intro]
*(The planetarium narration is abruptly cut off by an earth-shattering snare crack. A massive, chugging, drop-tuned electric guitar riff explodes into the stereo field. The drums are heavy, acoustic, and pounding. Pure 1990s industrial arena rock.)*

[Verse 1]
*(Aggressive male rock vocals)*
The ground is cracking right beneath my boots
We're ripping up the foundation, pulling the roots
The sky is falling in a million jagged pieces
The pressure building up and it never releases!
I look up and the moon is ripped in half
Nothing left to do but watch it burn and laugh

[Pre-Chorus]
The gravity is dead, the center cannot hold
The core is spilling out, a story never told
It's raining heavy metal from a shattered sky
Kiss the quiet sanctuary a bitter goodbye!

[Chorus]
Fragmentation! We're blowing it apart!
A million flying pieces of a heavy metal heart
Fragmentation! Welcome to the crash!
Turning all the history to cinders and to ash
We're living in the middle of a debris field
No blast doors, no shelter, no shield!
Fragmentation!

[Verse 2]
I can see the black guitars falling through the space
A violent collision in the human race
The magma is spilling from the broken crust
Turning all the monuments to powder and dust
You wanted a reaction, you wanted a spark?
Well now we're throwing fire right into the dark!

[Pre-Chorus]
The gravity is dead, the center cannot hold
The core is spilling out, a story never told
It's raining heavy metal from a shattered sky
Kiss the quiet sanctuary a bitter goodbye!

[Chorus]
Fragmentation! We're blowing it apart!
A million flying pieces of a heavy metal heart
Fragmentation! Welcome to the crash!
Turning all the history to cinders and to ash
We're living in the middle of a debris field
No blast doors, no shelter, no shield!
Fragmentation!

[Guitar & Drum Bridge]
*(The vocals drop out. The drummer goes absolutely berserk on the toms, building a tribal, industrial rhythm. Ryan layers in a series of screeching, dissonant guitar pick-slides that sound like massive tectonic plates grinding together and snapping.)*

[Guitar Solo]
*(A blistering, aggressive, wah-soaked guitar solo that rips through the heavy rhythm section. It is chaotic, unpolished, and completely visceral—the exact opposite of Cassidy's clean, classical piano arpeggios.)*

[Chorus]
Fragmentation! We're blowing it apart!
A million flying pieces of a heavy metal heart
Fragmentation! Welcome to the crash!
Turning all the history to cinders and to ash
We're living in the middle of a debris field
No blast doors, no shelter, no shield!
Fragmentation!
