[Radio Transmission: Heavy Distorted Static]
*(Muffled, indistinguishable male shouting)*
*(Radio static crackles violently)*

[Clear Female Lead]
The navigation is finally aligned
I left the atmosphere and gravity behind
Floating in the center of the velvet and the black
A million miles away and never looking back
But the console is blinking with a sudden glowing light
A heavy transmission cutting through the night

[Pre-Chorus]
The signal is crossing the great divide
A ghost in the machine from the other side
Two different orbits, two different speeds
But the mathematics give us everything we need

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Sanctuary, welcome to the clear
The zero-G is perfect and there is no friction here
Suspended in the silence, suspended in the deep
A promise that the metal and the memory will keep
We are spinning in the dark, we are flying through the sea
Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Radio Transmission: Fading Distortion]
[Male Rock Vocal]
I hear the heavy static of a broken engine roar
I hear the heavy knocking on the heavy blast door
You are burning up the friction in a fatal asteroid ring
[Clear Female Lead]
While I am in the silence listening to the planets sing
[Male and Female Duet]
But the radio is open and the frequency is shared
A twin moon system perfectly paired

[Pre-Chorus]
The signal is crossing the great divide
A ghost in the machine from the other side
Two different orbits, two different speeds
But the mathematics give us everything we need

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Sanctuary, welcome to the clear
The zero-G is perfect and there is no friction here
Suspended in the silence, suspended in the deep
A promise that the metal and the memory will keep
We are spinning in the dark, we are flying through the sea
Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Symphonic Crescendo]
*(The ultimate realization of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound. The classical piano arpeggios spiral upwards at lightning speed while massive, soaring synth-brass chords widen the stereo field. The massive stadium drums hit with earth-shattering force. A wordless, layered choir of male and female voices soars above the instrumentation.)*

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Sanctuary, welcome to the clear
The zero-G is perfect and there is no friction here
Suspended in the silence, suspended in the deep
A promise that the metal and the memory will keep
We are spinning in the dark, we are flying through the sea
Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Outro]
*(The massive wall of sound suddenly cuts out, leaving only a slow, beautiful, echoing piano line that slowly fades into total silence. A low, humming electronic drone remains.)*

[Spoken Outro]
*(Spoken clearly and calmly by the planetarium documentary narrator)*
This concludes our journey through the Zero-G Sanctuary. 
We have explored the physics of the tidal lock, the crushing isolation of the silent ocean, and the delicate balance of the Goldilocks zone. 
While the vacuum of space is vast and unforgiving, mathematical perfection provides a permanent, weightless refuge. 
Please gather your belongings as the house lights return. 
Thank you for visiting the Engine Room Records Planetarium. 
Safe travels on your return to terrestrial gravity.
*(The electronic drone completely fades out)*

title: Deep Pressure (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Cassidy's deeply personal synth-pop tribute to the grounding power of deep-pressure hugs during autistic sensory overload.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A warm, thick analog bass synthesizer fades in, vibrating with a soothing, low-frequency hum. Slow, heavy, and muffled drum beats establish a heartbeat rhythm. The synths are dense, completely filling the stereo field like a heavy velvet blanket.)*

[Verse 1]
The asteroid field is blindingly bright
A million sharp lasers cutting the night
The alarms on the console are flashing in red
A terrible static is filling my head
The sensory overload is breaching the hull
I'm losing the signal, I'm feeling the pull

[Pre-Chorus]
Close the blast shields, lock the heavy door
I don't want to see the flashing lights anymore
Turn up the gravity, lower the sound
Keep my boots heavy right here on the ground

[Chorus]
Give me that deep pressure, wrapping around
A sanctuary built in the underground
I need the weight, I need the heavy hold
To keep out the static, to keep out the cold
A protective atmosphere, dense and secure
Give me that deep pressure, perfect and pure

[Verse 2]
The vacuum outside is chaotic and loud
A dangerous storm in a nebula cloud
But inside this cabin, the air is so thick
The rhythmic machinery is doing the trick
The frequencies drop to a comforting hum
The panic is over, the sanctuary has come

[Pre-Chorus]
Close the blast shields, lock the heavy door
I don't want to see the flashing lights anymore
Turn up the gravity, lower the sound
Keep my boots heavy right here on the ground

[Chorus]
Give me that deep pressure, wrapping around
A sanctuary built in the underground
I need the weight, I need the heavy hold
To keep out the static, to keep out the cold
A protective atmosphere, dense and secure
Give me that deep pressure, perfect and pure

[Instrumental Safe Space]
*(The vocals drop out. The track leans entirely into the heavy, enveloping bassline and slow, muted drum beat. Shimmering, warm analog synths wash over the track in waves, specifically engineered to sound soothing, rhythmic, and incredibly dense.)*

[Chorus]
Give me that deep pressure, wrapping around
A sanctuary built in the underground
I need the weight, I need the heavy hold
To keep out the static, to keep out the cold
A protective atmosphere, dense and secure
Give me that deep pressure, perfect and pure

[Outro]
Perfect and pure.
Turn up the gravity.
Keep me secure.
*(The heavy, warm bass hum continues, slowing down its vibration until it seamlessly melts into a comfortable, quiet silence)*

title: The Anchor's Hold (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Completes the five-song *Twin Moons Live Suite* as Ryan and Cassidy lock Moon 1 and Moon 2 back into a single orbital system.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A slow, clean chorus-pedal electric guitar picks a melancholic, 1980s ballad progression. A heavy, echoing gated snare drum hits on the two and four, establishing a massive stadium-ballad tempo. The atmosphere is quiet but incredibly heavy.)*

[Verse 1]
*(Emotional, gritty male rock vocals)*
The monitors are humming in the artificial light
I've been staring at the ceiling through a never-ending night
I can't feel the floor beneath me, the gravity is gone
Just a broken piece of metal waiting for the dawn
But I turn my heavy head and look across the room
You're sleeping in the corner, a beacon in the gloom
You didn't take the transport, you didn't fly away
You planted down your boots and swore that you would stay

[Pre-Chorus]
The structural integrity is completely compromised
But I can see the sanctuary reflecting in your eyes
You cross the silent ward and you pull me to your chest
Holding down the armor so the Engine gets to rest!

[Chorus]
You are the Anchor's Hold!
Keeping me from drifting out into the cold
When the orbit was broken, when the vessel was wrecked
You wrapped your arms around the damage to protect!
A gravitational embrace in the middle of the dark
Holding all the pieces, saving the spark
I'm surviving the crash because you wouldn't let me go
You are the Anchor's Hold!

[Verse 2]
They're running the diagnostics, reading out the chart
They can fix the heavy machinery but they cannot fix the heart
I was terrified of floating into the endless black
A ghost inside a machine that is never coming back
But you're standing by the console, your hands upon the glass
Refusing every order to let the moment pass
You pull me in again, tighter than before
We're fighting off the vacuum right here on the floor!

[Pre-Chorus]
The structural integrity is completely compromised
But I can see the sanctuary reflecting in your eyes
You cross the silent ward and you pull me to your chest
Holding down the armor so the Engine gets to rest!

[Chorus]
You are the Anchor's Hold!
Keeping me from drifting out into the cold
When the orbit was broken, when the vessel was wrecked
You wrapped your arms around the damage to protect!
A gravitational embrace in the middle of the dark
Holding all the pieces, saving the spark
I'm surviving the crash because you wouldn't let me go
You are the Anchor's Hold!

[Guitar Solo]
*(The clean guitar drops out, replaced by a massive, soaring, distorted electric guitar solo. It is dripping with emotion, crying and bending notes over the slow, pounding drum beat. It is the peak of 1980s arena rock balladry.)*

[Bridge]
I can't feel my legs.
I can't feel the ground.
But I can feel your arms.
And I am safe and sound!

[Chorus]
You are the Anchor's Hold!
Keeping me from drifting out into the cold
When the orbit was broken, when the vessel was wrecked
You wrapped your arms around the damage to protect!
A gravitational embrace in the middle of the dark
Holding all the pieces, saving the spark
I'm surviving the crash because you wouldn't let me go
You are the Anchor's Hold!

[Outro]
Never let me go.
The gravitational embrace.
Holding me in place.
*(The heavy instrumentation drops away, leaving only the clean chorus guitar picking a final, beautiful chord that slowly fades into the silence of the medical bay)*

title: No Hidden Gravity (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**The Hometown Ghent Highlight.** Performing just blocks from Norfolk's historic Ghent neighborhood where Nate and Maya live, Ryan and Cassidy dedicate this booming power ballad to Ghent's favorite platonic safe-person duo.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
[Atmospheric 1980s Analog Synthesizer, Slow Echoing Piano]
They look at us and try to draw a line
Connecting the dots in their standard design
They expect the push, they expect the fall
But they don't understand this architecture at all

[Verse 1]
[Steady Bassline, Slow Driving Drum Beat]
I'm used to the guessing, the games, and the chase
The hidden agendas invading my space
But you left your armor right there at the door
You don't want a piece of me, you don't ask for more
I told you the boundary, I drew you the map
And you didn't treat it like some kind of trap

[Pre-Chorus]
[Building Tempo, Heavy Guitar Chords]
No blurred lines, no sudden attack!
I can turn around and know you've got my back!

[Chorus]
[Maximum Volume, Massive 80s Arena Rock, Booming Snare]
There's no hidden gravity pulling us down!
No fatal attraction, no spinning around!
We're flying in parallel, steady and true
The safest place in the world is right next to you!
We're breaking the script, we're changing the game
A different kind of fire without the flame!
Yeah, there's no hidden gravity here!

[Verse 2]
[Pulsing Synth, Driving Rhythm]
They say that two people can never just stand
Side by side without holding a hand
But society's ledger is broken and cheap
This is a promise I'm willing to keep
You don't have to perform, you don't have to pretend
I'm not your salvation, I'm just your friend

[Pre-Chorus]
[Building Tempo, Heavy Guitar Chords]
No blurred lines, no sudden attack!
I can turn around and know you've got my back!

[Chorus]
[Maximum Volume, Massive 80s Arena Rock, Booming Snare]
There's no hidden gravity pulling us down!
No fatal attraction, no spinning around!
We're flying in parallel, steady and true
The safest place in the world is right next to you!
We're breaking the script, we're changing the game
A different kind of fire without the flame!
Yeah, there's no hidden gravity here!

[Guitar Solo]
[Soaring, Melodic Electric Guitar Solo, Bright Synth Stabs, Heavy Half-Time Drums]

[Bridge]
[Music Drops Out, Just Piano and Vocals]
You don't need to conquer.
I don't need to hide.
We built a fortress.
With no one inside but us!

[Chorus]
[Explosive Re-entry, Full Band, Layered Vocals]
There's no hidden gravity pulling us down!
No fatal attraction, no spinning around!
We're flying in parallel, steady and true
The safest place in the world is right next to you!
We're breaking the script, we're changing the game
A different kind of fire without the flame!
Yeah, there's no hidden gravity here!

[Outro]
[Music Slowly Fading, Shimmering Synth Pad]
No hidden gravity.
Just the signal coming clear.
I'm right here.
[Final Sustained Piano Chord]
[End]

title: Route 1: Midnight Headlights (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
From 2004's *Progress Street*—celebrating the late-night highway miles and the custom tour coaches parked outside the Norfolk Prism Arena.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Pneumatic air-brake hiss into a pulsing 1980s synthesizer arpeggio)
(Driving palm-muted electric guitar riff and heavy gated-reverb drums kick in at 134 BPM)

[Verse 1]
Amber letters glowing through the valley fog
Rolling past the campus in an autumnlogue
Midnight at the shelter with my collar turned high
Watching silver headlights cut the Virginia sky
Step across the threshold, feel the diesel hum
Counting every mile of the road to come
Out along the corridor on four-sixty west
Put the nocturnal engine to the test!

[Pre-Chorus]
The mist is rising off the mountain ridge
We're flying high across the overpass bridge
Every fifteen minutes like a steady heart
Nothing in the dark can tear this ride apart!

[Chorus]
Roll on, Route One! Through the midnight glow!
Follow the headlights where the dreamers go!
From the campus mall to the edge of the night
We are chasing the horizon in the amber light!
Hold onto the rail while the wheels spin free
Route One is carrying my family and me!

[Verse 2]
Vinyl seats are cold against a tired back
Rhythm of the tires on the asphalt track
Passing by the diners with their neon signs
Reading future stories in the highway lines
We don't need a limousine, we don't need a throne
Long as we are riding down this road we own!

[Pre-Chorus]
The mist is rising off the mountain ridge
We're flying high across the overpass bridge
Every fifteen minutes like a steady heart
Nothing in the dark can tear this ride apart!

[Chorus]
Roll on, Route One! Through the midnight glow!
Follow the headlights where the dreamers go!
From the campus mall to the edge of the night
We are chasing the horizon in the amber light!
Hold onto the rail while the wheels spin free
Route One is carrying my family and me!

[Guitar Solo]
(Blistering, melodic 1980s stadium-rock electric guitar solo with soaring bends and bright synth counter-melodies)

[Bridge]
(Drums strip back to a pounding floor-tom pulse and shimmering synth pad)
Last run of the evening, clear the final bay
Carry all the weight of the world away
Green light flashing at the intersection line
Everything is locked and the night is mine!
(Explosive drum fill back to full speed)

[Chorus]
Roll on, Route One! Through the midnight glow!
Follow the headlights where the dreamers go!
From the campus mall to the edge of the night
We are chasing the horizon in the amber light!
Hold onto the rail while the wheels spin free
Route One is carrying my family and me!

[Outro]
Roll on, Route One!
Midnight headlights in the valley fog!
(Soaring guitar lead over driving drums, ending on a sharp stadium hit)

title: Before the Distance (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The emotional centerpiece of 2004's *Progress Street*, sung as a soaring sibling duet under the Prism dome.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Dramatic synth pad fades in, accompanied by a slow, heavy drum heartbeat)

[Verse 1]
I saw the shadow falling across your face
A quiet surrender in a crowded place
You wore a mask, but the edges were frayed
Lost in the rules of a game that we played
I should have reached out, I should have stood tall
But I let the silence echo down the hall

[Chorus]
When the steel doors close and the platform clears
You can hear the truth grinding in the gears
Heed the warning hiding in his eyes
Before the distance leaves your soul behind
Trust the silence when he calls your name
'Cause once it's gone, nothing stays the same

[Verse 2]
The rain on the window is blurring the lines
Between what is real and what we leave behind
I traded my courage for polite little lies
And watched as the storm gathered dark in your skies
Now I'm riding this track to the end of the day
Wishing to God I had pulled you away

[Chorus]
When the steel doors close and the platform clears
You can hear the truth grinding in the gears
Heed the warning hiding in his eyes
Before the distance leaves your soul behind
Trust the silence when he calls your name
'Cause once it's gone, nothing stays the same

[Bridge]
(Heavy, driving bassline builds with dramatic synthesizers)
Logic is a cage when the danger is real
You can't code the panic, you can't fake what you feel
I'm turning around, I'm breaking the track
Whatever it costs me, I'm taking it back!

[Guitar Solo]
(Soaring, emotional 80s arena-rock guitar solo)

[Chorus]
When the steel doors close and the platform clears
You can hear the truth grinding in the gears
Heed the warning hiding in his eyes
Before the distance leaves your soul behind
Trust the silence when he calls your name
'Cause once it's gone... nothing stays the same

[Outro]
Nothing stays the same.
Listen to the silence.
(Fading synth pad, slow drum beat out)

title: Fifth Gear: The Architect's Shield (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Cassidy's tribute to younger sister and CEO Holly O'Connell—who is watching from the side of the Norfolk stage, already preparing to shut down touring operations so her exhausted siblings can rest.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Punchy, driving 1980s sequenced synthesizer bassline and crisp gated-reverb drums)
(Bright electric guitar and keyboard hook lock in at 136 BPM)

[Verse 1]
Sixteen years old with a briefcase in her hand
Walking through the campus with a blueprint for the band
She never played a chord up underneath the spotlight beam
But she was the architect who guarded every dream
When the suits in the boardroom tried to change the rules
She read every line of print and schooled the corporate fools!

[Pre-Chorus]
Four musicians on the stage, giving all we've got
And the fifth member standing guard to lock the fortress plot!

[Chorus]
She's our fifth gear! Driving through the night!
Keeping all the wheels on the road and holding tight!
When the industry winds are blowing cold and hard
She's the iron shield standing in the front yard!
You never see her shadow in the spotlight's glare
But the engine only runs because our sister's there!

[Verse 2]
When the highway turned to ice and the world came crashing down
She held the clipboard steady in a cold hospital town
Law books in the van while we were rolling down the state
Building up a castle with an unbreakable gate
When we argued over melodies and couldn't see the light
She pulled us in a three-way hug and made the chaos right!

[Pre-Chorus]
Four musicians on the stage, giving all we've got
And the fifth member standing guard to lock the fortress plot!

[Chorus]
She's our fifth gear! Driving through the night!
Keeping all the wheels on the road and holding tight!
When the industry winds are blowing cold and hard
She's the iron shield standing in the front yard!
You never see her shadow in the spotlight's glare
But the engine only runs because our sister's there!

[Guitar Solo]
(Sharp, melodic 1980s AOR electric guitar solo trading rapid phrases with a bright analog synth lead)

[Bridge]
(Music drops to pulsing bass and shimmering keyboard chords)
Every contract sealed inside the family name
She turned a rigged casino into our own game
Not a note on the record, but she wrote the score
Keeping all the wolves away from our studio door!
(Drum fill builds to final chorus)

[Chorus]
She's our fifth gear! Driving through the night!
Keeping all the wheels on the road and holding tight!
When the industry winds are blowing cold and hard
She's the iron shield standing in the front yard!
You never see her shadow in the spotlight's glare
But the engine only runs because our sister's there!

[Outro]
She's our fifth gear!
The architect behind the sound!
(Punchy final synth-rock stabs and drum crash)

title: Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Before the final encore, Ryan and Cassidy sing their bittersweet farewell to the road—promising Forger Nation that while they are turning the lights out after four studio albums in four years to recharge, they *will* return one day.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Gentle, cinematic grand piano chords layered with a warm 1980s analog synthesizer pad)
(A melodic, crying electric guitar lead plays a nostalgic theme)

[Verse 1]
[male]
The final spotlight fades across the empty arena floor
The road cases are latched and rolled outside the stage door
[female]
For twenty years we gave the world the thunder in our chest
Now the highway's calling us to finally take our rest
[male]
Our custom low-floor shuttle bus is kneeling at the curb
[female]
Leading to a quiet place the static can't disturb.

[Pre-Chorus]
[male]
Aluminum ramp unfolds beneath the amber sign
[female]
Five of us together at the end of the line!

[Chorus]
(Massive 80s gated-reverb drums and soaring stadium guitars swell in)
We're taking the last bus home! Back to Progress Street!
Turning off the amplifiers and the stadium heat!
Lock the front door tight and let the curtains fall
We don't owe the outside world anything at all!
Through every storm we weathered and every song we played
This family is the greatest music that we ever made!

[Verse 2]
[female]
Unplug the synthesizers, set the guitars in their stands
[male]
Rest the tired voices and the callused, aching hands
[female]
Five pairs of sneakers lined up by the wooden stairs
[male]
Trading all the crowded rooms for quiet living room chairs
[female]
We're not fading into nothing, we're just tuning out the noise
[male]
Back to three sisters and brothers and the twin Wright boys!

[Chorus]
We're taking the last bus home! Back to Progress Street!
Turning off the amplifiers and the stadium heat!
Lock the front door tight and let the curtains fall
We don't owe the outside world anything at all!
Through every storm we weathered and every song we played
This family is the greatest music that we ever made!

[Bridge]
(Music softens to warm piano and glowing synth strings)
[female]
Someday when we're ready, we'll turn the switches on
[male]
And find out that the fire in the engine's never gone
[female]
But tonight the porch light's turning off in Blacksburg town
[male]
As we lay the heavy burden of the road right down!

[Guitar Solo]
(Epic, extended, deeply emotional 1980s stadium-rock guitar solo soaring over grand piano chords, lush analog synth pads, and massive slow gated-reverb drums)

[Final Chorus]
We're taking the last bus home! Back to Progress Street!
Turning off the amplifiers and the stadium heat!
Lock the front door tight and let the curtains fall
We don't owe the outside world anything at all!
Through every storm we weathered and every song we played
This family is the greatest music that we ever made!

[Outro]
(Drums and guitars slowly fade out, leaving only the upright piano and a gentle acoustic guitar chord)
[female]
Lights out on Progress Street...
[male]
Goodnight, Forger Nation.
(A warm, sustained piano and analog synth chord slowly fades into silence)

title: Electric Color (Live in Norfolk)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The mandatory closer—one final, cathartic explosion of color inside the Norfolk Prism Arena before the band heads home to Blacksburg for their 2005–2014 Burnout Hiatus. Unlike the 2016 *Live at the Crucible* AOR/Marching Band reclamation, this 2004 Norfolk tour finale preserves the classic high-energy 1980s Synth-Pop / Dance-Rock arrangement of *Electric Color*, supercharged with Ryan's live arena shred guitar solo. *(Note: By sacred band vow, 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible' and 'If You Walked Away' are strictly excluded).*

**LYRICS:**

[Live Arena Crowd Roar]

[Extended Instrumental Vamp]
(A massive, pulsing 1980s analog synthesizer pad and driving gated-reverb drum groove build tension across the arena floor as funky rhythm guitar scratches lock in)

[Spoken Word Intro]
(Spoken, female vocals, energetic and breathless over the vamp and cheering crowd)
We have been all over the world on this tour, Norfolk!
And there is no better place to finish this journey than right here on Virginia soil!
Before we pack up the buses and head home to Blacksburg... we've got one last song left in the tank!
Tonight, we're gonna turn the Prism into a dance floor one last time! Let me see you move, Norfolk!

[Instrumental Hook]
(The main sharp, catchy 1980s synthesizer hook and funky dance-rock beat slam in at full power)

[Verse 1]
Woke up this morning, the world was gray
Didn't know the colors had all faded away
Been living in a room with the curtains drawn tight
Then you flipped a switch and turned on the light

[Chorus]
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

[Verse 2]
(Funky rhythm guitar scratches enter, synthesizer swells, bassline gets busier)
The city sounds were just a buzz in my ear
A static station I could never quite hear
But now the noise is turning into a song
And I finally feel like I belong

[Chorus]
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

[Bridge]
The beat is getting stronger
I can't hide it any longer
My heart is playing catch-up
To the music turning way up!
(Spoken, shouting to the crowd)
Ryan, show them what you got!

[Guitar Solo]
(A blistering, high-gain rock guitar solo cuts through the synth-pop beat, melodic and fast)

[Chorus]
(High energy, drums crashing, crowd singing along)
Oh, I'm seeing in electric color
Finding a rhythm I never knew
Dancing in a brand new summer
My whole world feels bright and new
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all started with you!

[Outro]
(The synth hook returns over roaring arena crowd)
Electric color!
Feeling so new!
It's all because of you!
(Spoken)
Thank you Norfolk! We love you! Goodnight!
(Music ends on a clean synth hit and roaring arena applause)

title: Overture of the Frost
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

The symphonic-metal overture opening Tales from the Solstice. Commissioned in January 2007 at The Crown & Hound on Duke of Gloucester Street in Williamsburg after Samantha liberated the Rowlands family's masters from Vanguard Horizon, ethereal soprano vocals, Gwendolyn's cello, and Gabriel's neoclassical electric guitar set the stage for a 3-disc rock opera uniting Julian Rowlands' 1996 rescue beacon with Matthew's cross-country survival.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro]
[Symphonic Strings]

[Heavy Cello Build]
[Rock Drum Beat]

[Distorted Guitar Entrance]
[Epic Orchestral Drop]

[Choir]
Ahhh, Ohhh
Ahhh, Ohhh

[Massive Symphonic Rock Climax]
[Heavy Rhythm Section]

[Sudden Stop]
[Lonely Piano Outro]
[Fade to Silence]

title: The False Horizon
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

A dramatic symphonic rock duet chronicling the moment Matthew is lured past his HRT transfer point near the hospital glass onto a cross-country interstate coach at Olney and Granby in Norfolk, Virginia—echoing the terror Julian Rowlands survived a decade earlier.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
Rolling south down Hampton line
Tracing the grid inside the mind
The hospital glass is coming near
The transfer point is almost here
The air brakes hiss, the yellow cord is pulled
Following the rules, just like we were told

[Pre-Chorus]
A sudden hand upon the arm
A sweet smile to disarm the alarm
We're staying on, skipping the door
There's a little something more

[Chorus]
Look at the false horizon!
A detour in the master plan!
The curfew clock begins to fade
Just trying to play the easy hand
Ignore the warnings in the chest
For a spontaneous request
Swallow the panic, take the lead
Into the emerald greed!

[Verse 2]
Olney and Granby, stepping in the cold
This isn't the story we were told
A concrete fortress standing tall
The diesel fumes, the echoing hall
Wayfarer silver, Pathfinder blue
What exactly are we going to do?

[Bridge]
Two tickets out! Next bus to ride!
Richmond is waiting on the other side!
The borders break, the tether tears!
The armor's left upon the stairs!

[Outro]
A sudden twist, an outstretched hand
Walking blind into the sand
A quiet nod, the closing eyes
The heavy gate locks on the prize!
(The trap locks shut!)
(The trap locks shut!)

[Sudden Heavy Orchestral Hit]
[End]

title: Emerald City (The Trigger)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

Three thousand miles from Virginia in the rain-streaked neon of Seattle, the promised 'Emerald City' reveals itself as a locked concrete cage—crystallizing Matthew's plea ('I just want to go home') before Jyn defies her blood cousin to become his physical shield and bring him back to Virginia.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
Looking through the rain-streaked glass
Waiting for the gray to pass

title: Upon This Winter's Night
content:
**LORE NOTE:**

The English (United States) studio master of the legendary beacon track ('Sonic Armor'). Originally recorded in one take on December 11, 1996 in Ewell, Virginia—anchored by Maria Harrison's glockenspiel, Gabriel Rowlands' baritone and guitar, Gwendolyn Rowlands' arrangements, and Julian's wind-up Brahms 'Wiegenlied' music box—and hijacked onto the Shenandoah FM repeaters to reach 14-year-old Julian during his abduction to Ohio. Years later, this 1997 single became the sonic armor that grounded Matthew at the airport hub during his rescue flight home from Seattle.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Heavy, driving cello riff)
(Orchestral strings swell)
(Rock drums kick in—slow, heavy beat)

[Verse 1]
The clock upon the mantel chimes
Reminding me of better times
The window pane is frosted white
I'm searching for a sign tonight
I know the storm is raging on
I know the daylight’s dead and gone
But in this house, the fire burns
Until the traveler returns

[Pre-Chorus]
(Strings build tension)
Can you hear me calling?
Can you see the glow?
Through the miles of silence
And the drifting snow?

[Chorus]
So keep a candle burning bright
Upon this winter's night
Though you've wandered far and wide
Time remains upon your side
Follow the star, follow the light
And make it home tonight
(Make it home tonight!)

[Instrumental Break]
(Dramatic Cello Solo)

[Verse 2]
The world is cold and full of fear
But sanctuary waits in here
Don't let the shadows steal your way
Don't listen to the words they say
The journey’s hard, the road is steep
But promises are yours to keep
So lift your head and face the wind
And let the journey home begin

[Chorus]
So keep a candle burning bright
Upon this winter's night
Though you've wandered far and wide
Time remains upon your side
Follow the star, follow the light
And make it home tonight

[Bridge]
(Tempo speeds up - Rock Opera style)
(Male Lead) I’m sending out a prayer!
(Choir) (Bring him home! Bring him home!)
(Male Lead) To vanish all despair!
(Choir) (You are not alone!)
(Male Lead) No matter where you are
No matter how far!
Just look to the Northern Star!

[Guitar Solo]
(Soaring, melodic electric guitar solo with orchestral backing)

[Chorus]
So keep a candle burning bright
Upon this winter's night
Though you've wandered far and wide
Time remains upon your side
Follow the star, follow the light
And make it home tonight

[Outro]
Make it home tonight...
(Follow the light...)
Make it home tonight...
(Upon this winter's night...)

[Big Finish]
(Orchestral hit)
(Sustain cello note fading out)

title: Upon This Winter's Night (The Family Mix - Trilingual Edition)
content:

The sacred 5-minute Trilingual "Family Mix" (*Upon This Winter's Night / Ar Noson y Gaeaf Hon / En Cette Nuit d'Hiver*), performed across **English (United States)**, **French (Québécois)**, and **Cymraeg (Welsh)**. Upon this winter's night
Though you've wandered far and wide
Time remains upon your side

And make it home tonight

The journey’s hard, the road is steep

And let the journey home begin

[Chorus - Cymraeg]
(Sung entirely in Cymraeg to honor the mother's roots)
Felly cadwch gannwyll yn llosgi'n llachar [So keep a candle burning bright]

title: The Stardust Engine (The Rejected Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
This alternate version of "The Stardust Engine" was one of the original demos shopped around to record companies when the band formed in 1986. Apex Records signed them but rejected this version, burying the final studio version as track 13 on 1987's *Electric Color*. The band famously despises Apex for what happened to them during the 1992 label dispute. For this vault release, they officially retitled this early cut "(The Rejected Mix)" instead of naming Apex Records directly, serving as a quiet nod to their lingering resentment.

**LYRICS:**

(Verse 1)
We were looking for a signal
A light in the endless black
A single voice in the universe
To tell us we're on the right track

(Verse 2)
We found the fire in the wires
We found the heart in the machine
Building a dream from nothing
A sound the world has never seen

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Verse 3)
They tried to ground us, keep us small
Tell us that we were gonna fall
But they don't know the things we know
They haven't seen the places we'll go

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Guitar Solo)
(A soaring, melodic solo that trades licks with a bright synthesizer hook)

(Bridge)
We are the cosmos, we are the fire
We're taking this one, higher and higher
We are the Stardust!
(We are the Engine!)
We are the Stardust Engine!

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Outro)
Shining so bright...
We're taking flight...
(fades out on an epic, sustained guitar chord)

title: Midnight Drivers (Basement Demo)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
This is an early, raw basement recording of what would eventually become the title track of their 2001 retro-engineered album. Recorded in 1987 before the track was polished in the studio (which Apex Records ultimately deemed too dark and shelved), this gritty demo captures the isolating, moody energy the band originally envisioned before the label interference.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(Instrumental - A deep, pulsing synthesizer bassline cuts through the silence, anchored by a sparse, echoing drum machine that mimics the hypnotic rhythm of windshield wipers.)*

[Verse 1]
Headlights cut across the rain
Wipers keep the beat on the window pane
Static on the radio, fading in and out
We're just shadows in the dashboard lights

[Chorus]
Driving in the dark, running on neon fumes
Leaving all the ghosts in their empty rooms
This city's just a map of glowing, faded lines
But I'm safe right here, between your eyes and mine
Midnight drivers, in the fading light

[Verse 2]
The skyline's a promise, cold and blue
I don't know this road, but I'm with you
The analog display is a steady green glow
Got no destination, just a place to go

[Chorus]
Driving in the dark, running on neon fumes
Leaving all the ghosts in their empty rooms
This city's just a map of glowing, faded lines
But I'm safe right here, between your eyes and mine
Midnight drivers, in the fading light

[Bridge]
*(The beat drops out, leaving only an ethereal, sweeping synth pad. The vocals become intimate and quiet.)*
Don't have to talk
Don't have to say a thing
The engine hums a rhythm
The future's what we bring

[Synth Solo]
*(Instrumental - Cassidy delivers a moody, atmospheric synthesizer solo that weaves through the heavy reverb of the drum track.)*

[Chorus]
Driving in the dark, running on neon fumes
Leaving all the ghosts in their empty rooms
This city's just a map of glowing, faded lines
But I'm safe right here, between your eyes and mine
Midnight drivers, in the fading light

[Outro]
*(Instrumental fade-out with a heavy, distinct echo on the snare drum, trailing off into the dark)*

title: Radio Silence
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A 1986 deep cut demo that Apex Records threw out during the *Electric Color* selection process because it was deemed "too heavy on the synths and too light on the pop". It remained a fan-favorite myth among diehards who traded bootleg cassette tapes, finally getting an official release on this vault compilation.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
Transmission sent, but no reply
Just the static falling from the sky
I've got the dials turned up to ten
Waiting for the world to start again

[Chorus]
It's just radio silence
Nothing on the airwaves tonight
Radio silence
Waiting for a spark to ignite
I'm calling out into the dark
Just trying to make a mark
In the radio silence

[Verse 2]
The frequency is cold and dead
Just the ringing echoing in my head
We built this tower to the stars
But nobody knows who we are

[Chorus]
It's just radio silence
Nothing on the airwaves tonight
Radio silence
Waiting for a spark to ignite
I'm calling out into the dark
Just trying to make a mark
In the radio silence

Can anybody hear me?
Can anybody see the light?
I'm broadcasting on the edge of the night!

[Guitar Solo]
(A melodic, delayed guitar solo that cuts sharply against the synth backing)

[Chorus]
It's just radio silence
Nothing on the airwaves tonight
Radio silence
Waiting for a spark to ignite

Just trying to make a mark
In the radio silence

[Outro]
Just static...
Just silence...
(Fades out with the sound of a radio dial turning through dead stations)

title: Empty Arenas (Early Demo)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Recorded in late 1990 shortly after Ryan's life-altering bus accident, this solemn, stripped-down acoustic demo (`Empty Arenas (Early Demo)`) reflects the band's raw fear that they would never be able to play live again. Deemed too bleak for the *Friction* sessions, the tape remained locked in the vault until *Lost Sounds* (2007)—though fourteen years after cutting this sketch, the band resurrected the song during the 2004 *Progress Street* sessions and transformed it into a thunderous, full-band 1980s Album-Oriented Rock (AOR) stadium anthem with polished lyrics and a full drum kit.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
The spotlight's dead, the cables coiled
The magic trick has been completely spoiled
Just an echo bouncing off the concrete floor
No one's knocking at the backstage door

[Chorus]
Empty arenas, where the echoes go to die
Empty arenas, beneath a painted sky
We used to set this room on fire
Now we're just preaching to the wire
In these empty arenas

[Verse 2]
The ticket stubs are swept away
Just ghosts remembering yesterday
I look out at the velvet seats
And listen to my own heartbeat

[Chorus]
Empty arenas, where the echoes go to die
Empty arenas, beneath a painted sky
We used to set this room on fire
Now we're just preaching to the wire
In these empty arenas

[Bridge]
(A slow, mournful acoustic guitar progression)
Will the lights ever come back on?
Or is the final encore already gone?
If I scream into the vast unknown
Will I realize I'm all alone?

[Guitar Solo]
(A slow, bluesy, emotionally charged acoustic solo)

[Chorus]
Empty arenas, where the echoes go to die
Empty arenas, beneath a painted sky
We used to set this room on fire
Now we're just preaching to the wire
In these empty arenas

[Outro]
Just preaching to the wire...
Empty...
(Fades out with the ambient reverb of a large, empty hall)

title: The Contract
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The legendary 1992 punk-rock vent track. Recorded entirely in secret during their bitter legal dispute with Apex Records, the band absolutely shreds their former label for their suffocating creative control. The sheer anger in Ryan's guitar work makes this a standout deep cut. It was never intended for public release, serving strictly as a therapeutic middle finger to the studio executives.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Fast, aggressive, distorted punk-rock power chords)

[Verse 1]
Sign on the dotted line, sell your soul for a dime
Smile for the camera, pretend that you're doing fine
They dress you up, they pull the strings
They clip your feathers and they sell your wings!

[Chorus]
Tear up the contract!
Burn it to the ground!
We're taking back the music!
We're taking back the sound!
You can keep the money, you can keep the fame
But you're never gonna own our name!
Tear up the contract!

[Verse 2]
Read the fine print, the devil's in the ink
They tell you what to wear, they tell you what to think
A manufactured dream on an assembly line
Well you can take your plastic crown, the kingdom is mine!

[Chorus]
Tear up the contract!
Burn it to the ground!
We're taking back the music!
We're taking back the sound!
You can keep the money, you can keep the fame
But you're never gonna own our name!
Tear up the contract!

[Bridge]
(Driving, angry bassline with feedback swells)
We are not your property!
We are not your toys!
We're bringing back the static!
We're bringing back the noise!
(Scream) NOISE!

[Guitar Solo]
(A frantic, blistering punk guitar solo, heavily distorted and fast)

[Chorus]
Tear up the contract!
Burn it to the ground!
We're taking back the music!
We're taking back the sound!
You can keep the money, you can keep the fame
But you're never gonna own our name!
Tear up the contract!

[Outro]
Tear it up!
Burn it down!
We are out of here!
(Song ends abruptly on a final, crashing chord and the sound of paper ripping)

title: Neon Hearts (Acoustic Sketch)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
This is the raw, acoustic sketch of what would become their heavily manufactured 1989 hit, "Neon Hearts." Without the glossy, heavy studio synths imposed by Apex Records, this early draft reveals the song to be a surprisingly tender, intimate ballad rather than a club-ready pop anthem.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
The city's humming, the lights are low
I'm waiting for you, I'm ready to go
The rain is tapping on the glass
I knew this feeling was built to last

[Pre-Chorus]
I hear your footsteps in the hall
I'm not afraid to fall
This is the only thing I know is true

[Chorus]
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

[Verse 2]
We're walking fast on the wet concrete
The rhythm matches when our eyes meet
Don't need a promise, don't need a vow
My only moment is right here, right now

[Pre-Chorus]
I hear your footsteps in the hall
I'm not afraid to fall
This is the only thing I know is true

[Chorus]
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

[Bridge]
(A soft, melodic acoustic guitar solo)
Let the city sleep, we're wide awake
A chance that we're both gonna take!

[Chorus]
You've got my neon heart
Shining for you in the dark
A love so bright, it's off the charts
You've got my neon heart
It's an electric-colored feeling
And it all starts with you

[Outro]
My neon heart... (Shining for you)
My neon heart...
(fades out on a gentle acoustic strum)

title: Sanctuary: Zero G (Rough Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
An early demo outtake of the massive closer from the 2003 *Sanctuary: Zero-G* album. Before it was expanded into a 74-minute symphonic journey with a spoken-word planetarium outro, it existed as this raw, atmospheric space-rock demo. It showcases the core duet between Ryan and Cassidy and the foundation of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound® before the studio gloss and orchestral layers were applied.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A single, echoing piano chord strikes, followed by a slow, ethereal synthesizer pad and a deliberate 4/4 drum march)

[Clear Female Lead]
The navigation is finally aligned
I left the atmosphere and gravity behind
Floating in the center of the velvet and the black
A million miles away and never looking back
But the console is blinking with a sudden glowing light
A heavy transmission cutting through the night

[Pre-Chorus]
The signal is crossing the great divide
A ghost in the machine from the other side
Two different orbits, two different speeds
But the mathematics give us everything we need

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Sanctuary, welcome to the clear
The zero-G is perfect and there is no friction here
Suspended in the silence, suspended in the deep
A promise that the metal and the memory will keep
We are spinning in the dark, we are flying through the sea
Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Male Rock Vocal]
I hear the heavy static of a broken engine roar
I hear the heavy knocking on the heavy blast door
You are burning up the friction in a fatal asteroid ring
[Clear Female Lead]
While I am in the silence listening to the planets sing
[Male and Female Duet]
But the radio is open and the frequency is shared
A twin moon system perfectly paired

[Pre-Chorus]
The signal is crossing the great divide
A ghost in the machine from the other side
Two different orbits, two different speeds

A promise that the metal and the memory will keep

Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Guitar and Synth Duel]
(A soaring, ambient solo where the rock guitar and synth blend seamlessly, before building back up)

[Chorus]
Welcome to the Sanctuary, welcome to the clear
The zero-G is perfect and there is no friction here
Suspended in the silence, suspended in the deep
A promise that the metal and the memory will keep
We are spinning in the dark, we are flying through the sea
Floating forever in the Sanctuary!

[Outro]
(The track slowly fades into total silence with a beautiful, echoing piano line and deep space ambiance)

title: Steel and Synthetics
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Originally written during the 1997 *Hard Reset* sessions. It serves as a love letter to the band's dual identities—the "Steel" of rock and the "Synthetics" of electronic music. It was cut simply due to runtime constraints on the double album, but remains a fan favorite.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A driving, heavy drumbeat accompanied by a thick, analog synth bass and a distorted rhythm guitar)

[Verse 1]
They said we had to choose a side
The organic truth or the electric ride
They wanted us to draw the line
Between the circuit board and the grand design

[Chorus]
But we are made of steel and synthetics!
Flesh and bone and pure kinetics!
A heavy riff and a digital beat
The cold machine and the human heat!
Steel and synthetics!

[Verse 2]
The strings are bleeding, the motherboard's fried
There's no place left for us to hide
We take the rust and we make it shine
We take the code and we make it divine

[Chorus]
'Cause we are made of steel and synthetics!
Flesh and bone and pure kinetics!
A heavy riff and a digital beat
The cold machine and the human heat!
Steel and synthetics!

[Bridge]
(A staccato, syncopated rhythm section)
Upload the soul!
Plug in the heart!
This is where the science and the magic start!

[Guitar and Synth Duel]
(An epic, blazing solo section where a heavy metal guitar solo trades frantic licks with a rapid-fire synthesizer arpeggio)

[Chorus]
We are made of steel and synthetics!
Flesh and bone and pure kinetics!
A heavy riff and a digital beat
The cold machine and the human heat!
Steel and synthetics!

[Outro]
Steel!
Synthetics!
Human heat!
(The track ends on a massive, combined guitar and synth power chord that rings out for ten seconds before a digital power-down sound cuts it off)

title: Our Own Frequency
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A brand new track recorded specifically for the 2007 *Lost Sounds* compilation, intentionally designed to simulate the stripped-down, acoustic music Ryan and Cassidy were making together back in 1985 (before their cousins Evan and Tyler joined to form The Stardust Engine). After digging through years of painful, heavily-manufactured Apex Records history, they wanted to close the album by returning to their roots. Written and recorded in a single afternoon with just an acoustic guitar and a piano, "Our Own Frequency" is a triumphant, intimate declaration of their bond as brother and sister. It is the exact kind of acoustic scratch track they always wanted to make, completely free of label interference.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A warm, inviting acoustic guitar and piano duet intro)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
They want to paint us in neon light
They want to tell us how to burn tonight
But you and me, we know the truth
They can't buy what we built in our youth

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
Turn off the synths, unplug the drum
Look at the monsters that we have become
Let's strip it down to the wood and wire
And build ourselves a signal fire

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Verse 3]
(Cassidy)
They tried to sell a manufactured dream
A perfect picture on a glowing screen
(Ryan)
But all I need is sitting right here
The melody is finally clear

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Bridge]
(A soaring, deeply emotional piano and acoustic guitar instrumental duet)
(Cassidy)
No heavy gloss...
(Ryan)
No studio boss...
(Duet)
Just the music we wanted to make!

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Outro]
(Ryan)
Our own frequency...
(Cassidy)
Just you and me...
(Fades out with a lingering piano chord and a soft acoustic strum)

Ryan and Cassidy realized that stripping away the noise and returning to the raw, unfiltered "wood and wire" sound of their youth was the only way forward. They promoted this track to be the opener and title track of their 2008 album, *Our Own Frequency*, setting the intimate, deeply personal tone for the rest of the record.

On our own frequency

[Outro]
(Ryan)
Our own frequency...
(Cassidy)
Just you and me...
(Fades out with a lingering piano chord and a soft acoustic strum)

title: The Noise Outside
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Written as a direct response to the overwhelming press cycle and industry expectations that caused their 2008 burnout hiatus. "The Noise Outside" explores Ryan and Cassidy physically and metaphorically locking the studio doors to shut out the world. Driven by a warm acoustic guitar and an atmospheric synth pad, the track emphasizes their need to find a quiet space away from the friction of the industry.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Warm acoustic guitar intro, slow and deliberate)
(A soft, ambient synth pad hums beneath the strings)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Hear that rumble bleeding through the door?
Another heavy footstep on the floor
The press is waiting, cameras in the hall
Waiting for the moment that we fall

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Let them knock, let them wait out in the cold
I’m so tired of doing what we're told
In this room, the walls are thick and deep
We can finally let the monsters sleep

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Close the blinds and lock the heavy gate
Let the noise outside just dissipate
When the world gets loud and demands a show
We find a quiet place they'll never know
Just the strum of the strings and the hum of the light
Keeping the noise outside tonight

[Interlude]
(Acoustic guitar and ambient synth interlude)

[Verse 3]
(Cassidy)
They want the friction, they want the blazing fire
They want to see us burning on the wire

[Verse 4]
(Ryan)
But I can breathe when you are sitting near
You're the only truth I want to hear

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Close the blinds and lock the heavy gate
Let the noise outside just dissipate
When the world gets loud and demands a show
We find a quiet place they'll never know
Just the strum of the strings and the hum of the light
Keeping the noise outside tonight

[Outro]
(Ryan)
Let the noise outside...
(Cassidy)
Just fade away.
(Ending on a soft, lingering synth chord)

title: Safe Person
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The emotional core of the album. "Safe Person" strips away the protective rock-star armor to reveal the vulnerability underneath. Ryan, seated at his acoustic guitar, sings to Cassidy about being her anchor when the stadium lights and screaming crowds become too much to bear. Returning to the pure acoustic guitar and piano arrangement, this track cements their unbreakable sibling bond.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Gentle, solitary piano intro)
(Acoustic guitar softly joins the piano)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
The cameras flash, the questions start to blur
I smile and nod, playing the character
But underneath the makeup and the lights
I'm terrifyingly alone on these high wire nights
Until I catch your eye across the room
And suddenly I'm safe inside this tomb

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
You never have to wear the mask for me
I know exactly who you want to be
When the oxygen gets thin up on the stage
I'll be the one to open up the cage
Just breathe and let the heavy armor fall
I've got you when your back is to the wall

[Chorus]
(Duet)
You're my safe person, the calm inside the storm
The only place I know where I am warm
We tear down all the idols and the lies
And find the truth inside each other's eyes
No electric amps, no flashing lights
Just you and me surviving all the nights

[Interlude]
(Soft acoustic guitar interlude)

[Verse 3]
(Cassidy)
You're the only one who sees me clear
When everything I am begins to disappear

[Verse 4]
(Ryan)
And you're the melody I've always known
I'll never let you face the dark alone

[Chorus]
(Duet)
You're my safe person, the calm inside the storm
The only place I know where I am warm
We tear down all the idols and the lies
And find the truth inside each other's eyes
No electric amps, no flashing lights
Just you and me surviving all the nights

[Outro]
(Cassidy)
You're my safe person...
(Ryan)
Always.

title: Unplugged
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A literal and metaphorical deconstruction of the band's massive arena-rock sound. "Unplugged" is about cutting the power lines to the big machines and walking away from the "crazy circus" of the music industry. It leans heavily into a mellow acoustic guitar paired with a soft, atmospheric synth pad, creating a nocturnal, reflective mood as the siblings contemplate their hiatus.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Warm, mellow acoustic guitar intro)
(A soft, atmospheric synth hums gently)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Pull the cords out of the wall
Let the heavy feedback fall
I don't want to hear the overdrive
I just want to feel like we're alive
Just the wood, the wire, and the hollow sound
Before they tried to run us to the ground

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Take the master tapes and let them burn
There’s a different kind of truth we have to learn
No electric pulse to hide the pain

(Mellow acoustic guitar and synth interlude)

[Verse 3]
(Ryan)
It takes a lot of nerve to just be still
To stop the endless climbing of the hill

[Verse 4]

But in this quiet room, I find my grace

title: Brother's Keeper
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Brother's Keeper" explores the profound, life-or-death mutual protection Ryan and Cassidy offer one another. Due to his T-10 paralysis, Ryan literally would not survive without Cassidy. She fiercely guards him and performs his daily ADLs (Activities of Daily Living)—including toileting requirements and anti-atrophy leg stretches. At night, they share a bed pushed against the wall, with Ryan on the inside and Cassidy sleeping on the edge to act as a human bed-rail so he doesn't roll off. In return for this intense physical devotion, Ryan acts as Cassidy's emotional anchor, protecting her from the brutal psychological toll of the music industry. The acoustic guitar and piano arrangement creates a delicate, vulnerable atmosphere for this raw confession of absolute co-dependence. (The lyrics are intentionally written from a unified, perspective-neutral standpoint to reflect their shared reality).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A delicate, melancholy piano intro)
(Acoustic guitar joins with a steady, comforting rhythm)

[Verse 1]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
They look at the chair and they think it's weak
They whisper their pity whenever we speak
But they don't see the mornings, the stretches and pain
The quiet routines keeping us sane
Sleeping on the edge, a human bed rail
Catching the other whenever we fail

[Verse 2]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
Moving the pieces the body forgot
Holding the line whenever we're caught
Being the strength when the daily tasks break
Giving up comfort for the other one's sake
A brother and a sister, fighting to survive
The only reason we're staying alive

[Pre-Chorus]
Are we each other's keeper? We'll take the blame
Standing in the fire, walking through the flame
Answering the call when it gets too deep
Guarding all the secrets we're trying to keep

[Chorus]
(Duet)
We trade all the armor, we trade all the scars
We built our own world underneath all the stars
When the body won't work, we become our own feet
When the pressure is heavy, we make it retreat
They don't understand the blood in our veins
We’re holding the keys and we’re breaking the chains

[Interlude]
(Emotional piano and acoustic guitar interlude)

[Verse 3]
Pushing the wheels wherever we go
Being the shelter when bitter winds blow

[Chorus]
(Duet)
We trade all the armor, we trade all the scars
We built our own world underneath all the stars
When the body won't work, we become our own feet
When the pressure is heavy, we make it retreat
They don't understand the blood in our veins
We’re holding the keys and we’re breaking the chains

[Outro]
(Harmonizing gently)
We keep each other safe.
We keep each other grounded.
(Fade out on a single, resonating piano chord)

title: Through the Static
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Through the Static" explores Ryan and Cassidy's almost telepathic connection, born from years of shared trauma, recovery, and absolute reliance on one another. The title refers to the chaos of the music industry, the physical realities of Ryan's paralysis, and the overwhelming noise of the world. In the midst of all that static, they can always find each other's signal. A glance across a crowded room, a shift in breathing in the dark, a subtle change in the rhythm of the wheels—they understand it all. It is a song about tuning out the interference and focusing on the one frequency that matters: their bond. The acoustic guitar and piano arrangement leaves plenty of space for their vocal harmonies to interlock. (The lyrics are written to be perspective-neutral and fluid so that whichever vocal Suno randomly assigns won't break the canon).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Gentle acoustic fingerpicking)
(A haunting, soft piano melody)

[Verse 1]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
There's a hundred thousand voices in this room
A tidal wave of flashing lights and gloom
The industry is screaming in my ear
Telling me the things I ought to fear

[Verse 2]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
I can see the tension in your jaw
I can read the writing on the wall
You don't have to say a single word
I hear everything that goes unheard

[Chorus]
(Duet)
We can hear each other through the static
A signal cutting clear across the noise
When the world around us gets erratic
We just listen for the other's voice
Our own frequency, steady and true
I'm always tuned in to you

[Interlude]
(Acoustic guitar and piano intertwine, mimicking a steady heartbeat)

[Verse 3]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
When the pain is sharp and breathing's slow
You're the only one who seems to know
A silent conversation in the dark

[Verse 4]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
I feel the little changes in your spark
A subtle shift, a shadow in your eye
I'll be there before you have to try

[Chorus]
(Duet)
We can hear each other through the static
A signal cutting clear across the noise
When the world around us gets erratic
We just listen for the other's voice
Our own frequency, steady and true
I'm always tuned in to you

[Bridge]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
Let the cameras flash, let the critics speak
Let the record spin until it's weak
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
They can have the fame and all the gold
We have a connection they can't hold

[Outro]
(Harmonizing softly)
Through the static...
Just you and me.
Tuned in perfectly.
(Acoustic guitar fades into silence)

title: The Weight We Carry
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"The Weight We Carry" acknowledges that their profound codependence, while beautiful and necessary, is incredibly heavy. It’s an honest, acoustic confession that sometimes the pressure of being everything to someone else is overwhelming. Ryan carries the physical weight of his condition and the guilt of needing Cassidy so much. Cassidy carries the emotional weight of his physical survival and the constant vigilance required. It’s not resentment, but rather a somber realization of their reality. The song is a quiet promise that even when the weight is crushing, they will never drop each other. (The lyrics are written to be perspective-neutral and fluid so that whichever vocal Suno randomly assigns won't break the canon).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Slow, somber acoustic guitar picking)
(A heavy, resonant piano chord)

[Verse 1]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
Sometimes I look at the lines on your face
And I see all the years in this terrible place
I know what it costs you to stay by my side
The pieces of you that you're trying to hide

[Verse 2]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
Don't talk like it's a burden I didn't choose
There's nothing about you I'm willing to lose
It's heavy, it's hard, and it breaks me apart
But it's the only thing keeping a beat in my heart

[Chorus]
(Duet)
The weight we carry is pulling us down
But we're holding our breath so we never drown
It's a beautiful anchor, a terrible chain
It's the love that we found at the end of the pain
We won't let it fall, we won't let it go
It's the only gravity we'll ever know

[Verse 3]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
I hate that you can't have a life of your own
I hate that I need you to not be alone
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
But my life is right here in the dark of this room
We're flowers that only know how to bloom
In the shade of each other, away from the sun
When the rest of the world is all said and done

[Chorus]
(Duet)
The weight we carry is pulling us down
But we're holding our breath so we never drown
It's a beautiful anchor, a terrible chain
It's the love that we found at the end of the pain
We won't let it fall, we won't let it go
It's the only gravity we'll ever know

[Outro]
(Harmonizing softly)
It's heavy...
But I'm here.
I'm not going anywhere.
(Fade out on acoustic guitar)

title: Just Us
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
"Just Us" is the closing track of the album. After exploring their profound trauma, intense codependence, and the noise of the industry, the album ends on a note of quiet peace. It’s a stripped-down, acoustic lullaby. No matter what happens—whether the band fails or succeeds, whether the pain worsens or fades—at the end of the day, it is just Ryan and Cassidy. They are enough for each other. It's a gentle, reassuring end to a deeply emotional album. (The lyrics are written to be perspective-neutral and fluid so that whichever vocal Suno randomly assigns won't break the canon).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A warm, comforting acoustic guitar melody)
(Soft, twinkling piano notes)

[Verse 1]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)

[Verse 2]

My savior, my shadow, my only true friend

Just you and me
Like it's always gonna be

[Interlude]
(A beautiful, peaceful acoustic solo)

[Verse 3]
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
I'll keep you safe when the shadows creep
I'll hold your hand while you fall asleep
(Duet or Solo - Organic Routing)
We don't need the money, we don't need the fame
As long as you're here to whisper my name

[Chorus]
(Duet)
It's just us in the end
My savior, my shadow, my only true friend
When the music stops and the curtains fall
We're the only thing that matters at all
Just you and me
Like it's always gonna be

[Outro]
(Harmonizing gently)
Just us...
Just us...
(A final, resolving acoustic chord rings out)
(Silence)

title: The Stardust Engine (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Like the rest of *Electric Color*, *"The Stardust Engine"* was officially released in 1987 (buried by Apex Records at the very end of the album as Track 13). In truth, it was the very first song Cassidy and Ryan O'Connell came up with in 1986 when their twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright joined them at CPI in Blacksburg. Too scared at the time to shop the song around, the four of them kept it to themselves and decided to use that first song to name their band: **The Stardust Engine**. Twenty-five years later, the band's eponymous theme is reborn as the opening calibration sequence of 2011's *Starfield Calibration*—stripped of Apex Records' 1987 neon gloss and rebuilt from the ground up inside Cassidy O'Connell's proprietary **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** (an in-universe trademark of Engine Room Records, LLC; not registered in real life), suspending Ryan and Cassidy's sibling duet inside a 360-degree zero-gravity planetarium dome.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A sweeping, zero-gravity 1980s analog synthesizer pad blooms across the planetarium dome like a sunrise from orbit)
(A melodic, sliding fretless bassline locks into a steady, driving 4/4 gated reverb drum beat)
(Sparkling analog bell arpeggios and chorus-drenched space-rock guitar harmonics echo across the stereo field)

[female] In zero-G we're taking flight!
[male] Turning our future on, shining so bright!

[Verse 3]

[male] Tied to the earth, waiting for the fall
[female] But they can't reach the altitude we know
[female] Up in the sanctuary where the nebulae glow!

[female] The telemetry is locked in alignment tonight
[male] Leaving terrestrial gravity for the infinite light!

[Bridge]
(Drums drop out into weightless zero-gravity synth pads and echoing vocal reverb)

[male] Taking this orbit higher and higher

[male] We are the Engine!
[female] Locked in the tidal rhythm of the stars!

(Lush analog synthesizer chords, space-rock guitar harmonics, and fretless bass notes slowly drift outward into eternal cosmic reverb)

title: Electric Color (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
In 1987, *"Electric Color"* was the band's Trojan horse—a blindingly bright synth-pop hit engineered to satisfy Apex Records' radio quotas while concealing lyrics about dissociation and creative captivity. Twenty-four years later, Cassidy O'Connell reclaims the song completely on solo vocals, replacing the brittle 1980s studio brass with warm, zero-gravity analog polyphonic pads and a hypnotic fretless bassline by Evan Wright. In the Cosmic Tidal Lock mix, the "neon lights" are no longer fluorescent studio cages—they are deep-space auroras.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(A vast, zero-gravity wash of shimmering analog synthesizer pads opens in deep space)

title: Plastic Sky (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Originally written in 1987 as a sharp critique of Los Angeles artifice (*"Look up at the ceiling, painted blue and white / There are no stars in this fake night"*), *"Plastic Sky"* undergoes a breathtaking thematic inversion on *Starfield Calibration*. Performed inside real-world planetarium domes where the ceiling literally opens into a simulated universe, Cassidy's solo vocal and soaring analog keytar solo shatter the painted fiberglass ceiling and launch the listener into open orbit.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Echoing 4/4 gated drum beat and a hypnotic, sliding fretless bassline enter in the dark)
(Shimmering analog synthesizer bells and lush spatial reverb build a zero-gravity dome of sound)

[Verse 1]
The camera's on, the smile is bright
Another take in the fluorescent light
They painted the ceiling a counterfeit blue
It never felt real, it never felt true

[Pre-Chorus]
(Analog synth pads swell upward like an airlock opening to the stars)
I'm looking past the studio glass
Watching the constellations pass

[Chorus]

Now we're breaking through the plastic sky!

[Verse 2]
They wanted it safe, they wanted it thin

[Synthesizer Solo]

Into the velvet blue...

title: Worlds Apart (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)

**LORE NOTE:**

Re-engineered in **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™**, the song's "silent satellite" metaphor becomes literal—two voices separated across the vacuum of space, locking onto the same frequency across a million miles of static.

[Intro]

content:
**LORE NOTE:**
On 1987's *Electric Color*, *"Rearview Mirror"* was Cassidy's quiet lament about feeling like a passenger in her own career (*"I'm just a passenger in this ride / With all this 'Stardust' left inside"*), as Apex Records reduced her and Ryan's love of the cosmos and rockets into a cheap corporate naming gimmick. Looking back twenty-four years later on 2011's *Starfield Calibration* from the helm of her own zero-gravity sanctuary, Cassidy flips the 1987 lyric on its head: *"I used to be a passenger on their ride / With all this Stardust locked inside / Now I'm at the helm of the frequency / And the whole horizon belongs to me!"*

**LYRICS:**

title: Atmosphere (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Originally recorded in September 1992 for the canceled *Friction* album (where rogue Apex executive Julian Vance infamously misinterpreted its literal space-shuttle re-entry physics—*"Here comes the friction, feel the fire"*—as sexual innuendo), *"Atmosphere"* existed for nineteen years only as an early rough cut (*"Atmosphere (1992 Demo)"* on the 1996 *Ad Astra* single and *"Atmosphere (Warehouse Demo)"* on 2007's *Lost Sounds*). Because that 1992 rough demo sounded like an early-1990s track tracked under label pressure, the band was never happy with it. On 2011's *Starfield Calibration*, Cassidy and Ryan finally deliver the **definitive, finalized version** of *"Atmosphere"*—using **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** to bring the song back to the lush, shimmering 1980s sound they love so much.

We traded time for something real / A tidal lock that you can feel"*). title: Reignition: Lights Up on Progress Street
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Thematically answering the sign-off of 2004's "Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street" ("Lights out on Progress Street... Goodnight, Forger Nation"), the opening anthem of 2015's *Reignition* celebrates the end of the band's decade-long **2005–2014 Burnout Hiatus**. Opening with warm acoustic piano chords that erupt into Cassidy's bright analog polyphonic analog brass fanfare, Tyler's booming gated-reverb snare, Evan's driving eighth-note bassline, and Ryan's soaring electric guitar, it marks the family's triumphant return to full-throttle 1980s AOR studio rock.

**LYRICS:**

We hung the guitars on the living room wall
Let the silence heal us down the narrow hall
(Cassidy)
We kept the promise that we made that night
Turned down the dimmers on the blinding light
No broken pieces, no fading away
We were just resting for a brand new day!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Feel the transformers hum beneath the floor!
(Cassidy)
Hear the twin rhythm knocking at the door!
(Ryan)
Every tube is glowing cherry red!
(Duet)
And every word we left unsaid is waking up ahead!

[Chorus]
(Duet)
This is Reignition! Throw the master switch!
Climbing out of the quiet to the highest pitch!
Lights up on Progress Street, the fire's burning bright
Splitting through the shadow of a ten-year night!
From the basement breakers to the stadium sky
The Stardust Engine never said goodbye!
This is Reignition! Hear the thrusters roar!
We're lighting up the valley like we did before!

(Cassidy)
My Juno keys are warm beneath my hands
Ready for the stages in a hundred lands
(Ryan)
Locked my wheels in place beside the microphone
Never had to roll a single mile alone
(Cassidy)
Evan on the bassline, Tyler on the snare
(Ryan)
Holly in the corner with a fortress to spare!
Five hearts beating on the very same floor
Opening the locks upon the studio door!

(Cassidy)
Feel the transformers hum beneath the floor!
(Ryan)
Hear the twin rhythm knocking at the door!

Every tube is glowing cherry red!

[Chorus]

This is Reignition! Throw the master switch!
Climbing out of the quiet to the highest pitch!
Lights up on Progress Street, the fire's burning bright
Splitting through the shadow of a ten-year night!
From the basement breakers to the stadium sky
The Stardust Engine never said goodbye!
This is Reignition! Hear the thrusters roar!
We're lighting up the valley like we did before!

[Bridge]
(Music drops to pulsing analog synth pad and steady kick drum)
(Cassidy)
We didn't burn out, we just took our time
(Ryan)
Saved every spark for the second climb
(Cassidy)
Now the meters are pinning in the crimson zone!
(Ryan)
Blacksburg, Virginia—your band is home!

[Guitar & Synthesizer Solo]
(A soaring, melodic 1980s AOR electric guitar solo trading triumphant phrases with a bright polyphonic analog synthesizer lead)

[Final Chorus]
(Duet - Full Stadium Energy)
This is Reignition! Throw the master switch!
Climbing out of the quiet to the highest pitch!
Lights up on Progress Street, the fire's burning bright
Splitting through the shadow of a ten-year night!
From the basement breakers to the stadium sky
The Stardust Engine never said goodbye!
This is Reignition! Hear the thrusters roar!
