(Soaring twin guitar and synth harmony over pounding gated drums)
(Cassidy)
Lights up on Progress Street!
(Ryan)
The fire is back!
(Final ringing D-Major stadium power chord and gong crash)

title: Main Engine Start
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Inspired by the Space Shuttle launch on the album's cover and the band's lifelong love of the rockets that take you to the cosmos ("Engine"), Ryan leads a 142 BPM 1980s arena-rock thriller structured around a Cape Canaveral launch countdown ("T-minus six seconds... Main Engine Start... Zero... Liftoff!"). The song celebrates the sheer physical exhilaration of feeling the band's creative thrusters roar back to full power after ten years on the ground.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Sweeping 1980s analog synthesizer arpeggios panning across the stereo field)

[Spoken Word Intro]
(Ryan - spoken clearly)
Guidance is internal.
T-minus ten... nine... eight...
Seven... six...
Main Engine Start!
Four... three... two... one...
Zero! Liftoff!

[Instrumental Hook]
(Explosive 142 BPM palm-muted electric guitar riff and thunderous 80s gated-reverb drums kick in)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
White-hot steam billowing across the pad
Every ounce of horsepower we ever had
Three million pounds of thrust beneath the floor
Shaking every bolt upon the hangar door!
We spent a decade anchored to the ground
Waiting for the moment when the clock came round
Now the gantry pulls away into the night
And we're riding on a column of electric light!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Feel the G-force pressing on your chest!
Put the titanium airframe to the test!
(Gang Vocals)
Roll program! Pitch into the sky!
(Ryan)
Watch the blue horizon of the earth go by!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
Thirty miles up and the sky turns black
Nothing in the universe can hold us back
Solid rocket separation, clean and true
Look out the window at the endless view!
We built this vessel out of heart and steel
Two twin brothers and a brother on wheels
A sister on the keys and a sister at the helm
Crossing the border to a higher realm!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Feel the G-force pressing on your chest!
Put the titanium airframe to the test!
(Gang Vocals)
Max-Q cleared! Throttle up to full!
(Ryan)
Breaking every tether of the gravity pull!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Bridge]
(Half-time heavy arena rock groove with soaring synthesizer brass)
(Ryan)
They thought the countdown ended years ago
Thought the cold dark winter froze the afterglow
But an engine built for orbit never forgets the stars
Reaching for the heavens where the cosmos are!

[Guitar Solo]
(A soaring, virtuosic 1980s two-hand tapping electric guitar solo over galloping bass and rapid-fire double-kick drums)

[Final Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Outro]
(Gang Vocals)
Main Engine Start!
(Ryan)
All thrusters at one hundred and four percent!
We are in orbit!
(Final blazing guitar harmonic and gated drum crescendo)

title: The Iceberg: Submerged
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A sleek, driving 126 BPM 1980s melodic synth-rocker celebrating younger sister and CEO Holly O'Connell passing the Delaware Bar in August 2015 and executing "The Delaware Migration"—folding *Engine Room Records, LLC*, *Artists First Management, LLC*, *Stardust Properties, LLC*, and *Pacific Rim Properties, LLC* into anonymous Delaware corporate structures beneath *The O'Connell Family Revocable Trust*. As Cassidy sings over a sequenced analog bassline, nine-tenths of the family's $2.4B+ fortress sits permanently beneath the waterline where the outside world can never see it.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Sleek, pulsing 1980s sequenced analog synthesizer bassline in F# Minor)
(Shimmering polyphonic synth chords and crisp gated-reverb snare)
(Rhythmic chorused electric guitar riff locks in)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
Up on the surface it's a quiet street
Five pairs of boots and a steady beat
Just a small-town band from the mountain air
No flashy limousines anywhere
The suited strangers with their legal pads
Looking for the fortune that the lottery had
They search the registries from coast to coast
Chasing after shadows and a paper ghost!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
They only see the tip above the ocean wave
They don't know the sanctuary our sister gave
Deep beneath the surface where the waters gleam
Safe inside the quiet of a vaulted dream!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy & Backing Harmonies)
Like an iceberg—nine-tenths underneath the sea!
Submerged in the deep where the world can't see!
On paper we're just five kids from a mountain town
While the fortress underneath can never be torn down!
You can't buy the master and you can't find the key
The Iceberg is submerged and the family is free!

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Started with a notebook and a crimson pen
Sixteen years old with a steady plan
She crossed out the traps in the fine-print line
And built a shelter that would outlast time
Now the autumn wind blows across the bay
And the whole foundation is tucked away
From the western coast to the Blue Ridge crest
Held inside the harbor of the family chest!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
They only see the tip above the ocean wave
They don't know the sanctuary our sister gave
No public shareholders, no board of greed
Just the five of us and everything we'll ever need!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy & Backing Harmonies)
Like an iceberg—nine-tenths underneath the sea!
Submerged in the deep where the world can't see!
On paper we're just five kids from a mountain town
While the fortress underneath can never be torn down!
You can't buy the master and you can't find the key
The Iceberg is submerged and the family is free!

[Bridge]
(Atmospheric deep-ocean analog synth pad with fretless bass harmonics)
(Cassidy)
Let the tabloids guess, let the bankers pry
There's nothing on the radar underneath this sky
We play for the kids in the bleachers tonight
Because the foundation is watertight!

[Guitar & Synth Duel]
(Sleek, melodic 1980s electric guitar solo trading rapid arpeggios with a bright analog synthesizer lead)

[Final Chorus]
(Cassidy & Full Band)
Like an iceberg—nine-tenths underneath the sea!
Submerged in the deep where the world can't see!
On paper we're just five kids from a mountain town
While the fortress underneath can never be torn down!
You can't buy the master and you can't find the key
The Iceberg is submerged and the family is free!

[Outro]
(Sequenced analog synth bass pulses into the deep)
(Cassidy)
Submerged and untouchable.
Thank you, Holly.
(Final crisp synth chord and gated snare hit)

title: Orbital Return
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Cassidy's lush, zero-gravity 1980s Cosmic Pop centerpiece (**The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™**), bridging her 2011 silver-anniversary studio project *Starfield Calibration* into the full four-piece band's 2015 comeback. Layered with sweeping analog polyphonic pads, cascading analog polyphonic arpeggios, and a weightless, singing lead guitar solo from Ryan, it captures the sensation of a spacecraft rounding the far side of the moon and locking back onto the radio beacon of home.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Lush, sweeping 1980s analog polyphonic analog synthesizer pads and sparkling analog polyphonic arpeggios)
(Warm melodic bassline and booming gated-reverb drums enter at 118 BPM)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
Drifting in the silence on the lunar side
Where the radio waves have nowhere left to hide
Watching all the constellations wheeling slow
Three hundred thousand miles from the world below
Sometimes you need the vacuum and the velvet dark
To recalibrate the compass and protect the spark
Floating in the zero-G of our own design
Waiting for the telemetry to realign

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
Then the horizon curves into the golden light
Earthrise breaking through the endless night
A familiar frequency begins to hum
Telling every instrument the time has come!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy)
This is our Orbital Return!
Feel the retro-rockets softly burn!
Coming around from the quiet side of the moon
Locking on the signal of a hometown tune!
Weightless in the starlight, steady on the line
Every single trajectory is yours and mine!
From the deepest cosmos to the atmosphere
This is our Orbital Return—and we are here!

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Stardust in the capacitors, gold in the wire
Harmonic velocity and liquid fire
My brother's guitar singing through the solar wind
Picking up the melody where we began
Twin moons rising in a tidal lock
Steady as the pulse of an atomic clock
No longer hiding in the shadow cone
We're banking toward the beacon that brings us home!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
See the Blue Ridge glowing on the radar screen
The prettiest landing strip we've ever seen
Every frequency begins to hum
Telling Forger Nation that the time has come!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy)
This is our Orbital Return!
Feel the retro-rockets softly burn!
Coming around from the quiet side of the moon
Locking on the signal of a hometown tune!
Weightless in the starlight, steady on the line
Every single trajectory is yours and mine!
From the deepest cosmos to the atmosphere
This is our Orbital Return—and we are here!

[Bridge]
(Zero-gravity breakdown with shimmering bell synths and chorus guitar arpeggios)
(Cassidy)
Every orbit takes you far away
Only so it can bring you back someday
Stronger in the gravity, clearer in the sight
Wrapped inside a halo of electric light!

[Guitar Solo]
(A soaring, weightless, deeply melodic 1980s electric guitar solo floating over cascading analog synthesizer waves)

[Final Chorus]
(Cassidy & Ryan Harmonies)
This is our Orbital Return!
Feel the retro-rockets softly burn!
Coming around from the quiet side of the moon
Locking on the signal of a hometown tune!
Weightless in the starlight, steady on the line
Every single trajectory is yours and mine!
From the deepest cosmos to the atmosphere
This is our Orbital Return—and we are here!

[Outro]
(Cascading 1980s synthesizer arpeggios fade gently into warm cosmic starlight)
(Cassidy)
Telemetry locked. Welcome home.

title: Ten Years in the Quiet
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Work-life balance in song form: an honest, deeply moving 84 BPM 1980s AOR power ballad reflecting on the **2005–2014 Burnout Hiatus**. After recording four studio albums in four years and reaching complete sensory and physical exhaustion at the end of the 2004 Norfolk tour, Ryan and Cassidy sing about how choosing to walk away from the spotlight for ten years—drinking coffee on the Progress Street porch, cooking family dinners, and protecting their neurodivergent boundaries—saved their lives and kept the five of them whole.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Gentle acoustic piano and clean chorused electric guitar arpeggios at 84 BPM)
(Warm analog synthesizer strings swell softly underneath)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Two thousand and four under a concrete dome
Four albums in the rearview on the highway home
My hands were shaking on the steering rim
And the stage lights felt a little too bright and dim
(Cassidy)
Every room was spinning at a hundred degrees
Too many voices asking us to please
So we walked off the stage and we closed the door
And left the suitcases on the hallway floor

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
The world asked where we went and why we walked away
(Cassidy)
When we were at the summit of the game we play
(Duet)
Because a trophy doesn't matter if you lose your soul
So we chose each other just to keep us whole

[Chorus]
(Duet)
Ten years in the quiet, ten years in the shade
Best decision that this family ever made
Morning coffee on the Progress Street porch
Passing down the warmth instead of burning out the torch
No cameras in the kitchen, no schedules to keep
Just ten years in the quiet where the roots grow deep
And now we know the secret that the road can't teach:
Sometimes stepping back is how you keep the stars in reach

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Sunday dinners at a wooden table for five
Learning what it feels like just to be alive
Walking through the autumn leaves without a crowd
Where the morning melody was gentle and proud
(Ryan)
Evan fixing bicycles out in the drive
Tyler laughing til the neighbors knew we were alive
Holly with her law books and her steady grace
Keeping peace and quiet in our favorite place

[Pre-Chorus]
(Massive gated-reverb drum fill enters)
(Cassidy)
They said if you step off the train you'll fade to gray
(Ryan)
But love doesn't rust when you put it away!
(Duet)
Now the batteries are full and the spirit is clear
And we're ready for the music that brought us here!

[Chorus]
(Duet - Full 1980s Arena Power Ballad)
Ten years in the quiet, ten years in the shade
Best decision that this family ever made
Morning coffee on the Progress Street porch
Passing down the warmth instead of burning out the torch
No cameras in the kitchen, no schedules to keep
Just ten years in the quiet where the roots grow deep
And now we know the secret that the road can't teach:
Sometimes stepping back is how you keep the stars in reach!

[Guitar Solo]
(A deeply emotional, soaring 1980s arena power-ballad guitar solo climbing into the upper register over lush synth strings)

[Bridge]
(Piano and vocals only)
(Cassidy)
If your heart is running on a worn-out wire
(Ryan)
You don't owe the world your very last fire
(Duet)
Turn the switches off until the storm has passed
That's how you build a love that's gonna last!

[Final Chorus]
(Duet - Soaring Crescendo)
Ten years in the quiet, ten years in the shade
Best decision that this family ever made!
Morning coffee on the Progress Street porch
Passing down the warmth instead of burning out the torch!
And now we know the secret that the road can't teach:
Stepping back together kept the stars in reach!

[Outro]
(Gentle acoustic piano and clean electric guitar fade out together)
(Cassidy)
Ten years stronger.
(Ryan)
Ready when you are, sis.

title: Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Written and recorded in a burst of autumn excitement in October 2015 immediately after **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)** traveled down to Norfolk for **Virginia Dominion University (VDU)**'s Homecoming game. After VDU students printed thousands of mocking *"38–0"* t-shirts commemorating their 2014 upset, the Forgers walked into Norfolk and delivered a triumphant **52–0 shutout victory**. Featuring Tyler's thunderous marching snare cadence and a roaring stadium chorus, it became an instant autumn anthem across Blacksburg.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Thunderous marching drumline snare cadence by Tyler with massive 1980s gated reverb)
(Triumphant 1980s analog synthesizer brass fanfare in C Minor)
(Driving overdriven stadium electric guitar riff kicks in at 138 BPM)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Three hundred sixty-five days with the numbers on the wall
Stenciled on the mirrors down the weight-room hall
We kept our focus steady through the winter rain
Working every morning til we broke the chain
(Cassidy)
Then we rolled down to the harbor for the autumn crown
Saw the old numbers printed all across the town
Banners in the tidewater, music in the street
Listen to the iron marching down the concrete!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
No holding back today! Keep the starters on the grass!
(Cassidy)
Every single quarter is a masterclass!
(Duet)
From the opening kickoff to the final cheer
Hear the anvils ringing loud and clear!

[Chorus]
(Duet & Stadium Gang Vocals)
Fifty-two to nothing! Put it on the board!
Hear the mighty thunder of the Forger chord!
You wore the old numbers on your Homecoming chest
Till the mountains came down and put the talk to rest!
Maroon and burnt orange underneath the autumn sky
Raise our banners high for CPI!
Fifty-two to nothing! Hear the stadium call
Forger Nation stands above it all!

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Fourth quarter ticking and the defense holds the line
Protecting every inch of the goal-line design
(Ryan)
Maroon and burnt orange in the coastal breeze
Every single play is a masterpiece!
From Blacksburg to the harbor, hear the victory song
This is where the heart of the mountains belongs!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
No holding back today! Keep the starters on the grass!
(Ryan)
Every single quarter is a masterclass!
(Duet)
From the opening kickoff to the final cheer
Hear the anvils ringing loud and clear!

[Chorus]
(Duet & Stadium Gang Vocals)
Fifty-two to nothing! Put it on the board!
Hear the mighty thunder of the Forger chord!
You wore the old numbers on your Homecoming chest
Till the mountains came down and put the talk to rest!
Maroon and burnt orange underneath the autumn sky
Raise our banners high for CPI!
Fifty-two to nothing! Hear the stadium call
Forger Nation stands above it all!

[Bridge]
(Marching drumline breakdown with stomping stadium boots and brass stabs)
(Gang Chant)
HOLD THAT LINE! STRIKE THAT IRON!
HOLD THAT LINE! STRIKE THAT IRON!
(Ryan)
From the weight-room mirror to the scoreboard sky—
All hail CPI!

[Guitar & Synthesizer Solo]
(Blazing 1980s twin guitar and analog synth duel trading high-speed melodic runs over pounding double-kick drums)

[Final Chorus]
(Duet & Stadium Gang Vocals)
Fifty-two to nothing! Put it on the board!
Hear the mighty thunder of the Forger chord!
You wore the old numbers on your Homecoming chest
Till the mountains came down and put the talk to rest!
Fifty-two to nothing! Hear the stadium call
Forger Nation stands above it all!

[Outro]
(Stadium Brass & Gated Drums)
(Duet)
Fifty-two to nothing!
Go Forgers!
(Final ringing anvil chime and C-Minor power chord)

title: Twin Frequency: The Rhythm Section
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A high-energy, groove-driven 130 BPM 1980s arena rocker spotlighting identical twin brothers **Evan** (bass guitar) and **Tyler** (drums)—the unshakeable rhythmic engine of The Stardust Engine since 1985. Built around a syncopated slap-and-fingerstyle bass groove locked to Tyler's booming octoban fills and gated-reverb snare, the track celebrates the twins' telepathic connection both on stage and behind the wheel of *The Iron Horse*.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Explosive 1980s octoban drum roll by Tyler slamming into a funky, syncopated electric bass groove by Evan at 130 BPM)
(Punchy 80s analog synth-brass stabs and crisp rhythm guitar join the pocket)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Born on the very same morning in the Blue Ridge air
Finishing each other's sentences before they're even there
Nineteen eighty-five when they walked into the room
Four strings and a kick drum making the basement boom!
Never needed click tracks, never needed cues
Locked into a pocket that could never lose
One brother on the low end, one behind the kit
Every single measure is a dead-center hit!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Look across the stage—they don't even have to speak!
(Gang Shouts)
Locked in!
(Ryan)
Forty-five-foot Prevost rolling through the mountain peak!
(Gang Shouts)
Twin power!
(Ryan)
When the road gets rough and the night gets long
They're the iron chassis underneath every song!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
Twin Frequency! Hear the rhythm section roar!
Shaking every rafter from the ceiling to the floor!
Bassline and the backbeat in a telepathic lock
Steady as the gears inside an iron clock!
Two brothers, one heartbeat, driving through the night
Holding up the engine with all their might!
Turn up the low end—it's Twin Frequency!

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
Trading off the highway shifts at three A.M.
Airbrakes and the diesel humming under them
Keeping us protected while the singers sleep
Making every promise that a brother can keep
Then the house lights drop and they take the riser stand
Tightest rhythm section anywhere we stand!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Look across the stage—they don't even have to speak!
(Gang Shouts)
Locked in!
(Ryan)
Two identical grins at the rhythm's peak!
(Gang Shouts)
Twin power!
(Ryan)
When the stadium shakes and the bleachers sway
Listen to the brothers play!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
Twin Frequency! Hear the rhythm section roar!
Shaking every rafter from the ceiling to the floor!
Bassline and the backbeat in a telepathic lock
Steady as the gears inside an iron clock!
Two brothers, one heartbeat, driving through the night
Holding up the engine with all their might!
Turn up the low end—it's Twin Frequency!

[Bass & Drum Breakdown]
(Ryan)
Take it away, Evan and Tyler!
(Virtuosic 1980s slap-and-fingerstyle electric bass solo trading thunderous octoban and double-kick drum fills back and forth)

[Guitar Solo]
(Blazing melodic electric guitar solo riding over the relentless bass-and-drum groove)

[Final Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
Twin Frequency! Hear the rhythm section roar!
Shaking every rafter from the ceiling to the floor!
Bassline and the backbeat in a telepathic lock
Steady as the gears inside an iron clock!
Two brothers, one heartbeat, driving through the night
Turn up the low end—it's Twin Frequency!

[Outro]
(Syncopated bass and drum lock ending on a massive unison hit)
(Ryan)
The heartbeat of the Engine!

title: Neon on the Huckleberry Trail
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A nostalgic, shimmering 124 BPM 1980s melodic synth-pop and AOR gem celebrating autumn dusks in Blacksburg and Christiansburg—Cassidy riding her bicycle and Ryan rolling his everyday wheelchair along the paved six-mile **Huckleberry Trail** under a canopy of golden and crimson Appalachian maples as twilight settles over the New River Valley and the stadium lights of **The Crucible** flicker on in the distance.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Shimmering 1980s chorused electric guitar arpeggios and warm polyphonic analog synthesizer bells at 124 BPM)
(Breezy eighth-note bassline and crisp gated-reverb snare enter)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
October five-thirty and the air turns crisp
Woodsmoke curling in a silver wisp
Maples turning crimson by the old rail bed
Canopy of burnt orange overhead
You're pushing on your hand-rims at an easy pace
With the mountain wind cooling off your face
Six miles of asphalt from the library lawn
Where the old Huckleberry train used to roll on

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
No studio clocks and no city stress
Just the valley dressed in its autumn dress
Watch the sun dip low behind Price Mountain's crest
In the quiet corner that we love the best!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy & Harmonies)
Chasing the neon on the Huckleberry Trail!
Where the twilight glows and the shadows sail!
Spinning our wheels through the golden leaves
Underneath a sky that still believes!
See the stadium towers flicker on in the night
Painting the valley in electric light!
Every autumn evening tells the same old tale
We're home together on the Huckleberry Trail!

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
Passing by the pastures where the cattle graze
Wrapped inside the amber of the college days
Students in their hoodies jogging two by two
Nodding with a smile as we roll on through
No autographs asked, just a neighbor's wave
In the mountain sanctuary that our hometown gave
Thirty years of music and we still belong
To the winding path where we wrote this song!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
No studio clocks and no city stress
Just the valley dressed in its autumn dress
Watch the stars come out above the mountain's crest
In the quiet corner that we love the best!

[Chorus]
(Cassidy & Harmonies)
Chasing the neon on the Huckleberry Trail!
Where the twilight glows and the shadows sail!
Spinning our wheels through the golden leaves
Underneath a sky that still believes!
See the stadium towers flicker on in the night
Painting the valley in electric light!
Every autumn evening tells the same old tale
We're home together on the Huckleberry Trail!

[Bridge]
(Warm analog synth pad and melodic bass solo)
(Cassidy)
We've seen Tokyo towers and the London rain
Paris boulevards and the coastal train
But nothing on earth ever feels as sweet
As the six-mile path leading back to Progress Street!

[Guitar Solo]
(An uplifting, breezy 1980s melodic electric guitar solo harmonizing with shimmering analog synth bells)

[Final Chorus]
(Cassidy & Ryan Harmonies)
Chasing the neon on the Huckleberry Trail!
Where the twilight glows and the shadows sail!
Spinning our wheels through the golden leaves
Underneath a sky that still believes!
See the stadium towers flicker on in the night
Painting the valley in electric light!
Every autumn evening tells the same old tale
We're home together on the Huckleberry Trail!

[Outro]
(Shimmering chorus guitar and analog synth arpeggios fade into the autumn dusk)
(Cassidy)
Race you back to Progress Street.

title: No Strings on the Master
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A scorching 146 BPM 1980s hard-AOR guitar anthem celebrating thirty years of fiercely guarded creative independence. Ryan calls out the 1980s corporate label executives at Apex Records who once tried to reduce Cassidy to their "Stardust" and Ryan to their "Engine" as a cheap marketing gimmick, raising a glass to Holly's 1986 `$1.00` Cross-License and Cassidy's 1996 buyout that ensured the family owns every master tape in the vault.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Blistering 146 BPM overdriven 1980s electric guitar riff in D Minor)
(Driving analog tonewheel organ and polyphonic synth stabs)
(Galloping bassline and rapid-fire gated-reverb drums kick in)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Back in eighty-seven in a glass-walled tower
Men in tailored suits intoxicated by their power
Pointed at my sister, called her "Stardust" on a chart
Pointed at my wheelchair, called me "Engine" for the part!
Turned our love of rockets and the galaxies above
Into a cheap slogan that we never could love
Tried to put a price tag on a family name
Tried to lock the songbirds in a corporate frame!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
They didn't know a sixteen-year-old girl with a pen
Had already outsmarted all the king's horses and men!
And when ninety-six hit like a lightning bolt from the sky
We bought the whole building and we waved goodbye!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
There are no strings on the master! No chains on the tape!
No boardroom committee dictating the shape!
Every single note is in the family vault
Protected by the iron and the mountain basalt!
We play what we want and we answer to none
Underneath the fire of our own twin sun!
Spinning every reel a little bit faster—
There are no strings on the master!

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
They said a band can't vanish for a ten-year rest
Without a label leaning on your weary chest
They said the catalog would go up on the block
To pay the quarterly dividends around the clock!
Well look inside the ledger—there's a zero owed!
We own the studio, the bus, and the road!
Not a single penny to a middleman's hand
Just five kids running our own promised land!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
They didn't know a sixteen-year-old girl with a pen
Had already outsmarted all the king's horses and men!
From eighty-six forward til the stars burn cold
Not a single master will ever be sold!

[Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
There are no strings on the master! No chains on the tape!
No boardroom committee dictating the shape!
Every single note is in the family vault
Protected by the iron and the mountain basalt!
We play what we want and we answer to none
Underneath the fire of our own twin sun!
Spinning every reel a little bit faster—
There are no strings on the master!

[Bridge]
(Half-time heavy riff with soaring synth brass)
(Ryan)
Stardust is the cosmos!
Engine is the rocket ship!
Not a marketing gimmick on a salesman's lip!
And every magnetic reel spinning on the shelf
Belongs to the family that built it itself!

[Guitar Solo]
(A scorching, virtuosic 1980s hard-rock electric guitar solo with rapid two-hand tapping and soaring melodic bends)

[Final Chorus]
(Ryan & Gang Vocals)
There are no strings on the master! No chains on the tape!
No boardroom committee dictating the shape!
Every single note is in the family vault
Protected by the iron and the mountain basalt!
Spinning every reel a little bit faster—
There are no strings on the master!

[Outro]
(Blazing guitar harmony and rapid drum fills)
(Ryan)
One hundred percent owned!
Engine Room Records!
(Final ringing D-Minor power chord)

title: Still Your Safe Person
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The emotional heart of *Reignition*. Opening with just Cassidy's acoustic grand piano and Ryan's weeping clean electric guitar before building into a monumental 78 BPM 1980s arena power ballad, the brother and sister sing to each other—and to every neurodivergent, overwhelmed, or healing listener in Forger Nation: *"When the static hits a hundred and the room begins to spin / I am still your safe person, let the quiet in."*

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Warm, intimate acoustic grand piano chord progression at 78 BPM)
(Weeping, clean melodic electric guitar counter-melody enters gently)

[Verse 1]
(Cassidy)
When the fluorescent lights are humming way too loud
And you're spinning in the middle of a noisy crowd
When the rules don't match the script inside your head
And every single wire is flashing crimson red
(Ryan)
You don't have to explain why your hands are shaking now
You don't have to force a smile or take a final bow
Just reach across the console, I'm right beside your chair
Breathing in the cadence of the quiet mountain air

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
We've known each other since the nursery floor
(Ryan)
And I know what the heavy wooden door is for
(Duet)
No questions asked, no judgment in this room
Just a harbor in the middle of the sonic boom

[Chorus]
(Duet - Lush 1980s analog synth strings and booming gated-reverb drums enter)
When the static hits a hundred and the room begins to spin
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!
Put your headphones on or lean against my shoulder tight
I will hold the perimeter throughout the longest night!
You don't have to be unbroken just to be enough
I will be the anchor when the ocean gets too rough
Through every single storm and every place we've been
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!

[Verse 2]
(Ryan)
Back when the winter changed the road beneath my seat
And I had to learn a brand new way to move down Progress Street
You never looked at me with pity in your eyes
You just lowered every keyboard stand to match my size
(Cassidy)
And when the tour arenas made my senses overflow
You pulled the curtain closed and told the crowd we had to go
Because a brother and a sister don't leave anyone behind
When the world is overwhelming to a tender mind!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
And to every single kid out in the bleachers tonight
(Cassidy)
Who feels a little different in the stadium light
(Duet)
Take this song and keep it in your coat pocket deep
For the nights when the mountain feels a little too steep!

[Chorus]
(Duet - Full Monumental 1980s Arena Power Ballad)
When the static hits a hundred and the room begins to spin
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!
Put your headphones on or lean against my shoulder tight
I will hold the perimeter throughout the longest night!
You don't have to be unbroken just to be enough
I will be the anchor when the ocean gets too rough
Through every single storm and every place we've been
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!

[Guitar Solo]
(A monumental, weeping 1980s arena power-ballad electric guitar solo, soaring with long sustained bends over grand piano and lush synth strings)

[Bridge]
(Stripped back to just grand piano and sibling vocals)
(Cassidy)
Breathe in for four...
(Ryan)
Hold it steady now...
(Cassidy)
Let the noise fall away...
(Duet)
You are safe right here today!

[Final Chorus]
(Duet & Soaring Choir Harmonies)
When the static hits a hundred and the room begins to spin
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!
You don't have to be unbroken just to be enough
I will be the anchor when the ocean gets too rough
Through every single storm and every place we've been
I am still your safe person—let the quiet in!

[Outro]
(Acoustic grand piano and clean electric guitar resolve on a warm, lingering C-Major chord)
(Cassidy - soft)
I've got you. Always.

title: Where the Stars Still Burn
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The sweeping, horizon-bound 134 BPM 1980s AOR and cosmic stadium-rock finale of *Reignition*. Looking up at the autumn constellations above the Blue Ridge after a ten-year hiatus, Ryan and Cassidy celebrate the enduring bond of their five-person family—knowing that time has not dimmed the spark they lit in 1986 and that the open highway ahead is still waiting where the stars still burn.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Lush, sweeping 1980s polyphonic analog synthesizer fanfare and shimmering arpeggiated keyboards in G Major)
(Twin harmonizing electric guitars and massive 80s gated-reverb drums enter at 134 BPM)

[Verse 1]
(Ryan)
Standing on the ridgeline where the mountain meets the sky
Watching thirty autumn seasons go rolling by
We started with a four-track and a borrowed set of keys
Chasing down a signal through the Appalachian trees
(Cassidy)
The maps have all been folded and the highways changed their names
We stepped out of the spotlight and we walked away from games
But look up at Orion hanging steady in the blue
The very same horizon is still waiting here for you!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Ryan)
Time can weather iron, time can silver-streak the hair
(Cassidy)
But it cannot touch a melody that's built to share!
(Duet)
Open up the throttle, let the final chapter start
With a compass in the dashboard and a rocket in our heart!

[Chorus]
(Duet & Full Band Harmonies)
Out where the stars still burn! Across the open night!
Every mile ahead of us is bathed in golden light!
We took the long road home, we weathered every turn
And found the fire waiting out where the stars still burn!
Five hearts on the frequency, steady and true
The universe is wider than the one we knew!
Keep the engines running til the morning sun returns—
Meet us on the horizon where the stars still burn!

[Verse 2]
(Cassidy)
No regrets behind us in the valley down below
Every quiet winter only helped the timber grow
(Ryan)
Four wheels on the pavement and four strings on the bass
Ten drumsticks in the quiver and a smile on every face!
(Cassidy)
We don't play for yesterday or monuments of stone
(Ryan)
We play because this music is the truest home we've known!

[Pre-Chorus]
(Cassidy)
Time can weather iron, time can silver-streak the hair
(Ryan)
But it cannot touch a melody that's built to share!
(Duet)
Open up the throttle, let the next adventure start
With a compass in the dashboard and a rocket in our heart!

[Chorus]
(Duet & Full Band Harmonies)
Out where the stars still burn! Across the open night!
Every mile ahead of us is bathed in golden light!
We took the long road home, we weathered every turn
And found the fire waiting out where the stars still burn!
Five hearts on the frequency, steady and true
The universe is wider than the one we knew!
Keep the engines running til the morning sun returns—
Meet us on the horizon where the stars still burn!

[Bridge]
(Music softens to shimmering analog synth arpeggios and clean chorus guitar)
(Cassidy)
Look how far we traveled from the basement floor
(Ryan)
And the best songs that we carry haven't been sung before!
(Music swells with thunderous gated-reverb drum roll)
(Duet)
As long as we're together, the night is never cold
And the story of the Engine will never grow old!

[Guitar & Synthesizer Solo]
(An epic, horizon-spanning 1980s stadium-rock twin electric guitar and analog synthesizer solo soaring over pounding gated drums)

[Final Chorus]
(Duet & Full Band Harmonies)
Out where the stars still burn! Across the open night!
Every mile ahead of us is bathed in golden light!
We took the long road home, we weathered every turn
And found the fire waiting out where the stars still burn!
Five hearts on the frequency, steady and true
The universe is wider than the one we knew!
Keep the engines running til the morning sun returns—
Meet us on the horizon where the stars still burn!

[Outro]
(Soaring twin guitar harmonies and cascading analog synthesizer bells)
(Cassidy)
Where the stars still burn!
(Ryan)
See you out on the horizon!
(Final triumphant, sustained G-Major stadium chord fading into starlight)

title: Ignition: The Forger's Call (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The very first time in history that **"Ignition: The Forger's Call"** was ever played and recorded for a live concert release (previously, the only way to hear *Ignition* was to attend a CPI Home Football Game in person inside **The Crucible**). With no opening act—just CPI Alumni (*Class of 1989*) coming home to play for their alma mater—Ryan O'Connell rolls out to the edge of the stage in his manual chair, recalls the October 1986 student contest cassette recorded by five kids (Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, Tyler, and 16-year-old dual-enrolled Holly O'Connell) in the garage at `412 Progress Street NE` and protected by Holly's `$1.00` Perpetual Mutual Cross-License, and cues the stadium blackout. As Tyler strikes his steel brake drum (`TING... BOOM!`), 65,000 Ironheads execute **The Stomp** on the galvanized bleachers of **The Anvil** until the Copernicus Hall seismographs spike, and Ryan shouts his triumphant November 2015 `52–0` ad-lib (*"We're taking the Anchor BACK to the Mountains!"*) while the four-piece rock band and the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers** erupt into a deafening call-and-response of **"IGNITION!"**

**LYRICS:**

[Ambient Sound: Massive Crowd Roar, Wind, Feedback]

[Spoken Intro - Ryan O'Connell]
(Gravelly voice, intimate, over faint synth pad)
[male]
Thirty years ago...
We were just five kids in a garage on Progress Street.
We didn't have a record deal...
We didn't have a tour bus...
All we had was a cassette tape... and an idea.

(Voice gets louder, commanding)
We entered a contest to write a song for this stadium.
We wanted to make something loud enough...
To scare the HELL out of anyone who dared to come into our house!

(Crowd cheers swell)
For thirty years... you guys have been stomping your feet to our song every single Saturday.
So tonight... for the 30th Anniversary...
Let's see if we can break the seismographs!

[Drum Fill: Slow, Massive, Thundering Stadium Kit - 82 BPM]
[male]
IGNITION!

[Crowd Response: 60,000 People]
(IGNITION!)

[Music Starts: Slow, Crushing 82 BPM Industrial Riff - Heavy Half-Time Kick-Drum Groove]
[Instrumental Anvil & Stomp Intro: Ringing Steel Anvil Strike Answered by Thundering Kick Drum and 60,000-Person Bleacher Stomp]

[Verse 1]
[male]
The lights go dark... the tension builds...
A single pounding heavy sound...
The hammer striking on the steel...
It shakes the air... it shakes the ground!
The pressure's on... the time is now...
We're here to forge our name!
The spark is lit... the fire burns...
(Ryan Ad-Lib - Shouted)
We're taking the Anchor BACK to the Mountains!

[Chorus]
[male]
IGNITION!
[Crowd Chant]
(IGNITION!)

[male]
This is the Forger's Call!

[male]
IGNITION!
[Crowd Chant]
(IGNITION!)

[male]
We're standing ten feet tall!
We are the hammer, we're the flame
This is our house, this is our game!

[Instrumental Anvil & Bleacher Stomp Break: Slow 82 BPM Steel Anvil Strike and Kick-Drum Stomp]
(Rhythmic metallic steel anvil strike answered by thundering kick drum and 60,000 boots stomping on metal bleachers)

[Verse 2]
[male]
Molten iron pouring on the foundry floor!
Hear the valley tremble when the Forgers roar!
Concrete and Ironstone locked inside the night!
Step into the furnace, step into the light!

[Chorus]
[male]
IGNITION!
[Crowd Chant]
(IGNITION!)

[male]
This is the Forger's Call!

[male]
IGNITION!
[Crowd Chant]
(IGNITION!)

[male]
We're standing ten feet tall!
We are the hammer, we're the flame
This is our house, this is our game!

[Guitar Solo]
(Slow, soaring 1980s stadium electric guitar lead over the synchronized 60,000-person kick-drum bleacher stomp and 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers brass stabs)

[Bridge]
(Slow half-time foundry cadence)
[male]
Strike! ... Strike! ... Strike the steel!
Feel the earthquake in the night!
Drop the hammer! ... Shake the steel!
Make the whole mountain feel!

[Final Chorus]
(Full Rock Band and 300-Piece CPI Marching Forgers Explosion)
[male]
IGNITION!
[Crowd Chant]
(IGNITION!)

This is the Forger's Call!

title: CPI Tech Triumph: The Marching Forgers (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Directly out of the final anvil strike of *"Ignition"*, the Drum Major's whistle pierces the night air (`Tweet-Tweet-Tweet-Tweet!`) and **"The Engine Room"**—the high-tension Kevlar marching snare battery of the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers**—launches into the official Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute Fight Song. Forming the **CPI Hammer and Anvil** across the turf while 65,000 students and alumni clap in time and roar *"GO! FORGERS! FIGHT! FORGERS! WIN! CPI!"*, the Marching Forgers turn the opening minutes of the concert into the ultimate Saturday night inside The Crucible.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Deafening stadium crowd roar)
(Piercing Drum Major whistle blows: Tweet-Tweet-Tweet-Tweet!)
(Crisp high-tension Kevlar marching snare battery roll-off by "The Engine Room")
(Explosive 300-piece collegiate brass chord blast in Bb Major)

[Part I: The Engine Room Cadence]
(Driving Kevlar marching snares, tenor quads, tonal bass drums, and rumbling sousaphone ostinato at 144 BPM)

[Part II: CPI Tech Triumph Main Fight Song]
(Soaring trumpets, mellophones, and trombones carry the triumphant Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute Fight Song melody over a precision marching beat)

[Stadium Crowd Chant]
(65,000 fans clapping in rhythm with the band)
(Crowd)
GO! FORGERS!
(Brass Fanfare Response)
(Crowd)
FIGHT! FORGERS!
(Brass Fanfare Response)
(Crowd)
WIN! CPI!

[Part III: The Hammer and Anvil Formation]
(Majestic brass countermelody and rapid woodwind flourishes as the 300-piece band locks into the CPI Hammer and Anvil formation)
(High-speed Kevlar drumline roll)

[Finale]
(Massive sustained 300-horn triumph chord)
(Sharp Drum Major cut-off snap to instant silence, followed by a deafening 65,000-person stadium eruption)

title: The Stardust Engine (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
While standard Stardust Engine concerts open directly with **"The Stardust Engine"**, here at their alma mater it serves as the culminating third movement of the opening sequence—performed with all 300 members of the **CPI Marching Forgers** still on the stage! Harmonizing 300 collegiate brass instruments and sousaphones with Cassidy's iconic 1986 **"Stardust"** analog synthesizer leitmotif and locking the Kevlar snare battery to Ryan's **"Engine"** guitar and Tyler's gated drums, the performance brings the stadium to a fever pitch before the Marching Forgers march off through the field tunnel—convincing everyone in the building that their guest appearance for the night is over.

**LYRICS:**

[Live Stadium Intro]
(The 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers remain in formation across the stage and field)
[female]
Keep the Marching Forgers right here with us!
[male]
Thirty years ago in 1986, Evan and Tyler walked into our basement and we wrote our very first song together about the cosmos and the rockets that get you there! Let's hear it, CPI!

(Verse 1)
We were looking for a signal
A light in the endless black
A single voice in the universe
To tell us we're on the right track

(Verse 2)
We found the fire in the wires
We found the heart in the machine
Building a dream from nothing
A sound the world has never seen

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Verse 3)
They tried to ground us, keep us small
Tell us that we were gonna fall
But they don't know the things we know
They haven't seen the places we'll go

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Guitar Solo)
(A soaring, melodic solo that trades licks with a bright synthesizer hook)

(Bridge)
We are the cosmos, we are the fire
We're taking this one, higher and higher
We are the Stardust!
(We are the Engine!)
We are the Stardust Engine!

(Chorus)
We are the Stardust Engine!
Racing through the night
We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light
We are the Stardust Engine!
Yeah, we're taking flight
Turning our future on, shining so bright!

(Outro)
Shining so bright...
We're taking flight...
(fades out on an epic, sustained guitar chord)

title: Main Engine Start (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
As the main body of the Marching Forgers files into the tunnel (leaving their 20-piece Lead Brass & Drumline Honor Guard at the front lip of the turf), the core four-piece band—Cassidy on her wraparound synthesizers, Ryan in his manual chair at center-left on lead guitar, and identical twins Evan (bass) and Tyler (drums) on the back risers—backed on the stage-left riser by their 5-piece "Orbital Crew" stadium touring section (Marcus Vance on rhythm guitar, Darius "Doc" Holloway on second kit/percussion, Claire Lindqvist on auxiliary synths, and CPI Jazz soloists Prof. Julian Vance on trumpet and Elena Rostova on sax so not a single pre-recorded backing track is ever used on stage) slams straight into the 142 BPM countdown thriller from 2015's *Reignition*. Sixty-five thousand fans count down from ten to liftoff in unison.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
(Sweeping 1980s analog synthesizer arpeggios panning across the stereo field)

[Spoken Word Intro]
[male]
(spoken clearly)
Guidance is internal.
T-minus ten... nine... eight...
Seven... six...
Main Engine Start!
Four... three... two... one...
Zero! Liftoff!

[Instrumental Hook]
(Explosive 142 BPM palm-muted electric guitar riff and thunderous 80s gated-reverb drums kick in)

[Verse 1]
[male]
White-hot steam billowing across the pad
Every ounce of horsepower we ever had
Three million pounds of thrust beneath the floor
Shaking every bolt upon the hangar door!
We spent a decade anchored to the ground
Waiting for the moment when the clock came round
Now the gantry pulls away into the night
And we're riding on a column of electric light!

[Pre-Chorus]
[male]
Feel the G-force pressing on your chest!
Put the titanium airframe to the test!
(Gang Vocals)
Roll program! Pitch into the sky!
[male]
Watch the blue horizon of the earth go by!

[Chorus]
(Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Verse 2]
[male]
Thirty miles up and the sky turns black
Nothing in the universe can hold us back
Solid rocket separation, clean and true
Look out the window at the endless view!
We built this vessel out of heart and steel
Two twin brothers and a brother on wheels
A sister on the keys and a sister at the helm
Crossing the border to a higher realm!

[Pre-Chorus]
[male]
Feel the G-force pressing on your chest!
Put the titanium airframe to the test!
(Gang Vocals)
Max-Q cleared! Throttle up to full!
[male]
Breaking every tether of the gravity pull!

[Chorus]
(Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Bridge]
(Half-time heavy arena rock groove with soaring synthesizer brass)
[male]
They thought the countdown ended years ago
Thought the cold dark winter froze the afterglow
But an engine built for orbit never forgets the stars
Reaching for the heavens where the cosmos are!

[Guitar Solo]
(A soaring, virtuosic 1980s two-hand tapping electric guitar solo over galloping bass and rapid-fire double-kick drums)

[Final Chorus]
(Gang Chorus)
Main Engine Start! Feel the boosters burn!
Past the point of hesitation, past no return!
Through the maroon clouds and the orange flame
Climbing to the heavens where we wrote our name!
Punching through the atmosphere with all our heart
Hold on to the throttle—it's Main Engine Start!

[Outro]
(Gang Vocals)
Main Engine Start!
[male]
All thrusters at one hundred and four percent!
We are in orbit!
(Final blazing guitar harmonic and gated drum crescendo)

title: Hard Reset (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Rewinding to the 1997 title track that launched their independent stadium era after buying out their masters in 1996, Ryan and Cassidy trade blistering verses over Evan and Tyler's pounding arena rhythm section.

**LYRICS:**

[Verse 1]
The G-force fades, the shaking stops
We're floating past the mountain tops
The old computer's dead and gone
We're running on the break of dawn

[Verse 2]
The screens are black, the air is still
We're drifting on a silent hill
Engage the manual override
There's nowhere left for us to hide

[Pre-Chorus]
Thrusters? Ready
Vector? Steady
We have to jump the spark
To light up the dark!

[Chorus]
Hard Reset!
Flip the switch and clear the cache
We’re rising from the static crash
Hard Reset!
The code is new, the core is bright
We’re burning through the edge of night
No ground control!
No gravity!
Just the Engine and the Galaxy!
Hard Reset!

[Verse 3]
They said we'd burn, they said we'd break
That freedom was a huge mistake
But look at how the gauges glow
We're generating our own flow

[Pre-Chorus]
Thrusters? Ready
Vector? Steady
We have to jump the spark
To light up the dark!

[Chorus]
Hard Reset!
Flip the switch and clear the cache
We’re rising from the static crash
Hard Reset!
The code is new, the core is bright
We’re burning through the edge of night
No ground control!
No gravity!

Hard Reset!

Stabilizing...
Synchronizing...
The hull is holding
The view is unfolding
SYSTEM... ONLINE!

title: Not Your Doll (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
A massive, full-throttle stadium production number where Cassidy O'Connell hands her wraparound synthesizer rig over to touring keyboardist Claire Lindqvist, throws on a black leather jacket, and takes the stage **FRONT AND CENTER** at the lip of the thrust stage. Channeling ferocious 1980s hard-rock frontwoman grit, she tears apart Apex Records' 1980s attempt to package her as their fragile, obedient "Stardust" pop mascot while the 120-foot curved LED wall shatters a neon-pink porcelain doll mask into roaring crimson flames and twin fountains of gold pyrotechnics erupt across The Crucible.

**LYRICS:**

[Live Stadium Crowd Roar]
[Heavy Palm-Muted Electric Guitar Drone & Pounding Dual Stadium Drums]

[Spoken Word Intro]
[female]
Back in nineteen eighty-seven, a record executive in a three-thousand-dollar suit looked at my brother and me and decided that a girl from Blacksburg wasn't allowed to play heavy rock and roll! They pointed at Ryan and called him the Engine... and they pointed at me, handed me a pink plastic script, and told me to smile, stay quiet behind the keyboards, and be their little Stardust! Well, tonight I'm standing front and center in our house—and nobody puts a cage around this voice ever again!

[Intro]
(Explosive twin-lead 1980s hard rock electric guitars, thundering dual drum kits, and punchy stadium brass stabs)

[Verse 1]
[female]
(Raw, gritty, ferocious female rock vocals)

title: Escape Velocity (Ad Astra) (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**THE LIVE ALBUM PREMIERE — THE ONLY RECORDED LIVE CONCERT PERFORMANCE OF *"ESCAPE VELOCITY (AD ASTRA)"* IN THE BAND'S ENTIRE CATALOG.** Originally written and recorded by **Cassidy O'Connell** in 1995 during the financial struggle of the band's Wilderness Years (*The Warehouse Tapes*) and later featured as the closing magnum opus of 1997's *Hard Reset* (Disc 2: *The Twin Moons*), this monumental four-movement progressive symphonic rock suite (*Part I: The Cage*, *Part II: Ignition [Ad Astra]*, *Part III: The Cosmos*, and *Part IV: Re-entry [The New World]*) is Cassidy's autobiography and what she considers her single most important piece of work. Because it had not been written yet during 1990's *Live in Chicago* and was omitted from the tighter two-hour waterfront amphitheater setlist of 2005's *Live in Norfolk*, **2016's *Live at the Crucible* is the ONLY live album where you can experience *"Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"* performed live**.

To open **Act III: *Cosmic Tidal Lock*** in astrophysical launch order (achieving the `11.2 km/s` escape velocity required to break free of Earth's gravity before coasting to *Apoapsis* and locking into *Moon 1: Tidal Lock*), all four towering stadium floodlight banks inside The Crucible shut off completely, plunging 65,000 fans into the pitch-black Appalachian starfield while overhead planetarium lasers and the 120-foot curved LED screen transform the bowl into deep space. Across **13 minutes and 3 seconds** of uninterrupted live musicianship with **The Orbital Crew**, Cassidy journeys from the suffocating trauma of the 1992 *Friction* trial (*"The Shark was right, the nuke went off! / We won the battle, but at what cost?!"*), through the roaring rocket liftoff of *Ignition* (`0:00–6:30`) and the stadium-shaking **Main Engine Cutoff** applause at `6:30`, into the weightless zero-gravity sanctuary of *The Cosmos* (`6:30–10:45`, where she sings the line that defines the band's 1986 origin: *"This is the Stardust that is me! / The cosmos and the rocket's fire! / My one, my only true desire!"*), and finally into the triumphant stadium splashdown of *Part IV: Re-entry* (`10:45–13:03`), where all 65,000 Forgers roar ***"HELD BY THE SUN!"*** in unison before Cassidy whispers a breathless, deeply moved ***"Thank you so much..."*** into the microphone—bringing her 26-year journey from 1990's *"If You Walked Away"* full circle under the Blacksburg stars.

**LYRICS:**

[Live Stadium Crowd Hush]
[Ambient Synth Drone & Haunting Woodwind Intro]
[Operatic Female Vocalise]
Ahhhh-ahhh-ahhhhhh...
Oooooh-ahhhhh-ahhhhhh...

[16th-Note Synth Arpeggiator, Double-Kick Drums & Shred Guitar Duel]

[Part I: The Cage]
[Shimmering Piano & Dark Synth Pad]
The walls are cold, the air is thin
The noise outside is closing in
A single light, a buzzing sound
Another day in the underground...

[Twin-Lead Synth & Guitar Interlude]

[Galloping Prog-Rock Rhythm, Heavy Guitar]
I'm running from the face I see!
The victim-saint they made of me!
The wholesome girl, so sad and worn!
A David for their Goliath's scorn!

This rage is just a heavy stone!
A gravity I've outgrown!
Shedding skin, shedding weight!
Escaping from this world of hate!

They loved the trial, the family torn!
They loved the story, a new star born!
But not from music, not from grace!
From the hot-chocolate-drinking angel face!

The Shark was right, the nuke went off!
We won the battle, but at what cost?!
We're radioactive, we're litigious!
We're just the joke, the victim-saints!

[Half-Time Symphonic Chorus]
I'm trapped inside this Wilderness!
This Fortress built on bitterness!

[Dark Pulsing Sequencer]
This isn't freedom...
This is a cell...
This righteous hell...
This righteous hell...

[Part II: Ignition (Ad Astra)]
[High-Speed Prog-Rock Launch & Melodic Guitar Solo]

[Verse 1]
I see a signal in the endless black
A single light, no turning back
The pull of the old world fades away
A new horizon, a new day!

[Full Band Roars In]
The countdown's running in my head!
Ignoring all the things they said!
The Engine roars, a crimson light!
A pillar of fire in the night!

The pressure builds, I'm pinned to the seat!
My heart is pounding with the beat!
The G-force pulling a heavy stone!
The last chain breaks, I'm not alone!

[Chorus]
I'm climbing! Climbing!
Past the point of no return!
I'm flying! Flying!
With the fire I let burn!
Just a signal, a distant light!
Burning through the endless night!
Ad astra! (To the stars!)
Ad astra!

[Extended Guitar & Synth Arpeggio Duel]

[Verse 2]
The sky is tearing at the seams!
Awake now from their broken dreams!
The Stardust is just a trail of dust!
The Stardust is the thing I trust!

The clouds are falling far below!
A place of pain I used to know!
The blue gives way to endless black!
There is no thought of turning back!

[Chorus]
I'm climbing! Climbing!
Past the point of no return!
I'm flying! Flying!
With the fire I let burn!
Just a signal, a distant light!
Burning through the endless night!
Ad astra! (To the stars!)
Ad astra!

[High-Velocity Synth & Guitar Booster Climax]
[Abrupt Main Engine Cutoff into Roaring Stadium Applause]

[Part III: The Cosmos]
[Zero-G Liquid Synth Pads Swelling Out of the Darkness, Slow Tempo]
I'm floating now, the engine's off
The silence is a holy sound
The rage is gone, the fear is lost
In this new universe I've found

The Cage is just a distant star
A tiny light I left behind
I finally know just who you are
The other half of my own mind

[Celestial Chorus, Layered Vocals & Sweeping Strings]
I'm loved by the sun!
I'm held by the void!
An orbit just begun!
A life not destroyed!

I'm loved by the moon!
I'm cradled by the black!
My heart is back in tune!
There is no turning back!

And the stars are singing!
A song I understand!
I'm finally, finally
Reaching for your hand!

[Emotional Weeping Guitar Solo & Cosmic Synth Arpeggios]

[Bridge: Shimmering Synth Pad]
I see the colors of the nebula
A place I've only seen in dreams
The reds, the blues, the purples call
Flowing in majestic streams...

[Full Band Swells Triumphantly]
This is the place I was meant to be!
This is the Stardust that is me!
The cosmos and the rocket's fire!
My one, my only true desire!
Loved by the sun!

[Soaring Melodic Guitar Lead Into Driving Re-entry Groove]

[Part IV: Re-entry (The New World)]
[Warm Driving Stadium Rock, Bright Acoustic & Electric Guitars, Pounding Drums]
The walls are gone, the air is clear!
There is no noise, there is no fear!
The Stardust is a forgotten ghost!
The Engine has delivered me to the coast!

Of a new world, a new shore!
A place I've never been before!
The Cage is broken, the victim-saint is gone!
A new clean script is in my head!
The friction burned away in the fire!
Leaving only my true desire!

[Grand Finale: Maximum Stadium Volume, Full Band, Strings & Synths]
(65,000 Fans in Unison: HELD BY THE SUN!)
I'm held by the void!
My orbit has begun!
A life is not destroyed!

[Epic Sustained Guitar & Synth Finale Over Thundering Drums]
Ad astra!
Ad astra!
Ad astra!

[Final Crashing Stadium Chord & Roaring Ovation]
(Spoken softly into the microphone over the cheering crowd)
Thank you so much...

title: Apoapsis (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Having achieved escape velocity (`11.2 km/s`) to break free of Earth's gravity on the preceding 13-minute centerpiece, the vessel coasts upward to the highest point of its elliptical orbit on **"Apoapsis"**—the opening movement of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. As the stadium bowl remains bathed in deep-space planetarium projections, Cassidy's shimmering analog synthesizers, Evan's floating fretless bassline, and Ryan's volume-pedal guitar swells recreate the weightless silence of deep space inside The Crucible.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental]
*(The track opens with a sprawling, ethereal ambient intro across the darkened stadium. Shimmering, pristine analog synthesizers wash over the 65,000-seat bowl.)*

*(Evan introduces a slow, highly melodic bassline that anchors the floating atmosphere, joined by spacious, echoing percussion from Tyler Wright and Darius "Doc" Holloway.)*

*(Ryan utilizes a volume pedal on his electric guitar, creating swelling, atmospheric waves of sound that mimic the slow, majestic rotation of a planet viewed from high orbit.)*

title: Second Apoapsis (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The second movement of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. Drawing structural inspiration from the sprawling, multi-part instrumental epics on **Origin**'s self-titled 1983 album, **"Second Apoapsis"** flows gaplessly out of *"Apoapsis"*, introducing cinematic tension and intricate interlocking synthesizer arpeggios between Cassidy O'Connell and touring keyboardist Claire Lindqvist before dissolving directly into the vocal finale of the suite, *"The Spectrum (True Color)"*.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental]
*(Bleeding directly out of "Apoapsis", the spacious stadium percussion slowly begins to drive a more cinematic, deliberate rhythm.)*

*(Cassidy's synthesizers grow brighter and more complex, weaving intricate arpeggios around Evan's melodic bassline.)*

*(Ryan's volume-pedal guitar swells transform into a massive, echoing, cinematic build across the stadium PA, reaching a towering crescendo before suddenly dropping away into a quiet, ethereal outro that sets the stage for the vocals of "The Spectrum [True Color]".)*

title: The Spectrum (True Color) (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The sweeping vocal finale of **The Apoapsis Suite** from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset*. This progressive space-rock epic reimagines the band's 1987 debut single, *"Electric Color"*, from a sanitized corporate pop track into a sprawling observation of the cosmos (*"We left the atmosphere, the world was gray / The heavy gravity has finally faded away... And we are seeing the true spectrum! / A billion stars burning ultraviolet and blue"*). Performed here in **Act III: *Cosmic Tidal Lock***, it also serves as a brilliant mid-concert foreshadowing of the secret **Act VII True Ending**, when the band and all 300 **CPI Marching Forgers** will reclaim the original 1987 *"Electric Color"* as a blistering 1980s AOR Stadium Rock anthem to close the night.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro: The Gray]
*(The track opens seamlessly out of the fading echoes of "Second Apoapsis". A slow, pulsing bassline anchors a massive, shimmering synth pad across the darkened stadium before Cassidy's ethereal vocals drift in.)*

[Verse 1]
We left the atmosphere, the world was gray
The heavy gravity has finally faded away
We were living in a room with the curtains drawn tight
But out here in the void, there is only the light

[Pre-Chorus]
The terrestrial sounds are just a buzz in the ear
A static station that we no longer hear
The silence is turning into a song
This is the orbit where we belong

[Chorus]
And we are seeing the true spectrum!
A billion stars burning ultraviolet and blue
Dancing in the dust of a cosmic summer
The nebula is splitting the dark in two
This is the electric color!
The universe waking up for you...

[Instrumental Spacewalk]
*(A sweeping instrumental section. Evan's bassline locks into a slow, hypnotic groove while Cassidy layers intricate, sparkling synthesizer arpeggios that mimic stars passing by the observation deck window.)*

[Verse 2]
They wanted a painted sky, a plastic sun
A little radio hit when the day was done
But you cannot capture the burning of a star
When you keep the engine locked inside a jar
We're charting the coordinates they couldn't see
Out here in the quiet of the zero-G

[Pre-Chorus]
The terrestrial sounds are just a buzz in the ear
A static station that we no longer hear
The silence is turning into a song
This is the orbit where we belong

[Chorus]
And we are seeing the true spectrum!
A billion stars burning ultraviolet and blue
Dancing in the dust of a cosmic summer
The nebula is splitting the dark in two
This is the electric color!
The universe waking up for you...

[The Solo]
*(Ryan delivers a massive, soaring, and highly emotional electric guitar solo—vast and echoing, filling the open-air bowl of The Crucible under the Blacksburg stars.)*

[Outro]
The true spectrum.
Ultraviolet and blue.
We finally found the color.
*(The song slowly dissolves into an atmospheric synth fade-out, trailing off like stardust into "Moon 1: Tidal Lock".)*

title: Moon 1: Tidal Lock (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The stadium floodlights dim to a deep cosmic indigo as Cassidy bathes all 65,000 fans in the zero-gravity analog pads of **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** (from 1997's *Hard Reset* and 2003's *Sanctuary [Zero-G]*), turning the entire bowl of The Crucible into a glowing planetarium under the Blacksburg stars.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A tight, driving 1980s drum beat enters. A pulsing synth bassline locks into the rhythm, perfectly anchoring the track as shimmering analog synth pads slowly rise in the background.)*

They tried to spin us out of control
But we found the center, we found the soul

[Pre-Chorus]

Half in the shadow, half in the light
I'm caught in the orbit, spinning around
A million miles above the ground

[Chorus]

Suspended in the velvet and the blue
No matter how I turn, no matter where I fly
You are the only anchor in my sky
Yeah, I'm in a tidal lock with you!

[Verse 2]
The radio is quiet, the signal is dead
But I hear the rhythm inside my head
We don't need the sun to show us the way
We left the noise of the terrestrial day
We're charting the math that they couldn't see
Perfect alignment in the zero-G

title: Moon 2: Roche Limit (Live at the Crucible)
content:

Exploding directly out of the fading starfield of Cassidy's *"Moon 1: Tidal Lock"* to kick off **Act IV: *Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2 — Ryan's Heavy-Friction Orbit)***, **"Moon 2: Roche Limit"** (from Disc 2 of 1997's *Hard Reset* and Track 1 of Ryan's 2003 solo-led concept album *Mile Marker 98*) shatters the zero-gravity calm of the stadium with crimson strobe lights, pounding double-kit drums, and Ryan O'Connell's blistering, distorted electric guitar. Where Cassidy's *Moon 1* used the astrophysics of a tidal lock to celebrate stable, unbreakable loyalty, Ryan uses the **Roche limit**—the exact gravitational distance at which a satellite is torn to pieces by tidal forces—as a visceral, high-friction thesis statement confronting the trauma of the December 10, 1990 crash.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(An aggressive, pounding 1980s drum fill shatters the ambient space. Ryan's heavy, distorted electric guitar riff locks in with Evan's driving synth-bass.)*

You're a massive body, I'm a satellite

We crossed the Roche Limit!

A fatal attraction, a heavy heart!
There's no surviving when you get this close
A total system failure, a lethal dose

System failure.

title: Impact (Mile Marker 98) (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The visceral title cut of Ryan's 2003 concept album *Mile Marker 98* (*Moon 2*). Translating the night of December 10, 1990 into a cosmic collision in a treacherous debris field, **"Impact (Mile Marker 98)"** recounts how Ryan was cautiously piloting the band's 1988 Holt Freighter van at 40 MPH with hazard beacons active when a speeding vehicle clipped their rear quarter panel near Mile Marker 98, rolling the van twice and leaving Ryan pinned in the wreckage with a complete T10 spinal cord injury (*"We hit a massive fragment in the great unknown / At Mile Marker 98, I lost the throne! / We're barely alive, but we survived the night!"*).

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A driving, heavy 1980s electric guitar riff cuts through the stadium darkness, backed by a pounding, relentless hard-rock drumbeat.)*

[Verse 1]
I was holding the controls, trying to beat the storm
Trying to keep the Freighter steady, trying to keep it warm
Running forty through the dark, the hazard beacons bright
We were making steady time across the frozen night
But a shadow came flying through the passing lane
Too fast for the ice, too fast for the rain!

[Pre-Chorus]
A sudden violent strike on the quarter panel!
Ripped us right out of the safety channel!
Caught inside the debris field, spinning out of control
The massive broken planet taking its toll!

[Chorus]

Impact! Shattering the design!
Rolled twice in the black, thrown into the cold
The heaviest gravity the metal can hold
We hit a massive fragment in the great unknown
At Mile Marker 98, I lost the throne!
We're barely alive, but we survived the night!
Yeah, we're barely alive!

[Verse 2]
I wake up pinned underneath the twisted steel
I'm screaming to the console but I cannot feel
The alarms are blaring, everything is red
But I can hear the crew breathing in the bed
The T-10 circuit is completely blown
I'm looking at a body that is not my own!

The engine is running, but the connection is dead.
Nothing below the damage, just the static in my head.
They pulled me from the wreckage, pulled me from the fire.
But I left half of myself in the twisting wire.

Impact! Spinning off the line!

Mile Marker 98.

title: Mayday: The Intercept (Live at the Crucible)
content:

Transitioning directly from *Moon 1* into the heavy, high-friction arena rock of 2003's *Moon 2: Mile Marker 98*, Ryan and Cassidy sing the story of how their family intercepted the darkness after the 1990 Des Moines bus crash and brought everyone home alive.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A heavy, distorted electric guitar mimics the fast, staccato radar pings from "Telemetry". Suddenly, a massive, booming 1980s hard rock drum fill kicks in, followed by a driving, urgent bassline. The energy is desperate and fast.)*

[Verse 1]
*(Aggressive, emotional male rock vocals)*
I was suffocating slowly in the broken shell
Drowning in the static of a burning hell
But the console flickered with a sudden bright green
The cleanest set of numbers that I've ever seen!
I recognize the radar, I recognize the code
A transmission coming down the cosmic road!

[Pre-Chorus]
I'm punching in the frequency, I'm opening the mic

I'm bleeding out the oxygen, the temperature is low

title: Star City: Orbital Ward (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Following the rescue of *"Mayday: The Intercept"*, **"Star City: Orbital Ward"** (from 2003's *Mile Marker 98*) slows the tempo into a brooding, heavy 1980s hard-rock power ballad that transposes Ryan's 1990 recovery at Star City General Hospital into an orbital medical bay. Translating the strict daily survival routines of **"Protocol T-10"**—the four-hour hydration and catheterization clock, the 15-minute wheelchair pressure weight shifts, and Evan and Tyler's synchronized "Freight Dog" twin-lifts—into the manual maintenance of a damaged but surviving starship, this performance directly sets the stage for the next Act (*Our Own Frequency*), where Ryan will strip away the sci-fi metaphors on *"Brother's Keeper"* and talk openly about how those daily ADLs led to tonight's decision to end global touring and stay home in Blacksburg.

**LYRICS:**

[Spoken Intro]
*(Spoken clearly, calmly, and methodically by the Planetarium Narrator over a slow, echoing heartbeat monitor and Ryan's brooding clean electric guitar.)*
Welcome back to the Engine Room Records Planetarium.
Following the fragmentation event, the central engine has been salvaged and transported to the Star City Orbital Ward.
Diagnostics indicate a complete and permanent severing of the T-10 power conduit.
Automated systems below the damage threshold have officially failed.
Strict manual maintenance protocols must now be initiated to ensure system survival.

[Intro]
*(The narrator cuts out. The clean guitar is joined by a heavy, slow, stomping 1980s drum beat and a deep, pulsing bassline.)*

Lock the Iron Dome, keep the perimeter tight
I'm learning how to fly it in the middle of the night!

I've got a crew to lift me, I've got a spotter on the time
A heavy metal mountain that I still have to climb!
In the Orbital Ward!

Every fifteen minutes I've got to shift the weight
Trying to keep the pressure off, trying to stay straight
The freight dogs pull me up the maintenance hatch
A synchronized lift, a heavy metal catch
My hands are on the console, I've got the upper gear
We're rewriting the protocols right out here!

[Pre-Chorus]
The T-10 conduit is severed in the dark
I lost the lower thrusters, but I still have the spark
Lock the Iron Dome, keep the perimeter tight
I'm learning how to fly it in the middle of the night!

[Chorus]
Star City Orbital Ward!
Strapped to the table, strapped to the board!
I hate the heavy chair, I hate the diagnostic room
But I'm pushing through the fire and I'm pushing through the gloom
I've got a crew to lift me, I've got a spotter on the time
A heavy metal mountain that I still have to climb!
In the Orbital Ward!

The connection is broken.
But the hands still work.
The legs are silent.
But the engine still roars!

[Chorus]
Star City Orbital Ward!
Strapped to the table, strapped to the board!
I hate the heavy chair, I hate the diagnostic room

I've got a crew to lift me, I've got a spotter on the time

In the Orbital Ward!

Shift the weight.
Watch the clock.
Star City dock.

title: Twin Moons: Touchdown (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Closing **Act IV: *Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 (Moon 2)*** and uniting both halves of the 10-song *Twin Moons* cosmic journey (*Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock* + *Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98*), **"Twin Moons: Touchdown"** is the triumphant sibling duet that concludes 2003's *Mile Marker 98*. Fusing Ryan's heavy, distorted 1980s arena-rock guitar with Cassidy's sweeping analog synthesizers in locked unison (*"The Engine and the Anchor locking into the groove / We finally found the gravity, we're ready to move! / Touchdown!"*), the song brings the vessel out of the freezing vacuum of space and sets it safely down on solid ground in Blacksburg—concluding with the Planetarium Narrator's sign-off (*"Atmospheric entry complete. Gravity is stable... Please exit safely, and welcome home"*) right as Evan and Tyler leave the stage for the intimate living-room acoustic block of **Act V: *Our Own Frequency***.

**LYRICS:**

[Intro]
*(A massive, thundering 1980s hard-rock drum fill explodes out of the gate. Instantly, Ryan's heavy, distorted electric guitar locks into a triumphant riff, mirrored note-for-note by Cassidy's sweeping analog synthesizer.)*

[Verse 1: Ryan]
The heat shield cracked but the metal held the line
I'm breaking through the clouds, I'm reading every sign
The atmospheric fire is fading in the rear
I'm dropping down the landing gear!
I spent a stalemate year floating in the dark
But I brought the heavy engine back to light the spark!

[Verse 2: Cassidy]
I tracked the telemetry across the velvet black
I held the heavy tether just to pull you back
The gravity is equal, the orbital is done
We're landing in the light of the setting sun
The silent ocean fades, the violent friction ends
We're touching down exactly where the atmosphere bends!

[Pre-Chorus: Ryan & Cassidy]
The altitude is dropping, the horizon is wide
We're crossing the terminator side by side!

The center of the universe is coming into view!

[Chorus: Ryan & Cassidy]
Twin Moons! Touching down on the solid ground!

The Engine and the Anchor locking into the groove

Touchdown!
