*(Ryan and Cassidy trade solos across the stage—Ryan unleashing a blistering, bluesy hard-rock guitar lead and Cassidy answering immediately with a soaring, ethereal synthesizer run before intertwining in twin harmony.)*

[Bridge]
(Ryan) I thought I lost the wheels in the middle of the crash.
(Cassidy) But we built a sanctuary right out of the ash!
(Both) No more floating in the freezing unknown!
The orbit is over, we are finally home!

[Chorus: Ryan & Cassidy]
Twin Moons! Touching down on the solid ground!
Twin Moons! Listen to the heavy sound!
The metal and the stardust shining in the light
We're walking from the shadow and surviving the night!
The Engine and the Anchor locking into the groove
We finally found the gravity, we're ready to move!
Touchdown!

[Outro]
*(The heavy music crescendos into a massive, sustained final chord. The guitars and drums slowly fade away, leaving only a warm, pulsing synthesizer drone.)*

[Spoken Word Outro: Planetarium Narrator]
Atmospheric entry complete. Gravity is stable.
On behalf of the crew, we would like to thank you for visiting the Engine Room Records Planetarium.
The simulation is now concluded.
Please exit safely, and welcome home.

title: Our Own Frequency (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**Act IV: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 1 of 3).** Recorded in complete secrecy in the living room of the Blacksburg house during the middle of the band's decade-long Burnout Hiatus, 2008's *Our Own Frequency* was never toured, promoted, or accompanied by press interviews—Ryan and Cassidy simply uploaded it to the Engine Room Records website on a Tuesday morning with a one-sentence note: *"We're still here, and we're okay."* At the midpoint of *Live at the Crucible*, Evan and Tyler leave the stage completely, and the towering stadium light rigs dim to two solitary warm spotlights at center stage: Ryan in his wheelchair with an acoustic guitar, Cassidy at the piano, and two microphones. For the first time in front of a live audience, brother and sister strip away the stadium walls of sound to share their most private living-room conversation with their CPI family.

**LYRICS:**

[Audience Applause Softens to a Respectful Hush]
[Single Warm Spotlight on Acoustic Guitar and Piano]

[Spoken Word Intro]
[female]
Evan and Tyler are gonna take five backstage for a little bit. Back in two thousand and eight, right in the middle of our ten-year hiatus, Ryan and I couldn't face the cameras or the stadiums anymore. So we locked the front door of our house right down the road on Progress Street, sat down in the living room with just an acoustic guitar, a piano, and two microphones, and recorded an album we never toured.
[male]
We just uploaded it on a Tuesday morning with one sentence: "We're still here, and we're okay." We never thought we'd play these three songs in a stadium... but tonight, sixty-five thousand of you feel just like our living room.

[Intro]
(A warm, intimate acoustic guitar and piano duet intro in a hushed stadium)

[Verse 1]
[female]
They want to paint us in neon light
They want to tell us how to burn tonight
But you and me, we know the truth
They can't buy what we built in our youth

[Verse 2]
[male]
Turn off the synths, unplug the drum
Look at the monsters that we have become
Let's strip it down to the wood and wire
And build ourselves a signal fire

[Chorus]
(Intimate brother and sister vocal harmony over acoustic guitar and piano)
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Verse 3]
[female]
They tried to sell a manufactured dream
A perfect picture on a glowing screen
[male]
But all I need is sitting right here
The melody is finally clear

[Chorus]
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Bridge]
(A tender, deeply emotional piano and acoustic guitar instrumental duet)
[female]
No heavy gloss...
[male]
No studio boss...
[female]
Just the music we wanted to make!

[Chorus]
Just the piano and the six-string strum
Before the noise and the kingdom come
No one to tell us how the story ends
Just a brother and a sister and the time we spend
On our own frequency
Just you and me

[Outro]
[male]
Our own frequency...
[female]
Just you and me...
(Fades out with a lingering piano chord, a soft acoustic strum, and gentle applause across The Crucible)

title: Brother's Keeper (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**Act IV Centerpiece: *"Brother's Keeper"* — The Intimate Reality of Ryan's ADLs & The End of Touring / Forger Nation Summer Festival Announcement (Part 2 of 3).** The emotional centerpiece of 2008's *Our Own Frequency* and the most private, vulnerable song Ryan and Cassidy have ever written. *"Brother's Keeper"* is an unflinchingly intimate look at the life-or-death mutual protection between brother and sister and what Cassidy and the family go through every single day taking care of Ryan's **ADLs (Activities of Daily Living)** due to his T10 paralysis from the 1990 crash—performing his daily toileting requirements and morning anti-atrophy leg stretches, pushing his wheelchair when the road is steep, and sharing a bed pushed against the wall at night with Ryan on the inside and Cassidy sleeping on the outside edge to act as a **human bed-rail** so he doesn't roll off, while Ryan serves as Cassidy's emotional anchor against the overwhelming sensory and psychological toll of the world. Before playing the song in the pin-drop silence of The Crucible, Ryan explains that twenty-six years after the 1990 crash, the daily physical toll of those ADLs on the road has gotten too hard on his body and family—revealing that tonight's *Reignition* Tour finale at The Crucible is the **last concert a touring The Stardust Engine will ever play**. When the stadium gasps, Cassidy immediately reassures the crowd that they aren't retiring: to give the Town of Blacksburg and CPI time to plan, starting in **August 2017** (the first weekend of August), The Stardust Engine will stay home in Blacksburg to headline the annual **Forger Nation Summer Festival**—combining a campus-wide CPI Open House, a massive downtown Blacksburg block party for signed and unsigned bands, and The Stardust Engine's permanent annual residency concert + fireworks inside The Crucible.

**LYRICS:**

[Pin-Drop Stadium Silence]
[Soft Fingerpicked Acoustic Guitar Note]

[Spoken Word Intro]
[male]
This next song is the centerpiece of Our Own Frequency, and it's the most private song Cassidy and I have ever written. People look up at a stage and see two hours of lights and guitars. They don't see what T-ten paralysis actually takes behind closed doors. They don't see Cassidy and Evan and Tyler helping me through my daily care and toileting routines, or stretching my legs every morning so they don't atrophy. They don't see how we push the bed against the wall at night so I can sleep on the inside, and my sister sleeps on the outside edge as a human bed rail so I don't roll off in the dark.
[female]
And they don't see how you keep me anchored when the world gets too loud for my head to handle. We take care of each other. That's what family does.
[male]
Doing all of those daily routines on tour buses and in hotel rooms across the world was one thing when I was twenty-two in nineteen-ninety. Twenty-six years later... I'm gonna be honest with you, Forger Nation. Accommodating this chair on the road has gotten too hard on my body, and on my family. Tonight is the final stop of the Reignition tour, and tonight is the last concert a touring Stardust Engine will ever play.
[Audience Gasps Softly, Then Applauds Warmly in Support]
[female]
Wait—don't be sad! We aren't retiring! If touring the world is too hard on Ryan, then the world can come to Blacksburg! To give the Town of Blacksburg and CPI time to build this right, starting in August twenty-seventeen, we're launching the annual Forger Nation Summer Festival! A massive CPI Open House for incoming and prospective freshmen, the biggest downtown Blacksburg block party of the summer with stages for signed and unsigned bands, and every single year we'll close the festival right here inside The Crucible with fireworks—and sleep in our own beds on Progress Street every night!
[Deafening Cheers and Applause Before Hushing Back to Silence]
[male]
This is "Brother's Keeper."

[Intro]
(A delicate, melancholy grand piano intro)
(Acoustic guitar joins with a steady, comforting fingerpicked rhythm)

[Verse 1]
[male]
They look at the chair and they think it's weak
They whisper their pity whenever we speak
But they don't see the mornings, the stretches and pain
The quiet routines keeping us sane
[female]
Sleeping on the edge, a human bed rail
Catching the other whenever we fail

[Verse 2]
[female]
Moving the pieces the body forgot
Holding the line whenever we're caught
Being the strength when the daily tasks break
Giving up comfort for the other one's sake
[male]
A brother and a sister, fighting to survive
The only reason we're staying alive

[Pre-Chorus]
[female]
Are we each other's keeper? We'll take the blame
[male]
Standing in the fire, walking through the flame
[female]
Answering the call when it gets too deep
[male]
Guarding all the secrets we're trying to keep

[Chorus]
(Raw, emotional brother and sister vocal harmony over acoustic guitar and piano)
We trade all the armor, we trade all the scars
We built our own world underneath all the stars
When the body won't work, we become our own feet
When the pressure is heavy, we make it retreat
They don't understand the blood in our veins
We're holding the keys and we're breaking the chains

[Interlude]
(Intimate, emotional piano and acoustic guitar interlude in the quiet stadium night)

[Verse 3]
[female]
Pushing the wheels wherever we go
[male]
Being the shelter when bitter winds blow

[Chorus]
We trade all the armor, we trade all the scars
We built our own world underneath all the stars
When the body won't work, we become our own feet
When the pressure is heavy, we make it retreat
They don't understand the blood in our veins
We're holding the keys and we're breaking the chains

[Outro]
(Harmonizing gently into the two microphones)
[female]
We keep each other safe.
[male]
We keep each other grounded.
(Fade out on a single, resonating piano chord as 65,000 fans rise in a deeply moved standing ovation)

title: Safe Person (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
**Act IV: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 3 of 3).** Completing the three-song *Our Own Frequency* (2008) living-room trilogy, **"Safe Person"** answers the physical devotion of *"Brother's Keeper"* by revealing the other half of their unbreakable bond: how Ryan acts as Cassidy's safe person and emotional anchor when the flashing cameras, press questions, and autistic sensory overload threaten to overwhelm her. Performed strictly by Ryan on acoustic guitar and Cassidy at the piano with zero electric amps or stadium lights, sixty-five thousand Forgers hold up quiet white phone lights across the dark bowl of The Crucible.

**LYRICS:**

[Quiet Stadium Ambience]
[Gentle, Solitary Piano Intro]
(Acoustic guitar softly joins the piano)

[Verse 1]
[female]
The cameras flash, the questions start to blur
I smile and nod, playing the character
But underneath the makeup and the lights
I'm terrifyingly alone on these high wire nights
Until I catch your eye across the room
And suddenly I'm safe inside this tomb

[Verse 2]
[male]
You never have to wear the mask for me
I know exactly who you want to be
When the oxygen gets thin up on the stage
I'll be the one to open up the cage
Just breathe and let the heavy armor fall
I've got you when your back is to the wall

[Chorus]
(Heartfelt brother and sister duet over pure acoustic guitar and piano)
You're my safe person, the calm inside the storm
The only place I know where I am warm
We tear down all the idols and the lies
And find the truth inside each other's eyes
No electric amps, no flashing lights
Just you and me surviving all the nights

title: Electric Color (Live at the Crucible)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The secret 5-minute-26-second Grand Finale Encore of the May 21, 2016 homecoming concert inside **The Crucible**—and the very first time in the band's 30-year history that **"Electric Color"** was ever performed as the blistering **1980s Album-Oriented Rock (Stadium Rock)** anthem Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler originally heard in their heads before Apex Records forced them to release it as a glossy 1987 Dance Synth-Pop single.

Protected prior to concert night by Holly O'Connell's **$300,000 collective student escrow ("The Forger Pot")** under Addendum No. 4 to her 1986 Cross-License—and disguised in the **CPI Marching Forgers**' rehearsal folders as *"Exercise 87-B: The Anvil Finale"* with the vocal melody stripped out—the band first staged **"Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street"** as a false ending, plunging the stadium into darkness so the audience believed the concert was over. Then, in the pitch black, all 300 members of the Marching Forgers marched back onto the stage to join the band (just as they had in the four-song opening act) for the actual ending. For the first **1 minute and 40 seconds**—through Cassidy's spoken greeting over a lone piano chord (*"Blacksburg! We've been all over the world..."*), the Kevlar snare roll-off, and a massive 77-second AOR stadium guitar and 300-horn brass overture (`0:23–1:40`)—not a single fan in the 65,000-seat stadium knew what song the band was playing, until **`1:40`** on the dot when the instruments dropped to a lone heavy kick drum and Cassidy sang the opening words of Verse 1: *"Woke up this morning, the world was gray..."*

title: Ignition: The Forger's Call
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The official **October 1986 Crucible Stadium Master** played over the PA system at **The Crucible** during every CPI Forgers home football game as the football team runs out of the tunnel onto the field—released on an album for the very first time on October 15, 2016 alongside *Live at the Crucible* (both inside the *Live at the Crucible* 30th-Anniversary Box Set at The Foundry and as a standalone companion release). After `Demo Take 3` (Track 2) won the October 1986 CPI Student Government Association anthem contest—and after 16-year-old dual-enrolled **Holly O'Connell** executed the **`$1.00` Perpetual Mutual Cross-License** ("The Progress Street Redline") with CPI's Office of University Counsel—Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler tracked this finished **`82 BPM`** stadium master specifically for the press-box audio booth at The Crucible. Replacing the cassette demo's vocalized `(TING... BOOM!)` placeholders with an actual steel foundry anvil strike and Tyler Wright's chest-rattling kick-drum impact, this is the exact recording to which the student section in **The Anvil** organically crafted **The Stomp** on the heavy kick-drum hits over several successive plays.

title: Ignition: The Forger's Call (Demo Take 3)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The legendary **October 1986 4-track Tascam Portastudio cassette demo (`Demo Take 3`)** recorded inside the unheated garage at `412 Progress Street NE` in Blacksburg, Virginia—submitted by five college kids (Ryan O'Connell, Cassidy O'Connell, Evan Wright, Tyler Wright, and 16-year-old dual-enrolled Holly O'Connell) to the CPI Student Government Association contest to replace the football team's entrance march. Before submitting the Maxell XLII-S 90 cassette tape, 16-year-old Holly redlined the university's standard *"Work Made for Hire"* entry form at the Progress Street kitchen table and negotiated the historic **`$1.00` Perpetual Mutual Cross-License** ("The Progress Street Redline"), retaining 100% of the band's master and publishing ownership while granting CPI Athletics and the Marching Forgers a perpetual, royalty-free stadium license.

Recorded before the student section in **The Anvil** ever organically invented **The Stomp** over several successive plays in the stadium—and twenty-eight years before the VDU *Anchor* rivalry inspired Ryan's 2016 live ad-lib—this raw 1986 cassette cut is the very first of the three canonical versions of *"Ignition: The Forger's Call"* (followed by the 1986 Crucible Stadium Version played at CPI football games and the 2016 *Live at the Crucible* concert opener). Because the five college kids were tracking inside an unheated garage without a real foundry anvil yet, the demo features the mechanical click of Holly's 4-track tape deck, the band members vocalizing `(TING... BOOM!)` to test the idea of where the anvil strike and heavy kick-drum impact would go, Cassidy's raw Oberheim OB-Xa analog synth brass, Ryan's overdriven garage-rock guitar riff, and Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler shouting the gang-vocal `(IGNITION!)` response into a single shared Shure SM57 microphone.

title: A Sister's Love (Main Theme)
album: The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel, Book I: The Unwinding Path (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
The soaring 1980s-inspired main theme of *The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel*, establishing the unbreakable twin bond between Kaelan (the Golden Sun) and Kaela (the Silver Sun) after Lord Malakor's forces abduct Kaela to the Shadowspire.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro: Shimmering Synth Arpeggios & Soaring Melodic Lead Guitar]

[Verse 1]
A shadow falls across the land
A kingdom dressed in grey
A tyrant's laugh, a cruel command
Has stolen you away
They took you to the highest tower
Upon a wicked throne
But they don't know the secret power
A bond of soul we've known

[Chorus]
Turn around!
Face the coming night!
A sister's love
A burning light!
Through endless dark, a guiding star
No matter where you are!
For the Gauntlet of Aethel awaits the true
A hero's heart will see you through!

[Verse 2]
The winding path is dark and long
With trials yet unknown
But in my heart, I hear our song
I'll never walk alone
For every beast and magic spell
For every trick and test
Your memory will serve me well
And put me to my best!

[Chorus]
Turn around!
Face the coming night!
A sister's love
A burning light!
Through endless dark, a guiding star
No matter where you are!
For the Gauntlet of Aethel awaits the true
A hero's heart will see you through!

[Bridge]
And when the stars begin to fade
And hope is hard to find
I'll see your face, unafraid
Forever in my mind!

[Instrumental Solo: Twin-Lead Power Metal Guitar & 80s Arpeggiated Synth Duel]

[Final Chorus]
Turn around! (Turn around!)
Face the coming night! (Coming night!)
A sister's love (A sister's love)
A burning light!
Through endless dark, a guiding star
No matter where you are!
For the Gauntlet of Aethel awaits the true
A hero's heart will see me through!

[Outro]
To you...
To you...

content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Featured in Book I, Chapter 1, Scene 12 (*"One Step at a Time"*). As Kaelan marches north from Sunstead into the Razor Peaks completely severed from Kaela's telepathic link for the first time in his life, he learns how to channel his panic into discipline and walk without a hand to hold—one step at a time.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro: High-Octane 80s Arena Rock Guitar Solo & Brass Fanfare]

[Verse 1]
The road is long, the mountain's high
A single step beneath a pale grey sky
A heavy heart, a promise I must keep, yeah
A thousand miles before I get to sleep
The shadows fall, the path unclear
The whispers of the past are always near!

[Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Verse 2]
They test my will with trick and stone
But I know I'll never walk alone
'Cause every stumble, every single test
Just puts a fire burning in my chest!
I'm learning fast, I'm getting strong
Right here in the place where I belong!

[Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Bridge]
Don't look back, don't you dare look down
Just find your feet on this uncertain ground
The night is cold, but I can feel the sun
My journey's only just begun!

[Instrumental Solo: Shredding Arena Guitar Solo & Triumphant Synth-Brass Fanfare]

[Final Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Outro: Shredding Arena Guitar Solo & Final Cymbal Crash]

title: The Tyrant's Throne (Shadow's Heart)
album: The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel, Book II: The Shadow's Heart (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Featured in Book II, Chapter 2, Part 2 (*"The Tyrant's Throne"*). Lord Malakor's theatrical progressive-metal villain anthem in the throne room of the Shadowspire, where he lays out his chilling philosophy of extinguishing the Twin Suns to impose eternal Order over Aethel.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro: Ominous Harpsichord-Synth Arpeggios & Searing Progressive Metal Guitar Solo]

[Verse 1]
My child, you stand in hallowed halls of grey
And dream of some nostalgic, sun-drenched day
You see this world, so flawed and incomplete
A chaotic dance of triumph and defeat
The golden sun, a rash and fiery breath
The silver one, a whisper soft as death
They flicker, fade, a fickle, cosmic game
But I have come to conquer and to tame!

[Chorus]
This broken world is crying for a guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!
To snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From the Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I'll give them order, I'll provide the spark
One perfect dawn, born of unending dark!

[Verse 2]
They called it heresy, my grand design
To make the suns' chaotic power mine
Those fearful fools who sat upon the throne
They cast me out to wander all alone
But in the wastes, the endless, silent night
I found a truth more pure than any light
The Gloom provides a focus, sharp and true
A gift I've brought to mortals and to you!

[Chorus]
This broken world is crying for a guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!

[Instrumental Interlude: Melodic Lead Guitar Theme]

To snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From the Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I'll give them order, I'll provide the spark
One perfect dawn, born of unending dark!

[Bridge]
Don't you see? You're not my captive, you're the final piece
Your silver soul, the key to their release
A vessel pure, a conduit of grace
To channel all their power to this place
You think your brother comes to set you free?
He only fights for what used to be
But you and I will build what is to come...

[Instrumental Solo: Delicate Piano Transition into Shredding Progressive Metal Guitar Solo]

[Final Chorus]
This broken world has found its one true guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!
I'll snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From my Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I bring them order, I am the spark
One perfect dawn...
Born of unending dark...

[Outro: Haunting Piano Arpeggios & Final Resolving Low Chord]

content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Featured in Book I, Chapter 1, Scene 12 (*"One Step at a Time"*). As Kaelan marches north from Sunstead into the Razor Peaks completely severed from Kaela's telepathic link for the first time in his life, he learns how to channel his panic into discipline and walk without a hand to hold—one step at a time.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro: High-Octane 80s Arena Rock Guitar Solo & Brass Fanfare]

[Verse 1]
The road is long, the mountain's high
A single step beneath a pale grey sky
A heavy heart, a promise I must keep, yeah
A thousand miles before I get to sleep
The shadows fall, the path unclear
The whispers of the past are always near!

[Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Verse 2]
They test my will with trick and stone
But I know I'll never walk alone
'Cause every stumble, every single test
Just puts a fire burning in my chest!
I'm learning fast, I'm getting strong
Right here in the place where I belong!

[Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Bridge]
Don't look back, don't you dare look down
Just find your feet on this uncertain ground
The night is cold, but I can feel the sun
My journey's only just begun!

[Instrumental Solo: Shredding Arena Guitar Solo & Triumphant Synth-Brass Fanfare]

[Final Chorus]
Just one step at a time!
Leave the doubt and fear behind!
With every move, a new design
I'm gonna make this moment mine
One step at a time!

[Outro: Shredding Arena Guitar Solo & Final Cymbal Crash]

title: The Tyrant's Throne (Shadow's Heart)
album: The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
content:
**LORE NOTE:**
Featured in Book II, Chapter 2, Part 2 (*"The Tyrant's Throne"*). Lord Malakor's theatrical progressive-metal villain anthem in the throne room of the Shadowspire, where he lays out his chilling philosophy of extinguishing the Twin Suns to impose eternal Order over Aethel.

**LYRICS:**

[Instrumental Intro: Ominous Harpsichord-Synth Arpeggios & Searing Progressive Metal Guitar Solo]

[Verse 1]
My child, you stand in hallowed halls of grey
And dream of some nostalgic, sun-drenched day
You see this world, so flawed and incomplete
A chaotic dance of triumph and defeat
The golden sun, a rash and fiery breath
The silver one, a whisper soft as death
They flicker, fade, a fickle, cosmic game
But I have come to conquer and to tame!

[Chorus]
This broken world is crying for a guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!
To snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From the Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I'll give them order, I'll provide the spark
One perfect dawn, born of unending dark!

[Verse 2]
They called it heresy, my grand design
To make the suns' chaotic power mine
Those fearful fools who sat upon the throne
They cast me out to wander all alone
But in the wastes, the endless, silent night
I found a truth more pure than any light
The Gloom provides a focus, sharp and true
A gift I've brought to mortals and to you!

[Chorus]
This broken world is crying for a guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!

[Instrumental Interlude: Melodic Lead Guitar Theme]

To snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From the Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I'll give them order, I'll provide the spark
One perfect dawn, born of unending dark!

[Bridge]
Don't you see? You're not my captive, you're the final piece
Your silver soul, the key to their release
A vessel pure, a conduit of grace
To channel all their power to this place
You think your brother comes to set you free?
He only fights for what used to be
But you and I will build what is to come...

[Instrumental Solo: Delicate Piano Transition into Shredding Progressive Metal Guitar Solo]

[Final Chorus]
This broken world has found its one true guide!
A single will, with nothing left to hide!
I'll snuff the stars and tear the skies apart
From my Tyrant's Throne, with a Shadow's Heart!
I bring them order, I am the spark
One perfect dawn...
Born of unending dark...

[Outro: Haunting Piano Arpeggios & Final Resolving Low Chord]
